fields.title: Procurement Officer
fields.description: Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise (EBPE) is Ethiopia’s state-owned pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise, established to build the nation’s capacity to manufacture vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, medical supplies and other healthcare technologies locally. Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services. Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services. I. GENERAL POSITION DESCRIPTION Main Purpose of the post The Procurement Officer is responsible for the timely and cost-effective acquisition of goods, services, and works necessary for the operation of Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise. The Officer ensures that all procurement activities are conducted in strict compliance with the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Proclamation, the Public Procurement Directive, and the enterprise’s internal manuals. The role focuses on ensuring "Value for Money," transparency, and fairness in the selection of suppliers, while maintaining the technical and quality standards required for pharmaceutical and administrative inputs. I. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY A. Procurement Planning and Requisition Handling 1. Assists in the preparation of the Enterprise’s Annual Procurement Plan based on inputs from various departments and projects. 2. Reviews and verifies purchase requisitions to ensure specifications are clear, authorized, and supported by budget availability. 3. Consolidates requirements to achieve economies of scale and updates the procurement schedule regularly. B. Sourcing and Tendering Operations 1. Prepares Bid Documents, Requests for Quotations (RFQ), and Requests for Proposals (RFP) in accordance with government standard formats. 2. Identifies and maintains a database of reliable suppliers and contractors, ensuring they are registered on the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Agency (FPPA) suppliers' list. 3. Coordinates the advertisement of tenders and manages the bid opening process in the presence of the Tender Committee and bidders. C. Evaluation and Contract Award 1. Serves as a technical member or secretary for the Procurement Endorsing/Evaluation Committee. 2. Performs commercial evaluations of bids and coordinates with technical units for quality/technical assessments. 3. Prepares evaluation reports and recommendations for award based on the "Lowest Evaluated Bid" or "Quality and Cost-Based" criteria. 4. Drafts purchase orders and formal contracts, ensuring all legal and performance security requirements are met. D. Contract Management and Follow-up 1. Monitors the delivery timelines of goods and services, ensuring suppliers adhere to the terms of the contract/PO. 2. Coordinates with the Property/Store unit to ensure that delivered items match the technical specifications and quantities ordered (Inspection and Receiving). 3. Handles claims, liquidating damages, and disputes with suppliers in consultation with the Legal unit and the Manager. E. Compliance and Record Keeping 1. Ensures that the "Five Pillars" of public procurement (Value for Money, Transparency, Non-discrimination, Accountability, and Fairness) are strictly upheld. 2. Maintains comprehensive and organized procurement files for every transaction to ensure readiness for audit by the Federal Auditor General or internal auditors. 3. Prepares periodic procurement status reports for management. II. Authority The Procurement Officer is authorized to: a. Communicate with potential suppliers to obtain market information and price estimates. b. Reject requisitions that do not meet the enterprise’s procurement guidelines or lack technical specifications. c. Propose the disqualification of bidders who fail to meet mandatory legal or technical requirements. d. Verify the accuracy of supplier invoices before they are forwarded to the Finance department for payment. Effort required 1. The position requires high integrity, negotiation skills, and the ability to work under pressure to meet project deadlines. 2. Work involves frequent market visits, attending bid openings, and detailed scrutiny of technical documents.

raw_payload.description:
Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise (EBPE) is Ethiopia’s state-owned pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise, established to build the nation’s capacity to manufacture vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, medical supplies and other healthcare technologies locally. Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services. Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services.


I. GENERAL  POSITION DESCRIPTION

Main Purpose of the post

The Procurement Officer is responsible for the timely and cost-effective acquisition of goods, services, and works necessary for the operation of Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise. The Officer ensures that all procurement activities are conducted in strict compliance with the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Proclamation, the Public Procurement Directive, and the enterprise’s internal manuals. The role focuses on ensuring "Value for Money," transparency, and fairness in the selection of suppliers, while maintaining the technical and quality standards required for pharmaceutical and administrative inputs.

I.        KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY

A. Procurement Planning and Requisition Handling

1. Assists in the preparation of the Enterprise’s Annual Procurement Plan based on inputs from various departments and projects.

2. Reviews and verifies purchase requisitions to ensure specifications are clear, authorized, and supported by budget availability.

3. Consolidates requirements to achieve economies of scale and updates the procurement schedule regularly.

B. Sourcing and Tendering Operations

1. Prepares Bid Documents, Requests for Quotations (RFQ), and Requests for Proposals (RFP) in accordance with government standard formats.

2. Identifies and maintains a database of reliable suppliers and contractors, ensuring they are registered on the Federal Public Procurement and Property Administration Agency (FPPA) suppliers' list.

3. Coordinates the advertisement of tenders and manages the bid opening process in the presence of the Tender Committee and bidders.

C. Evaluation and Contract Award

1.  Serves as a technical member or secretary for the Procurement Endorsing/Evaluation Committee.

2.  Performs commercial evaluations of bids and coordinates with technical units for quality/technical assessments.

3.  Prepares evaluation reports and recommendations for award based on the "Lowest Evaluated Bid" or "Quality and Cost-Based" criteria.

4.  Drafts purchase orders and formal contracts, ensuring all legal and performance security requirements are met.

D. Contract Management and Follow-up

1.  Monitors the delivery timelines of goods and services, ensuring suppliers adhere to the terms of the contract/PO.

2.  Coordinates with the Property/Store unit to ensure that delivered items match the technical specifications and quantities ordered (Inspection and Receiving).

3.  Handles claims, liquidating damages, and disputes with suppliers in consultation with the Legal unit and the Manager.

E. Compliance and Record Keeping

1. Ensures that the "Five Pillars" of public procurement (Value for Money, Transparency, Non-discrimination, Accountability, and Fairness) are strictly upheld.

2. Maintains comprehensive and organized procurement files for every transaction to ensure readiness for audit by the Federal Auditor General or internal auditors.

3. Prepares periodic procurement status reports for management.

II.     Authority

The Procurement Officer is authorized to:

a. Communicate with potential suppliers to obtain market information and price estimates.

b. Reject requisitions that do not meet the enterprise’s procurement guidelines or lack technical specifications.

c. Propose the disqualification of bidders who fail to meet mandatory legal or technical requirements.

d. Verify the accuracy of supplier invoices before they are forwarded to the Finance department for payment.

Effort required

1. The position requires high integrity, negotiation skills, and the ability to work under pressure to meet project deadlines.

2. Work involves frequent market visits, attending bid openings, and detailed scrutiny of technical documents.

fields.description: Position: Battery Hardware Team Lead Salary : 55,000 gross Department: Engineering / Battery Systems Reports To: Head of Engineering Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Employment Type: Full-Time Company Overview Our client is a confidential manufacturing company operating in the advanced technology and industrial manufacturing sector. The company is expanding its engineering capabilities and is seeking a technically strong Battery Hardware Team Lead to support product development, testing, and production readiness. Position Summary The Battery Hardware Team Lead will be responsible for the mechanical and electrical integration of battery pack systems, including hardware validation, testing, documentation, and failure analysis. The role provides hands-on technical leadership to engineering technicians and ensures that all battery systems meet structural, electrical, thermal, and safety requirements. Key Responsibilities Lead mechanical and electrical integration activities for battery hardware systems. Conduct and supervise environmental, thermal, vibration, shock, and electrical testing. Own engineering documentation including drawings, test reports, revision control, and engineering change records. Define quality standards, testing procedures, and acceptance criteria for hardware builds. Supervise and mentor mechanical and electrical technicians. Ensure compliance with engineering, manufacturing, and safety standards. Support continuous improvement initiatives across engineering and production operations. Coordinate with cross-functional teams including manufacturing, quality, and supply chain.

fields.description: Graphic Designer Company: RE/MAX Ethiopia Department: Marketing Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Employment Type: Full-Time About RE/MAX Ethiopia RE/MAX Ethiopia is the Ethiopian franchise of RE/MAX®, one of the world’s largest and most recognized real estate franchise organizations. As part of the global RE/MAX network, we connect property owners, developers, investors, buyers, tenants, and members of the Ethiopian diaspora with international best practices in real estate sales, marketing, consulting, and investment advisory. We are committed to raising the standard of real estate in Ethiopia through professional, transparent, technology-driven, and client-focused services. About the Role We are looking for a Graphic Designer to create visually compelling and professional marketing materials that strengthen the RE/MAX Ethiopia brand and support our marketing campaigns, property promotions, social media activities, and events. The ideal candidate will have a strong eye for design and be able to translate marketing ideas and property information into creative, engaging, and brand-consistent visual materials across both digital and print formats. Key Responsibilities Design creative and engaging visual content for social media platforms and digital marketing campaigns. Develop promotional materials for property listings, sales campaigns, events, and other marketing activities. Create designs for both digital and print use, ensuring materials are visually appealing and technically accurate. Work closely with the Marketing Manager, Digital Marketing Officer, Content Creator, and Sales Team to develop creative materials aligned with campaign objectives. Translate marketing briefs and ideas into clear, effective, and visually compelling designs. Ensure all designs consistently follow RE/MAX brand guidelines and maintain a professional brand identity. Revise and refine artwork based on feedback while maintaining design quality and project timelines. Support event branding and the development of materials for company events and promotional activities. Maintain and organize design files, templates, and other creative assets for easy access and future use. Develop and update design templates and creative formats to improve efficiency and consistency. Stay informed about current design, social media, and marketing trends and bring fresh creative ideas to the team. Review completed designs for accuracy, quality, and consistency before publication or printing. What We Are Looking For We are looking for a creative, detail-oriented, and reliable designer who can work across a range of marketing materials and understands how good design contributes to brand recognition and business growth. The ideal candidate should be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple design requests, receiving feedback, and delivering high-quality work within agreed timelines. Key Competencies Graphic Design: Strong understanding of visual design principles, composition, typography, and layout. Digital & Social Media Design: Ability to create engaging designs optimized for social media and digital platforms. Brand Consistency: Strong attention to detail and ability to consistently apply brand guidelines. Creative Thinking: Ability to develop fresh, visually compelling concepts that support marketing objectives. Time Management: Ability to manage multiple projects, respond to revisions, and deliver quality work on time.

company.name: East Africa Bottling Share Company - Coca Cola
company.name_legal: East Africa Bottling Share Company - Coca Cola
company.description:
About the company

Coca-Cola was first bottled in Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa, in 1959 by the Ethiopian Bottling Share Company, which later opened a second branch in Dire Dawa in 1965.

The two plants were nationalized in 1975 and ran as public companies until 1996 when they were bought by Ethiopian entrepreneurs through privatization. Just prior to this, in 1995, Coca-Cola Sabco bought shares in the business and, in 1999, signed joint venture agreement with Ethiopian owners. With its leadership working hand in hand with employees, the business has seen significant growth over the years. Processes and functions have improved, resulting in considerable sales increases. On July 02, 2016, SABMiller plc, The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments (controlling 80% of Coca-Cola South African Bottling Company (Sabco) officilay merged and created Africa’s largest Coca-Cola bottler - Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA)

With the aim of increasing its foot prints across the nation, a new plant was commissioned in 2016 at Bahir Dar having state-of-the-art production facility.

East Africa Bottling Share Company as a Coca Cola Franchise Bottler in Ethiopia under Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) has three production plants in Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa and Bahir Dar with an aggressive expansion plan throughout the country, hence bringing the total number of employees to more than 1,800.


Our Vision

To Refresh Africa and Create Shared Value


Our Mission

• to be the Leading and Most admired Company in Africa


Refresh Africa every day and make our continent a better place for all 

Our Values

➢   We have a passion for the coca-cola business and for the brand

➢   We think and act like “owners” at all times

➢   We work and win in teams across the business

➢   Accountability is clear and personal

➢   We hare humble but confident in all we do

➢   Safety, quality, the environment, and our communities are integral to our working lives All of this we do it with the highest integrity

Why work for us

Why join us?

  • We always act with the belief of Growing our people, "grows the busi­ ness". Our people will always be our competitive advantage. Become part of a large community where employees get a chance to network and build connections.
  • We empower our people to learn a new skill on the job through self-direction. Work with many talented and experienced people who are able to guide employees' career development.
  • Our leaders possess ample expertise in the Industry making them ideal Mentors & Coaches. As we are made up of small teams, employees will get unique opportunities to learn a variety of skills.
  • Our Genetic make-up highly values teamwork, positive attitude, effective communication, diversity, innovative mindset, agility, and continuous learning.
  • We engage in executing our social responsibility where we operate making sure we play our part in alleviating social challenges with respect to community education, women entrepreneurship, environmental protection - This is the basis for a brighter future, built on a hand up, not a handout.
  • Work for a brand that is well-known internationally and instantly recognizable. Our brand has been a leading brand for over 130 years and still continues to grow because We are not constrained by traditional thinking but prefer to "think like a consumer" and take risks.

Team Benefits

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We are true believers of pay for performance principle which is why we continuously review our packages towards motivating our people to pursue excellence in their duties and drive business productivity.


PROFESSIONAL ADVANCEMENT


Promotion and salary advancement are determined by merit based on a fair, equitable, and transparent performance measurement process, and the employee’s capability to assume increased responsibilities through the internal recruitment process.


Managers regularly review employee performance to obtain the most effective use of their services and expertise. We actively encourage our employees to upgrade their skills and broaden their experience in different functional areas through training and career development opportunities by investing in employees learning and development program.

fields.title: Human Resources Officer (Junior)
fields.description: Ascend Consulting Engineers Plc is an Ethiopian consulting engineering firm based in Addis Ababa. The firm specializes in construction contract administration, claims management and dispute resolution. We advise Employers, Contractors and Consultants on contracts governed by the FIDIC Conditions of Contract and by the Ethiopian public procurement, conditions and we represent clients in Dispute Review Expert, Dispute Board and arbitration proceedings. Our portfolio covers road, bridge, building, aviation and industrial park projects across Ethiopia. We work in small, senior teams. Every member is expected to take direct responsibility for the files placed in their hands. To meet a growing workload, the firm invites applications from qualified professionals for the following positions. Position 1: Human Resources Officer (Junior) Number required: One (1) Duty Station: Head Office, Addis Ababa Minimum Experience: 2 years Education: BA or BSc Degree Employment type: Full time, permanent, subject to a probation period Purpose of the Position: The Human Resources Officer manages the full personnel cycle of the firm, from recruitment to separation, and keeps the firm compliant with Ethiopian labour, pension and tax requirements. The role also supports the administration of staff who work remotely and staff who are seconded to project sites. Main Duties and Responsibilities: Prepare job descriptions, advertise vacancies, screen applications, arrange interviews and prepare offers of employment. Prepare employment contracts, secondment letters and amendments, and keep them properly executed and filed. Maintain complete and confidential personnel files for all staff, including qualifications, licences and professional registrations. Administer attendance, timesheets, leave, overtime records and field allowances, including for remote and site based staff, and submit the monthly input to payroll. Register and update employees with the pension scheme, income tax authority and any insurance schemes the firm maintains. Prepare and monitor staff performance evaluation cycles and keep the records that support promotion and salary review decisions. Support the preparation of staff CVs, staffing schedules and personnel schedules required for consultancy proposals and client compliance submissions. Coordinate onboarding, induction, training plans and exit formalities including clearance and final settlement. Draft internal HR circulars, policies and procedures for approval, and follow their application. Handle general office administration duties assigned by the General Manager. Terms of Employment: Salary is negotiable and will be fixed according to qualification, experience and the outcome of the interview. Benefits and allowances are provided in accordance with the firm's personnel policy. Appointment is subject to a probation period in accordance with the Ethiopian Labour Proclamation.

Amhara Bank operates a network of over 322 branches across Ethiopia, serving a customer base of approximately 2.9 million individuals.


Digital Banking

The bank provides digital financial services, primarily through a proprietary mobile banking application. The digital platform has registered over 1.2 million subscribers.

fields.title: Social Worker
fields.description: Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda) Duration: 12 months Report To: Protection Officer Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) Organizational Profile 1.1 General Information New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments. The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services. The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities. Key Responsibilities A. Community-Based Social Work Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures. Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities. Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions. Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. B. Community Mobilization and Engagement Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions. Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities. Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities. Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children. Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions. Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate. C. Protection Identification and Referral Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns. Provide information on available services and support options. Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways. Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements. Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required. Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures. D. Support to Community Protection Mechanisms Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures. Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors. Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns. Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices. Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer. E. Support to Women and Girls Safe Space Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS. Promote safe access and participation of women and girls. Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role. Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services. Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect. Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer. F. Community Prevention and Social Support Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices. Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors. Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions. Encourage positive family and community support systems. Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services. G. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement. Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer. Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback. Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements. Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible. Ensure all records are safely stored and protected. H. Safeguarding and Accountability Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies. Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members. Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns. Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles. Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

fields.title: Contract Engineer
fields.description: Ascend Consulting Engineers Plc is an Ethiopian consulting engineering firm based in Addis Ababa. The firm specializes in construction contract administration, claims management and dispute resolution. We advise Employers, Contractors and Consultants on contracts governed by the FIDIC Conditions of Contract and by the Ethiopian public procurement, conditions and we represent clients in Dispute Review Expert, Dispute Board and arbitration proceedings. Our portfolio covers road, bridge, building, aviation and industrial park projects across Ethiopia. We work in small, senior teams. Every member is expected to take direct responsibility for the files placed in their hands. To meet a growing workload, the firm invites applications from qualified professionals for the following positions. Position 2: Contract Engineer Number required: One (1) Duty Station: Head Office, with mobilization to project sites Minimum Experience: 7 years Education: BSc in Civil Engineering/COTM Employment type: Full time, permanent, subject to a probation period Purpose of the Position : The Contract Engineer takes independent responsibility for the contractual and claim files assigned to the firm. The holder prepares, defends and negotiates claims, drafts contractual correspondence, supports dispute proceedings, and guides the junior contract engineers. The position is based at the head office, but the holder must be ready to travel to any project site in the country to inspect the works, verify records, interview site staff and lead time critical assignments. Main Duties and Responsibilities: Read and interpret contract documents, particular conditions, specifications and agreements, and advise on the rights, obligations and risks of the party we represent. Identify claim events in good time, prepare and serve the required notices, and protect entitlement under the notice and time bar provisions of the contract. Prepare fully substantiated claims for extension of time, prolongation cost, disruption, acceleration, variations, price adjustment, financing charges and contractual interest. Carry out and review delay analysis using accepted methods, and check the quality of programme records and progress data supporting the analysis. Value variations, evaluate rate revision proposals, and prepare and check measurement and payment positions. Draft contractual correspondence, determinations, replies to the Engineer and the Employer, notices of suspension, reduction of rate of progress and termination, where instructed. Prepare submissions and supporting bundles for Dispute Review Experts, Dispute Boards, amicable settlement negotiations and arbitration, and attend hearings with the client. Prepare amicable settlement proposals and take part in negotiation meetings. Review tender and bid documents at bid stage, prepare requests for clarification, and produce risk analysis reports on the proposed conditions of contract. Mobilize to project sites for inspection, record verification, joint measurement, site interviews and other critical assignments. Review, correct and improve the work of the junior contract engineers, and train them on contract administration practice. Maintain an accurate register of claims, notices, deadlines and dispute milestones for each assigned project, and report status to the General Manager. Terms of Employment: Salary is negotiable and will be fixed according to qualification, experience and the outcome of the interview. Benefits and allowances are provided in accordance with the firm's personnel policy. Appointment is subject to a probation period in accordance with the Ethiopian Labour Proclamation.

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable.

  • Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems.
  • Promote locally appropriate prevention and response mechanisms for protection concerns.

  • Monitor protection risks and trends within the assigned woreda.

  • Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways.
  • Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services.
  • Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms.

D.   Community Engagement and Prevention

  • Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers.
  • Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally owned solutions to identified protection concerns.
  • Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

E.   Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls.
  • Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services.
  • Monitor the quality and accessibility of services provided through the WGSS.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, and informed choice for women and girls accessing services.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS.

F.    Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting

  • Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards.
  • Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information.
  • Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning.
  • Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially.

G.  Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards.
  • Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups.
  • Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks.
  • Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Immediately report safeguarding, PSEA, and serious protection concerns through established organizational procedures.

H.  Financial and Resource Management

  • Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures.
  • Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps.
  • Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.

fields.title: Mechanic
fields.description: Position Title: Mechanic Job Purpose To perform preventive, corrective, and breakdown maintenance of mechanical machinery and equipment to ensure reliable, safe, and efficient operation of production facilities. The position is responsible for inspection, troubleshooting, repair, adjustment, installation, and maintenance of mechanical systems while minimizing equipment downtime and supporting continuous production. Key Duties and Responsibilities Carry out preventive, corrective, and breakdown maintenance of production and utility equipment. Inspect mechanical equipment regularly to identify wear, defects, abnormal conditions, and potential failures. Diagnose mechanical faults and determine appropriate repair and maintenance requirements. Repair, replace, adjust, and align mechanical components such as bearings, shafts, gears, chains, sprockets, belts, pulleys, couplings, valves, pumps, and other machine parts. Perform mechanical maintenance on production-line equipment, conveyors, fillers, packers, compressors, pumps, mixers, and other associated machinery as applicable. Conduct machine dismantling, assembly, alignment, adjustment, and installation activities safely and correctly. Perform lubrication of machinery and equipment according to approved lubrication schedules and procedures. Monitor equipment operating conditions and identify unusual vibration, noise, temperature, leakage, or other signs of mechanical failure. Respond promptly to equipment breakdowns and carry out corrective actions to restore production safely and efficiently. Support maintenance activities during machine changeovers, installation, commissioning, and modification of equipment. Work closely with electrical, instrumentation, production, and other maintenance personnel to resolve equipment-related problems. Participate in planned preventive maintenance activities and ensure maintenance tasks are completed according to the maintenance schedule. Use appropriate hand tools, power tools, measuring instruments, and maintenance equipment safely and correctly. Conduct basic measurements and inspections to verify equipment alignment, clearances, dimensions, and operating conditions. Ensure that repaired equipment is properly tested and safe for operation before handing it over to the production team. Maintain accurate records of breakdowns, maintenance activities, spare parts used, equipment condition, and repair history. Report equipment defects, spare-part requirements, safety hazards, and other maintenance issues to the immediate supervisor. Maintain and properly use maintenance tools, equipment, and workshop facilities. Ensure proper housekeeping and 5S standards in the workshop and maintenance work areas. Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), permit-to-work, machine isolation, and other applicable safety procedures before undertaking maintenance work. Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety, environmental, quality, food safety, GMP, and company requirements. Participate in root-cause analysis of repeated equipment failures and recommend corrective and preventive actions. Contribute to reducing machine downtime, maintenance costs, equipment failures, and production losses. Participate in continuous improvement activities to improve equipment reliability, availability, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE). Perform other related duties assigned by the immediate supervisor.

fields.title: RMNCH Commodity and Service-Delivery Lead
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Ensure that the program addresses the distinct forecasting, availability, quality, accountability and service-readiness requirements of maternal, newborn and child health commodities, including their relationship to family planning and primary-healthcare services. Key responsibilities · Map priority RMNCH commodity pathways, service protocols, consumption signals, resupply processes and causes of missed service opportunities. · Define and maintain the prioritized commodity list, product attributes, kit relationships, substitutions and service-readiness rules. · Translate clinical and program requirements into transactional workflows, data elements, alerts and performance indicators. · Ensure alignment between commodity data, service-delivery events, eCHIS or other service systems and national product and facility registries. · Support forecasting, quantification, inventory policy, redistribution and replenishment approaches for priority commodities. · Work with facilities and program teams to test whether digital information results in timely operational decisions. · Design and support training, supportive supervision, review meetings and corrective-action processes. · Identify gender, equity and access implications of commodity gaps and proposed digital workflows. · Support evaluation, learning and development of scale-up and sustainability recommendations. Expected results · A validated RMNCH commodity and service-readiness requirements package. · Improved visibility and response to priority commodity gaps at service-delivery points. · Operational linkages between commodity availability, service plans and performance reviews. · Institutionalized SOPs and decision routines for RMNCH commodity management.

raw_payload.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead

Role purpose

Ensure that the program addresses the distinct forecasting, availability, quality, accountability and service-readiness requirements of maternal, newborn and child health commodities, including their relationship to family planning and primary-healthcare services.

Key responsibilities

· Map priority RMNCH commodity pathways, service protocols, consumption signals, resupply processes and causes of missed service opportunities.

· Define and maintain the prioritized commodity list, product attributes, kit relationships, substitutions and service-readiness rules.

· Translate clinical and program requirements into transactional workflows, data elements, alerts and performance indicators.

· Ensure alignment between commodity data, service-delivery events, eCHIS or other service systems and national product and facility registries.

· Support forecasting, quantification, inventory policy, redistribution and replenishment approaches for priority commodities.

· Work with facilities and program teams to test whether digital information results in timely operational decisions.

· Design and support training, supportive supervision, review meetings and corrective-action processes.

· Identify gender, equity and access implications of commodity gaps and proposed digital workflows.

· Support evaluation, learning and development of scale-up and sustainability recommendations.

Expected results

· A validated RMNCH commodity and service-readiness requirements package.

· Improved visibility and response to priority commodity gaps at service-delivery points.

· Operational linkages between commodity availability, service plans and performance reviews.

· Institutionalized SOPs and decision routines for RMNCH commodity management.

About Us


Mullege PLC is a prominent coffee exporter in Ethiopia, specializing in green Arabica coffee beans. With over three decades of experience, the company has grown from a small supplier to an internationally recognized exporter, serving clients on four continents. They operate two major plants in Addis Ababa and have a substantial annual production capacity and logistics operations. Additionally, Mullege maintains a state-of-the-art warehouse with a capacity to store over 5,000 tons of coffee. 


Our vision


Mullege's vision is to become an internationally recognized exporter of green coffee beans, driven by a strong foundation, innovative ideas, and dedication. Their mission is to provide the most refined coffee to coffee lovers globally through two processing plants in Addis Ababa and pulping stations across Ethiopia. They also aim to be a recognized freight service provider, as evidenced by their national recognition and significant revenue. 


Our success

Mullege PLC is a prominent coffee exporter in Ethiopia, specializing in green Arabica coffee beans. With over three decades of experience, the company has grown from a small supplier to an internationally recognized exporter, serving clients on four continents. They operate two major plants in Addis Ababa and have a substantial annual production capacity and logistics operations. Additionally, Mullege maintains a state-of-the-art warehouse with a capacity to store over 5,000 tons of coffee. 


Our vision


Mullege's vision is to become an internationally recognized exporter of green coffee beans, driven by a strong foundation, innovative ideas, and dedication. Their mission is to provide the most refined coffee to coffee lovers globally through two processing plants in Addis Ababa and pulping stations across Ethiopia. They also aim to be a recognized freight service provider, as evidenced by their national recognition and significant revenue. 


Our success


Mullege's success story highlights its evolution from a small coffee supplier to a major exporter within three generations. Its commitment to quality control, efficient logistics, and a global reach is key to its success. Mullege has a substantial annual production capacity of 22,000 tons of coffee and a state-of-the-art warehouse. It also owns and operates a fleet of trucks for efficient coffee transportation.

Salary: As per the Organization's Scale The Organization Addis Jemari is a non-governmental organization operating in Addis Ababa. Job Summary The Family Empowerment Program (FEP) Social worker is responsible for assisting and monitoring the socio-economic development of the beneficiaries based on the program. This role will support Health Centers, Health Posts, and communities, coordinating IYCF in emergency strategies, providing nutrition education, and enhancing health outcomes for mothers and children in the project areas. Support the integration of accountability practices into program activities by following established procedures during planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding. Perform another Other duty as required.

company.name: Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association(EWLA)
company.description:
The Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA) is a non-profit women's advocacy group founded by Ethiopian women lawyers. It was legally registered in 1995 and began operation in 1996. EWLA is headquartered in Addis Ababa and has six branches in Bahir Dar, Assosa, Hawassa, Adama/Nazareth, Diredawa and Gambella. The branch/regional offices are supported by 53 trained voluntary committee members organized at woreda and zonal levels; these offices provide structures to reach women at grass root level in Ethiopia.

EWLA’s vision is to see a country where women are equal to men and articulates its mission as promoting the economic, political, social and legal rights of women and assist them to secure full protection of their rights under the Constitution of Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia and other international human rights conventions. 

 

The Association, to achieve its mission, works through three core programs:

Under its Legal Aid Program EWLA assists women, particularly disadvantaged women, who are victims of gender-based violence free of charge. The service includes legal advice/counseling, writing court briefs (court charges and affidavits) as well as representing clients in courts.  

The second program, Public Education and Capacity Building Program works on raising awareness on women's rights. This program conducts training and advocacy workshops on the legal, social and political rights of women for students, government, and civil society organization (CSO) employees.

Through the third program, Research and Law Reform Advocacy, EWLA conducts various researches on women's rights issues and findings are used as a major resource for law reform advocacy and public education.

raw_payload.description:
TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR)

Development of a Standardized Paralegal Training Curriculum and Manual for EWLA Volunteer Committee Members

Background

The Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA) has been working for over three decades to advance women's rights, access to justice, and legal reform in Ethiopia. EWLA provides free legal aid services to women and girls through its Head Office, regional branch offices, and volunteer committees operating at zonal and woreda levels across nine regional states. These services are further supported by a network of volunteer members, including lawyers, law graduates, and community-based paralegals.

EWLA's volunteer committee members often serve as the first point of contact for women seeking legal assistance on matters such as family law, gender-based violence (GBV), property and inheritance disputes, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), and other human rights issues. They play a critical role in facilitating access to justice for women and girls within their communities. It is therefore essential to strengthen their capacity to deliver quality, gender-responsive, and survivor-centered legal aid services.

Although EWLA has provided training to volunteers on basic laws, legal procedures, and the legal frameworks that safeguard the rights of women and children, there remains a need to standardize the training content and delivery methods. A comprehensive and consistent training program should be provided regularly to all EWLA volunteers to ensure the quality and effectiveness of legal aid services across all regions.

To this end, EWLA seeks to engage qualified expert(s) to develop a standardized paralegal training manual and curriculum that will serve as the foundation for capacity-building initiatives for its volunteer committees nationwide.

Objectives of the Assignment

Overall Objective

To develop a standardized, practical, and Ethiopia-specific Paralegal Aid Training Manual that strengthens the knowledge, skills, and ethical grounding of EWLA's volunteer paralegal aid providers.

Specific Objectives

  • Develop a curriculum, modular training manual covering core legal knowledge, referral pathways, and paralegal skills relevant to EWLA's legal aid mandate
  • Ensure the manual reflects current Ethiopian law, including family law (federal and regional laws), criminal law provisions on GBV/HTPs, property/inheritance law (including land rights), labor laws and SRHR-related legal protections
  • Incorporate survivor-centered, trauma-informed, and confidentiality-based approaches consistent with EWLA's institutional values
  • Produce accompanying facilitation tools (trainer's guide, session plans, case scenarios, assessment tools) to support consistent delivery across branch offices
  • Ensure the manual is written in accessible language for volunteers without formal legal training in (Amharic and English)

Main Tasks

Inception and Planning

  • Develop an inception note outlining methodology, scope, structure, and timeline
  • Review existing EWLA materials and identify content areas to be prioritized

Desk Review and Content Mapping

  • Conduct a comprehensive review of relevant Ethiopian laws
  • Review prior training or induction materials used by EWLA, if any
  • Identify core substantive and procedural content areas to be covered in the manual

Training Needs Consultation

  • Conduct consultations (interviews/focus group discussions) with EWLA staff, branch office coordinators, and a sample of current volunteer paralegals
  • Identify existing capacity gaps, common case types, and practical challenges faced by volunteers in the field
  • Document findings in a brief training needs summary

Manual Drafting

  • Develop a detailed curriculum and manual outline/table of contents for EWLA review and approval
  • Draft the full training manual, covering at minimum:
    • Roles, responsibilities, and ethical conduct of paralegal aid volunteers, including confidentiality and do-no-harm principles
    • Overview of the Ethiopian legal system and relevant institutions (courts, police, prosecutors, social affairs bureaus)
    • Core substantive law modules: family law, GBV-related criminal law, property and inheritance, labor and SRHR legal protections
    • Client interviewing, basic case documentation, and referral pathways
    • Survivor-centered and trauma-informed communication techniques
    • Case studies and practice scenarios grounded in the Ethiopian context

Trainer's Guide Development

  • Develop a companion trainer's guide with session plans, timing, suggested methodology, and pre/post-training assessment tools
  • Prepare PowerPoint Presentation
  • Pilot test the manual through the provision training to paralegals

Pilot test, Review and Validation

  • Incorporate feedback from EWLA Head Office through at least two rounds of review and revision
  • Facilitate an internal validation session with relevant staff and volunteer representatives
  • Finalize the manual based on the pilot test and validations feedback.

Scope of the Training Manual

The manual will cover (but is not limited to):

1 Substantive and Procedural Legal Content

  • Family law (marriage, divorce, inheritance)
  • Criminal law provisions related to GBV/VAW
  • Property and inheritance rights (including land rights
  • Extra contractual liabilities
  • SRHR-related legal protections
  • ADR/ customary court laws and guides
  • Relevant procedural and referral frameworks
    • Criminal procedure and evidence law relevant to GBV/VAW
    • Civil procedure law – basic procedural and evidence requirement

2 Paralegal Skills and Conduct

  • Client interviewing and basic case documentation
  • Referral pathways and case management
  • Ethical conduct, confidentiality, and do-no-harm principles
  • Survivor-centered, trauma-informed communication

3 Audience and Use

  • Primary audience: EWLA volunteer paralegal aid members (community-based paralegals, law graduates, volunteer lawyers)
  • Use context: induction training, refresher training, and ongoing reference at Head Office and branch offices

Key Deliverables

  • Inception note (methodology and work plan)
  • Training needs summary
  • Draft manual outline/table of contents
  • First full draft of the training manual
  • Trainer's guide (session plans, methodology, assessment tools)
  • Pilot test
  • Final training manual and trainer's guide, print-ready  and PPP (Amharic and English

fields.description: Job Title: Nephrologist Location: Silk Road Hospital Date: August 8th, 2026 Employment Type: Part-time Job Summary The Nephrologist is responsible for providing specialized medical care to patients with kidney diseases and related conditions. The role involves assessing, diagnosing, treating, and managing acute and chronic renal disorders, developing individualized treatment plans, and promoting preventive care. The Nephrologist collaborates with multidisciplinary healthcare teams to ensure high-quality, patient-centered care while maintaining accurate medical records and adhering to professional and ethical standards. This is a part-time position at Silk Road General Hospital. Duties & Responsibilities Examine, diagnose, and treat patients with acute and chronic kidney diseases and related medical conditions. Evaluate patients by reviewing medical histories, conducting physical examinations, and interpreting laboratory and diagnostic test results. Develop and implement individualized treatment and follow-up plans based on patients’ clinical needs. Manage chronic kidney disease, hypertension, electrolyte imbalances, and other renal disorders using evidence-based practices. Prescribe medications and other appropriate treatments in accordance with established clinical guidelines. Educate patients and their families on kidney disease prevention, treatment options, lifestyle modifications, and medication adherence. Refer patients for dialysis, kidney transplantation, or other specialized services when clinically indicated. Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals to ensure coordinated, high-quality patient care. Maintain accurate, complete, and timely medical records in accordance with hospital policies and regulatory requirements. Adhere to professional ethics, clinical standards, infection prevention protocols, and hospital policies. Participate in quality improvement initiatives, continuing medical education, and departmental activities as required.

AASRH includes Medical Departments with Operating Room, Training Center, Intensive Care Unit, Outpatient Department, Emergency Room, Hemodialysis/Lithotripsy Center, Diagnostic Center, and Administrative/Logistics center and provides the high level of acute care, general, intermediate, and intensive/critical care with the services of general internal medicine, neurosurgery, cardiology, endocrinology, obstetrics, gynecology, urology, orthopedics, E.E.N.T, ophthalmology, dentistry, and pediatrics.

Generic Functions: · Actively participate in developing, reviewing and implementing policies & procedures, plan /budget of the division · Mentor and enable staffs below his/grades towards achieving their effective performance · Demonstrate the Bank’s code of conduct; embody the bank’s good culture and corporate image to the public · Engage in teamwork, collaboration, and transparency work practices · Provide services as per the service level agreement · Handle other related generic activities as deemed necessary Specific Functions: · Monitor the overall loan book for asset quality, delinquency, and default trends · Conduct sectoral and geographic risk assessments to identify concentration risks · Analyze trends in key credit risk indicators (NPL ratio, cost of risk ratio, coverage ratio, concentration ratios) · Develop credit & financing risk management program, risk appetite, limit, policies, procedures and/or guidelines in line with the Bank’s strategic policies · Prepare regular and executive level credit and financing portfolio reports · Handle other related duties as may be required

company.name: Amhara Bank S.C.
company.description:
The bank was established with the largest initial shareholder base in the history of Ethiopia's private banking sector, comprising over 167,000 shareholders. The bank's paid-up capital has reached more than 7.4 billion ETB. As of recent financial reporting, its total capital reserves exceed 10.285 billion Birr.


Operations and Services

Amhara Bank operates a network of over 322 branches across Ethiopia, serving a customer base of approximately 2.9 million individuals.


Digital Banking

The bank provides digital financial services, primarily through a proprietary mobile banking application. The digital platform has registered over 1.2 million subscribers.


Interest-Free Banking

Amhara Bank operates a full-fledged interest-free banking (IFB) window under the brand name "Marhaba," which was launched on March 18, 2023. The service offers Sharia-compliant financial products tailored for customers seeking non-interest financial solutions.

The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments. The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services. The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities. Key Responsibilities A. Community-Based Social Work Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures. Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities. Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions. Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. B. Community Mobilization and Engagement Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions. Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities. Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities. Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children. Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions. Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate. C. Protection Identification and Referral Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns. Provide information on available services and support options. Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways. Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements. Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required. Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures. D. Support to Community Protection Mechanisms Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures. Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors. Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns. Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices. Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer. E. Support to Women and Girls Safe Space Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS. Promote safe access and participation of women and girls. Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role. Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services. Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect. Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer. F. Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors. Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions. Encourage positive family and community support systems. Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services. G. Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback. Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements. Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible. Ensure all records are safely stored and protected. H. Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members. Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns. Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles. Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.
