Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.

  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

fields.title: Product Director / Product Owner
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Own the end-to-end product strategy and translate real supply-chain and service-delivery problems into prioritized, testable and sustainable digital capabilities. The Product Director will ensure that ForLab+ strengthens existing transactional and national systems rather than becoming a parallel reporting platform. Key responsibilities · Define the product vision, operating model, outcomes, roadmap and release priorities in partnership with government and users. · Lead discovery with health facilities, woreda teams, regional managers, supply hubs and national programs to document actual decisions, workflows and constraints. · Convert workflows into clear user stories, acceptance criteria, data requirements and measurable product outcomes. · Prioritize capabilities that improve source transaction capture, inventory accuracy, traceability, replenishment and closed-loop issue resolution. · Maintain alignment between ForLab+, authoritative registries, existing logistics systems, service-delivery systems and national analytics platforms. · Balance user value, policy requirements, interoperability dependencies, technical feasibility, cost and transition readiness. · Lead usability testing, pilot feedback loops, backlog refinement, release acceptance and product performance reviews. · Define adoption and usage measures, including active use, workflow completion, data quality, latency and action closure. · Build government product-management capacity and transfer the roadmap, backlog and release-governance processes. Expected results · A stakeholder-approved product strategy and phased roadmap tied to operational outcomes. · Validated workflows and requirements covering vaccines and RMNCH commodities at relevant supply-chain levels. · Usable, offline-capable product releases accepted by representative end users. · A government-owned product backlog, release process and performance-monitoring approach.

fields.title: Vaccine Supply-Chain Lead
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Provide authoritative technical leadership on vaccine forecasting, allocation, storage, distribution, cold chain, wastage, accountability and the connection between vaccine availability and immunization service delivery. Key responsibilities · Map vaccine flows, decision rights, information flows and performance bottlenecks from national level to service-delivery points. · Define functional requirements for vaccine receipts, issues, adjustments, stock counts, batch and expiry tracking, temperature events and outreach allocation. · Ensure that digital workflows support forecasting, replenishment, redistribution, new vaccine introduction and immunization microplanning. · Specify indicators and business rules for stock availability, wastage, expiry, cold-chain excursions, emergency resupply and session readiness. · Work with product and technical teams to validate data models, workflows, alerts and decision-support logic. · Support pilot-site selection, baseline assessment, training, supportive supervision and performance reviews. · Facilitate coordination among EPI, supply-chain agencies, cold-chain functions, regional bureaus, woredas and facilities. · Document and test SOPs and accountability mechanisms for responding to vaccine-supply risks. · Support evaluation, interpretation of findings, national learning and scale-up recommendations. Expected results · Validated vaccine supply-chain workflows and digital requirements. · Improved visibility of vaccine stock, batch, expiry, wastage and cold-chain risks in pilot areas. · Documented evidence that data are used for allocation, replenishment, redistribution and service planning. · Vaccine-management SOPs and competency-development materials integrated into routine practice.

raw_payload.description:
Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark

Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda)

Duration: 12 months

Report To: Project Coordinator

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable.

The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Protection Programme Coordination

  • Lead the day-to-day implementation of protection activities in the assigned woreda.
  • Translate project plans and objectives into practical woreda-level implementation plans.
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved plans, budgets, quality standards, and timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with the Project Coordinator on progress, priorities, challenges, and required actions.
  • Provide technical supervision and guidance to the Social Worker.
  • Maintain effective coordination with relevant government offices, community structures, religious leaders, and other stakeholders.
  • Represent the project in relevant woreda-level coordination forums and meetings.
  • Identify protection risks, operational challenges, and emerging needs and recommend appropriate responses.

B.   Community-Based Protection and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming.
  • Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms.
  • Facilitate meaningful engagement of community leaders, religious leaders, local authorities, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other relevant groups.
  • Promote community-led identification and prioritization of protection concerns and solutions.
  • Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems.
  • Promote locally appropriate prevention and response mechanisms for protection concerns.

C.   Protection Risk Identification and Referral

  • Monitor protection risks and trends within the assigned woreda.
  • Ensure appropriate identification and referral of individuals requiring specialized protection and other essential services.
  • Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways.
  • Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services.
  • Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms.

D.   Community Engagement and Prevention

  • Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers.
  • Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally owned solutions to identified protection concerns.
  • Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

E.   Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls.
  • Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services.
  • Monitor the quality and accessibility of services provided through the WGSS.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, and informed choice for women and girls accessing services.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS.

F.    Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting

  • Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards.
  • Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information.
  • Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning.
  • Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially.

G.  Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards.
  • Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups.
  • Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks.
  • Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Immediately report safeguarding, PSEA, and serious protection concerns through established organizational procedures.

H.  Financial and Resource Management

  • Support efficient use of project resources at woreda level.
  • Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures.
  • Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps.
  • Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.

GIZ works worldwide in the field of international cooperation for sustainable development and has over 50 years of experience in a wide variety of areas. The Project “Support to the Transitional Justice Process in Ethiopia” (S2TJ) is accompanying the Ethiopian Transitional Justice (TJ) process as per Ethiopia’s TJ policy from 2024. The project is advising and strengthening key government institutions as well as Civil Society Organizations (CSO) in order to promote an inclusive, gender responsive, survivor- and victim centred TJ-process in line with international human rights standards. To this end, S2TJ is cooperating with associations of victims and survivors of grave human rights violations, conflict, displacement, SGBV and other types of atrocities. This collaborative support focuses on network building within and across regions, capacity building on TJ-related topics, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), memorialization, peacebuilding initiatives, and organizational development support. fields.description: Company: RE/MAX Ethiopia Department: Marketing Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Employment Type: Full-Time About RE/MAX Ethiopia RE/MAX Ethiopia is the Ethiopian franchise of RE/MAX®, one of the world’s largest and most recognized real estate franchise organizations. As part of the global RE/MAX network, we connect property owners, developers, investors, buyers, tenants, and members of the Ethiopian diaspora with international best practices in real estate sales, marketing, consulting, and investment advisory. We are committed to raising the standard of real estate in Ethiopia through professional, transparent, technology-driven, and client-focused services. About the Role We are looking for a Content Creator – Photo, Video & Content Production to produce high-quality visual and storytelling content that showcases properties, promotes our agents and services, documents events, and strengthens the RE/MAX Ethiopia brand. The ideal candidate is a creative, hands-on visual storyteller who can take an idea from concept to final production from planning a shoot and capturing compelling footage to editing polished photos, videos, Reels, and promotional content for digital platforms. Key Responsibilities Plan and execute photo and video shoots for properties, agents, events, campaigns, and other RE/MAX Ethiopia activities. Capture high-quality property photography and videography that presents properties accurately and attractively. Produce engaging short-form video content, including Reels and other social media videos. Create video content featuring agents, including interviews, testimonials, educational content, and promotional pieces. Develop creative concepts and storytelling approaches for property marketing, brand campaigns, social media, and promotional activities. Edit photos and videos to produce polished, professional, and platform-ready content. Work closely with the Digital Marketing Officer, Marketing Manager, Sales Team, and other relevant team members to develop content aligned with marketing objectives. Coordinate and manage shooting schedules and ensure assigned properties, events, and activities are properly documented. Organize, manage, and archive photo and video files so that completed projects and media assets are easily accessible. Stay up to date with current social media formats, visual trends, and creative content styles, and introduce new ideas and approaches. Review content performance and use insights from high-performing content to improve future creative concepts and production. Ensure all visual content consistently reflects RE/MAX Ethiopia’s brand identity and professional standards. What We Are Looking For We are looking for a creative, hands-on, and visually driven content creator who can confidently handle the full content production process. You should be comfortable working on location, particularly at properties and events, and able to turn real estate spaces, people, and stories into engaging content. The ideal candidate should have a strong eye for visual quality, be willing to experiment with new creative ideas, and be able to work independently while collaborating closely with the marketing and sales teams. Key Competencies Photography & Videography: Strong ability to capture high-quality photos and video, particularly for property and lifestyle content. Video Editing: Ability to edit professional, engaging short-form and promotional videos. Creative Storytelling: Ability to develop concepts and turn properties, people, and events into compelling visual stories. Social Media Content: Understanding of current social media formats, Reels, short-form video, and content trends. Creativity & Initiative: Strong creative instincts, attention to detail, and the initiative to continuously develop new content ideas.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute photo and video shoots for properties, agents, events, campaigns, and other RE/MAX Ethiopia activities.
  • Capture high-quality property photography and videography that presents properties accurately and attractively.
  • Produce engaging short-form video content, including Reels and other social media videos.
  • Create video content featuring agents, including interviews, testimonials, educational content, and promotional pieces.
  • Develop creative concepts and storytelling approaches for property marketing, brand campaigns, social media, and promotional activities.
  • Edit photos and videos to produce polished, professional, and platform-ready content.
  • Work closely with the Digital Marketing Officer, Marketing Manager, Sales Team, and other relevant team members to develop content aligned with marketing objectives.
  • Coordinate and manage shooting schedules and ensure assigned properties, events, and activities are properly documented.
  • Organize, manage, and archive photo and video files so that completed projects and media assets are easily accessible.
  • Stay up to date with current social media formats, visual trends, and creative content styles, and introduce new ideas and approaches.
  • Review content performance and use insights from high-performing content to improve future creative concepts and production.
  • Ensure all visual content consistently reflects RE/MAX Ethiopia’s brand identity and professional standards.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for a creative, hands-on, and visually driven content creator who can confidently handle the full content production process. You should be comfortable working on location, particularly at properties and events, and able to turn real estate spaces, people, and stories into engaging content.

The ideal candidate should have a strong eye for visual quality, be willing to experiment with new creative ideas, and be able to work independently while collaborating closely with the marketing and sales teams.

Key Competencies

  • Photography & Videography: Strong ability to capture high-quality photos and video, particularly for property and lifestyle content.
  • Video Editing: Ability to edit professional, engaging short-form and promotional videos.
  • Creative Storytelling: Ability to develop concepts and turn properties, people, and events into compelling visual stories.
  • Social Media Content: Understanding of current social media formats, Reels, short-form video, and content trends.
  • Creativity & Initiative: Strong creative instincts, attention to detail, and the initiative to continuously develop new content ideas.

fields.title: DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
fields.description: Birrama Digital Commerce PLC is seeking a skilled and hands-on DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer to manage, secure, automate, and continuously improve the company's technology infrastructure. The successful candidate will work across Linux systems, local/private and public cloud environments, networking, containerized applications, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure security, monitoring, and observability. This is a practical engineering role suited for someone who is comfortable working directly with production environments, troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues, automating deployments, and ensuring that systems and applications remain secure, reliable, scalable, and highly available. Strong practical experience with local/private cloud infrastructure is particularly valued for this position. Key Responsibilities 1. Operating Systems & Networking Administer and maintain Linux-based environments, particularly Ubuntu, RHEL, and Alpine Linux . Manage operating system packages, updates, patches, system services, and dependencies. Monitor and optimize server performance and resource utilization. Configure and maintain users, groups, directories, file permissions, and access controls. Troubleshoot Linux server, operating system, and application-level issues. Configure and manage DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, and related network protocols . Install, renew, configure, and troubleshoot SSL/TLS certificates . Manage SSH keys and secure remote access. Configure and maintain firewall rules and network access controls. Diagnose network connectivity, routing, DNS, ports, latency, and service availability issues. 2. Cloud Infrastructure & Services Deploy, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot virtual machines and cloud compute resources. Manage infrastructure hosted primarily on local/private cloud environments , as well as public cloud platforms where required. Administer object storage solutions such as S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage , or similar platforms. Configure and manage: Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) Subnets Routing NAT gateways Load balancers Security groups Firewall rules Implement and maintain secure Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies. Apply the principle of least privilege across infrastructure resources. Monitor infrastructure utilization and recommend improvements related to performance, scalability, availability, security, and cost. Support backup, recovery, business continuity, and disaster recovery processes. Maintain appropriate separation between development, testing/staging, and production environments. 3. Containerization & Kubernetes Build and maintain optimized and secure Docker images and Dockerfiles . Implement multi-stage Docker builds to improve image efficiency and security. Manage container registries and image versioning. Implement or integrate container vulnerability and security scanning. Deploy, configure, and maintain containerized applications. Manage Kubernetes (K8s) workloads and infrastructure. Configure, manage, and troubleshoot: Pods Deployments StatefulSets Services ConfigMaps Secrets Persistent Volumes Ingress Controllers Manage application deployments and configurations using Helm charts . Troubleshoot failed deployments, pod failures, networking problems, resource constraints, and other Kubernetes-related incidents. Support scaling, resilience, high availability, and efficient resource allocation for containerized workloads. 4. CI/CD, Automation & Version Control Manage source code and infrastructure repositories using Git . Work with platforms such as GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket . Design, build, maintain, and improve automated CI/CD pipelines . Automate software build, testing, packaging, and deployment processes. Work with CI/CD and GitOps technologies such as: GitHub Actions GitLab CI/CD Jenkins ArgoCD Implement controlled deployment processes across development, staging, and production environments. Securely manage secrets, environment variables, credentials, and deployment permissions. Identify and automate repetitive infrastructure and operational tasks. Maintain clear versioning, rollback, and deployment procedures. 5. Monitoring, Logging & Observability Establish and maintain monitoring for infrastructure, applications, containers, and services. Develop operational dashboards providing visibility into system health and performance. Configure alerts for system failures, performance degradation, unusual behavior, and capacity limitations. Work with monitoring and observability platforms such as: Prometheus Grafana Datadog New Relic Implement centralized log collection, aggregation, analysis, and retention. Work with logging and tracing technologies including: Elasticsearch Logstash Kibana Fluentd / Fluent Bit CloudWatch GCP Cloud Logging Similar cloud-native tools Support distributed tracing and application diagnostics where required. Investigate production incidents using metrics, logs, and traces. Conduct root-cause analysis and recommend preventive measures. 6. Infrastructure Security & Reliability Apply infrastructure security best practices across servers, networks, cloud resources, containers, and Kubernetes environments. Regularly patch and update operating systems, infrastructure components, and dependencies. Securely manage certificates, access credentials, SSH keys, secrets, and tokens. Identify infrastructure vulnerabilities and coordinate remediation. Implement and maintain backup and restoration procedures. Support the high availability and reliability of production systems. Participate in infrastructure-related incident response and resolution. Document incidents, root causes, corrective actions, and preventive measures. 7. Documentation & Technical Collaboration Maintain accurate technical documentation for infrastructure architecture, configurations, deployment procedures, and operational workflows. Prepare deployment guides, troubleshooting procedures, operational runbooks, and recovery documentation. Work closely with software developers and other technical team members to improve application deployment and operational reliability. Support development teams in resolving infrastructure and environment-related issues. Recommend improvements to infrastructure architecture, automation, security, scalability, and operational processes.

company.name: Repi Soap & Detergent PLC
company.description:
REPI SOAP & DETERGENT PLC formerly known as REPI Soap factory was established 1974 by the name Bianil Ethiopia Share Company by foreign investors of Swiss & Greek origin aiming to produce and distributed powdered detergent to East Africa market which was dominantly by Uniliver brand OMO. Less than a year after its formation, it was owned by the Ethiopian government & was managed under the direct supervision of the National Chemical Corporation and was re-established as a public enterprise in 1992 by the council of Ministers and was recapitalized by Birr 1,525,000.00.

 

At that time, the company main vision was  to compete  against  local & imported powder detergent through its famous brand “ROL” , due to the machinery age and technological issues there was an issue of wastage which nearly bankrupted the company but thanks to a pioneering idea of creating detergent bar (cake) in 1979, Repi gave birth to a new line of product and a new brand  “Ajax”. Again in 1994 production of a liquid detergent was introduced under the brand name ‘LARGO”

Following the earmarking of REPI Soap factory by the government for joint venture partnership , LINA PLC having registered its interest in the joint venture Commissioned Vision Consultancy PVT LTD CO to undertake a series of studies on the factory with the aim of concluding a joint venture agreement with the factory management and the E.F.D.R Privatization & Public Enterprise Supervising Authority.

 

A joint venture partnership between “LENA PLC” and E.F.D.R Privatization & Public Enterprise Supervising Authority (PESSA) was then established  during the fiscal  period 2007/2008 after intensive negotiation was carried out between both parties involved which there after paved the way for the establishment of REPI SOAP & DETERGENT SHARE COMPANY.

 

LINA PLC is a share company  mainly involved  in trading ,real estate  and small scale manufacturing of corrugated steel & tea and added REPI SOAP & DETERGENT PLC to its portfolio of investment by acquiring 51% of share amounting to Birr 9,360,000.00 of the total share amounting to 18,360 ,000 while the remaining 49% amounting to birr 9,000,000 was raised by PESSA in the form of assets based on business evaluation of the factory.

The joint venture arrangement lasted one year followed by a full takeover of the share company by

LENA PLC after settling of the remaining 49% share previously held by the Ethiopian government.

 

 In response to the growing demands of the soap & detergent, today our company is a leading player  and well respected organization in the country detergent industry. The current market demand for our product and the fact that the current factory could not provide us the product volume due to imperfect condition and age of machinery and equipment’s therefore not supplying the capacity required ,we are committed to exciting expansion project  which is in a final phase ,would be beneficial for the shareholder ,employees local businesses and overall the company. In this sector REPI has positioned itself at the fore-front of the market.

In July,2014 Repi Soap and Detergent S. Co. (Repi) and Wilmar International Limited (Wilmar) have signed a joint investment agreement for the upgrading of an existing manufacturing facility in Sebeta Road, Kolfe Karenio Sub City and building of a new integrated manufacturing complex in Dima, Sebeta Town, Oromia Region in Ethiopia that will house an edible oil refinery and packing plant, production plants for specialty fats, soft oils, soaps and detergents, as well as a facility for sesame seed processing. Repi and Wilmar will each have a 50%participation in the joint investment.

Repi is a sister company of AL-SAM Private Limited Company, incorporated and existing under the laws of the Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. It engages in the manufacturing of soap and detergent products. Headquartered in Singapore, Wilmar is Asia’s leading agribusiness group engaging in oil palm cultivation, oilseed crushing, edible oils refining, sugar milling and refining, specialty fats, oleo-chemical, biodiesel and fertilizer manufacturing, and grain processing. It has a presence in 14 countries across Africa. This joint investment marks Wilmar’s first operations in Ethiopia.

Combining the expertise of both parties, the joint investment will have a positive impact on the development of the manufacturing and export sector, as well as create employment opportunities in Ethiopia.



About Wilmar

﻿

Wilmar International Limited, founded in 1991 and headquartered in Singapore, is today Asia’s leading agribusiness group. Wilmar is ranked amongst the largest listed companies by market capitalisation on the Singapore Exchange.Wilmar’s business activities include oil palm cultivation, oilseed crushing, edible oilsrefining, sugar milling and refining, specialty fats, oleochemical, biodiesel and fertiliser manufacturing, and grain processing.

At the core of Wilmar’s strategy is a resilient integrated agribusiness model that encompasses the entire value chain of the agricultural commodity processing business, from origination and processing to branding, merchandising and distribution of a wide range of agricultural products. It has over 450 manufacturing plants and an extensive distribution network covering China, India, Indonesia and some 50 other countries. The Group is backed by a multinational workforce of about 90,000 people. Wilmar’s portfolio of high quality processed agricultural products is the preferred choice of the food manufacturing industry, as well as the industrial and consumer food businesses. Its consumer-packed products occupy a leading share in its targeted markets. Through scale, integration and the logistical advantages of its business model, Wilmar is able to extract margins at every step of the value chain, thereby reaping operational synergies and cost efficiencies.

Wilmar remains a firm advocate of sustainable growth and is committed to its role as a responsible corporate citizen.

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

company.description:
Ethiopian Engineering Corporation ( EEC) is transforming and diversifying from the current consultancy business operations. Taking advantage of the existing EEC strength and maximizing on the newly emerging external opportunities that are being prevalent with the shifts in Ethiopian Economic Policy – the Corporation is aiming to play a significant role to the success of the Ethiopian Construction Industry -by creating a vibrant business institution that will not only fill the gap that is in the current construction industry, but also replace the need for having international construction companies that are dominating the government mega scale projects.

company.name: Kerchanshe Trading Company
company.description:
About the company

As the largest producer and exporter of coffee in Ethiopia, Kerchanshe Trading has a proud history of providing quality coffees to the local and international markets. Founded on the principles of bringing fairness and transparency to the coffee value chain while satisfying customer demand, Kerchanshe is also a company with heart and vision.

Kerchanshe specializes in coffees sourced from Yirgacheffe, Lekempti, Gimbi, Djimma, and Sidamo, names that epitomise fine Arabica coffee. Since its inception 15 years ago, Kerchanshe has established a track record of fair trading and excellent customer service, and now employs over 1,250 permanent staff and 10,000 seasonal staff. Directly and indirectly, it impacts the livelihoods of over 1 million coffee growers throughout the southern and south-western coffee-cultivating regions of Ethiopia.

The passion for fine coffee is coupled with consistent reinvestment not only in improved infrastructure, technology and processes, but Kerchanshe also invests 10% of its annual profits into social responsibility programs such as building schools and providing clean water to the communities it serves

OUR VISION

To be the leader in innovation and quality among coffee producers and exporters while caring for the environment.

OUR MISSION

We are committed to providing the finest high-quality coffee beans to our customers worldwide while forging mutually beneficial relationships with the community and the environment that we live in.

QUALITY POLICY

At Kerchanshe we are highly conscious of the fact that the quality of our beans is what sets us apart.

 

Our Mission

"We are driven to deliver unparalleled quality coffee beans to discerning customers worldwide, fostering enduring relationships with both our communities and the natural world."

Our Vision

"To pioneer innovation and excellence within the global coffee industry while nurturing a profound respect for environmental preservation."

Our Values

Ethical Integrity: We steadfastly adhere to the highest ethical standards in all our dealings, prioritizing integrity and accountability.

Sustainable Practices: We embrace sustainable methodologies that seamlessly integrate with the environment, ensuring responsible stewardship of our resources.

Customer-Centric Excellence: Our unwavering commitment to consistency, integrity, and excellence ensures unparalleled service and satisfaction for our customers.

Empowered Workforce: We empower and champion our diverse workforce, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous growth.

Community Enrichment: We are deeply committed to giving back to our communities through meaningful engagement and impactful initiatives, embodying our ethos of corporate citizenship.

Why work for us

Embark on a fulfilling journey with Kerchanshe Group, where you'll discover more than just a job. Join us for stimulating career opportunities, personalized work schedules that accommodate your lifestyle, a vibrant and inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and innovation, and comprehensive compensation and benefits packages designed to enhance your overall satisfaction and well-being.

In addition to these offerings, you'll have access to ongoing professional development and training programs to further hone your skills and expand your expertise. Furthermore, at Kerchanshe, we prioritize work-life balance, providing resources and support to help you thrive both personally and professionally.

Join our community at Kerchanshe Group, where your individuality is celebrated, your growth is nurtured, and your contributions make a meaningful impact. Together, let's build a brighter future for ourselves and our communities.

Team Benefits

At Kerchanshe Group, we prioritize the welfare and satisfaction of our employees by providing a suite of professional benefits tailored to enhance their work experience. Our comprehensive offerings include:

  • Subsidized canteen services at both headquarters and coffee washing stations/farms
  • Dedicated employee transportation services
  • Annual employee recognition program, celebrating outstanding contributions
  • Provision of vehicles with fuel for executive management
  • These benefits underscore our commitment to cultivating a supportive and rewarding environment, where employee well-being and professional growth are paramount.

Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.
  • Encourage community-based prevention and referral practices.
  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of activities and community engagement.
  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies.
  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles.
  • Promote accessibility and inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
  •   Inform communities about available feedback and complaint mechanisms.

fields.description: Re-Advert Internal /External Vacancy Announcement The Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) wants to recruit employees in the following vacant positions, the details of which are mentioned below. About the Ethiopian Red Cross Society The Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) was established in 1935 and is one of the oldest and largest humanitarian organizations in Ethiopia. ERCS provides services to communities affected by natural and manmade disasters through the provision of emergency responses,ambulance and first aid, family reunification, essential drugs, water and sanitation, and other humanitarian services. ERCS also runs disaster risk reduction programs with the aim of creating resilient households and communities. Currently, the ERCS has a structure consisting of 15 Regional Offices, Zonal Branches, District/Woreda Branches, Woreda Red Cross Committees, and Kebele Red Cross committees. ERCS also runs disaster risk reduction programs relating to food security, climate change adaptation, livelihood diversification, and institutional capacity building interventions, with the aim of creating resilient households and communities. ERCS works in partnership with the Ethiopian Government, International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent (IFRC), International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), partnering National Societies, members, volunteers, and the communities we serve. I. Details of the Vacant Position Job Title: Office Assistant/Administration Assistant Work Unit: Humanitarian Supply Chain Department Reports to: Humanitarian Supply Chain Director Terms of Employment: Permanent after probation period Place of Work: Addis Ababa Salary: As per the organization's salary scale II. Job Summary The Office Assistant/Administration Assistant plays a vital role in supporting the day-to-day operations of the humanitarian supply chain department, ensuring a well-organized and efficient workplace. Reporting to the department director, this position serves as the primary point of contact for staff and stakeholders, addressing concerns related to office safety, security, and operational needs. The Office Assistant provides essential administrative support, including managing correspondence, scheduling appointments, coordinating meetings, and maintaining office systems. This role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to multitask effectively to ensure smooth office operations and enhance team productivity. Key Performance Area Acts as a primary liaison to communicate with various stakeholders on issues and problems to ensure a safe and effective office (i.e., mechanical systems, security, etc.); serves as the primary point of contact for staff concerns related to the department. Ensures appropriate documentation is shared and filed with the department director on all correspondence made with all stakeholders. Handles routine administrative matters of the humanitarian supply chain director's Office. Communicates work instructions, feedback, and directives given by the director to divisions of the department, individuals, and follows up their status. Provides administrative support in facilitating the department activities and the staff. Assist the department’s overall activities to ensure the function is sufficiently covered at all times. Makes appointments with internal and external customers on behalf of the department and reminds him/her when they are due. Transcribes audiovisual materials; types manuscripts and documents as needed proofreads same for accuracy; drafts routine letters and correspondences; scans documents and other materials and compiles reports as instructed by the department director. Summarizes reports directed to the department director and presents the same on time as instructed. Organize day-to-day office operations and procedures, including transportation, warehousing, purchasing and maintaining office supplies, and mailing and documentation. Assist in organizing, arranging, and scheduling regular and extraordinary meetings and discussions to be held with the department director and different stakeholders; takes minutes of meetings and gets the same duly signed by participants. Assist in coordinating workspaces and work with the department work units to plan and execute activities of the department to enhance smooth communication and productivity. Oversees the coordination of the department’s work units to ensure the integration of activities for better performance and creating a good team spirit. Ensures that the Office of the department and work units within the department is properly furnished, arranged, and kept clean. Closely follow up the work progress of the procurement, warehouse, and transport divisions weekly/monthly plan performance and report to the director. Summarizes reports directed to the department director and presents same on time as instructed. Classifies and codifies all incoming documents going documents/letters/electronic mails and properly file the same. Manage incoming and outgoing documents, prepare reports; track office-related spending. Performs other related duties and responsibilities of the office as assigned by the humanitarian supply chain director.

company.name_legal: East Africa Bottling Share Company - Coca Cola
company.description:
About the company

Coca-Cola was first bottled in Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa, in 1959 by the Ethiopian Bottling Share Company, which later opened a second branch in Dire Dawa in 1965.

The two plants were nationalized in 1975 and ran as public companies until 1996 when they were bought by Ethiopian entrepreneurs through privatization. Just prior to this, in 1995, Coca-Cola Sabco bought shares in the business and, in 1999, signed joint venture agreement with Ethiopian owners. With its leadership working hand in hand with employees, the business has seen significant growth over the years. Processes and functions have improved, resulting in considerable sales increases. On July 02, 2016, SABMiller plc, The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments (controlling 80% of Coca-Cola South African Bottling Company (Sabco) officilay merged and created Africa’s largest Coca-Cola bottler - Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA)

With the aim of increasing its foot prints across the nation, a new plant was commissioned in 2016 at Bahir Dar having state-of-the-art production facility.

East Africa Bottling Share Company as a Coca Cola Franchise Bottler in Ethiopia under Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) has three production plants in Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa and Bahir Dar with an aggressive expansion plan throughout the country, hence bringing the total number of employees to more than 1,800.


Our Vision

To Refresh Africa and Create Shared Value


Our Mission

• to be the Leading and Most admired Company in Africa


Refresh Africa every day and make our continent a better place for all 

Our Values

➢   We have a passion for the coca-cola business and for the brand

➢   We think and act like “owners” at all times

➢   We work and win in teams across the business

➢   Accountability is clear and personal

➢   We hare humble but confident in all we do

➢   Safety, quality, the environment, and our communities are integral to our working lives All of this we do it with the highest integrity

Why work for us

Why join us?

  • We always act with the belief of Growing our people, "grows the busi­ ness". Our people will always be our competitive advantage. Become part of a large community where employees get a chance to network and build connections.
  • We empower our people to learn a new skill on the job through self-direction. Work with many talented and experienced people who are able to guide employees' career development.
  • Our leaders possess ample expertise in the Industry making them ideal Mentors & Coaches. As we are made up of small teams, employees will get unique opportunities to learn a variety of skills.
  • Our Genetic make-up highly values teamwork, positive attitude, effective communication, diversity, innovative mindset, agility, and continuous learning.
  • We engage in executing our social responsibility where we operate making sure we play our part in alleviating social challenges with respect to community education, women entrepreneurship, environmental protection - This is the basis for a brighter future, built on a hand up, not a handout.
  • Work for a brand that is well-known internationally and instantly recognizable. Our brand has been a leading brand for over 130 years and still continues to grow because We are not constrained by traditional thinking but prefer to "think like a consumer" and take risks.

Team Benefits

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We are true believers of pay for performance principle which is why we continuously review our packages towards motivating our people to pursue excellence in their duties and drive business productivity.


PROFESSIONAL ADVANCEMENT


Promotion and salary advancement are determined by merit based on a fair, equitable, and transparent performance measurement process, and the employee’s capability to assume increased responsibilities through the internal recruitment process.


Managers regularly review employee performance to obtain the most effective use of their services and expertise. We actively encourage our employees to upgrade their skills and broaden their experience in different functional areas through training and career development opportunities by investing in employees learning and development program.

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

company.name: Ethiopian Engineering Corporation
company.description:
Ethiopian Engineering Corporation ( EEC) is transforming and diversifying from the current consultancy business operations. Taking advantage of the existing EEC strength and maximizing on the newly emerging external opportunities that are being prevalent with the shifts in Ethiopian Economic Policy – the Corporation is aiming to play a significant role to the success of the Ethiopian Construction Industry -by creating a vibrant business institution that will not only fill the gap that is in the current construction industry, but also replace the need for having international construction companies that are dominating the government mega scale projects.


EEC-Construction business unit key activities are high-end complex construction projects, predominately high-rise commercial and residential buildings, real-estate; infrastructure (roads, railways and airports) & water and energy sector construction. EEC-Construction alone would grow into a conglomerate of several business units including Piling, underground and foundation Works, Fit-Out, Energy (Solar Solutions), Electro- Mechanical Solution, Facility Management, Landscape and Construction Materials Production.


EEC-Construction is launched with the vision of being the best construction company in Ethiopia with a strategy of Timeously executing high-end complex projects, by utilizing proactive management skills as a Design and Build Contractor in order to achieve an optimum return and aspiring to be a competitive and preferred choice that can replace the current dependence on international contractors and deliver excellence. EEC Construction will uphold Courage, Integrity, Reliability, Value for its People and Innovation as its core values.

fields.title: Junior Cupping Officer
fields.description: Job Title: Junior Cupping Officer Department: Quality Control & Sensory Laboratory Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Reports To: Senior Cupping Officer / Quality Control Manager Position Summary The Junior Cupping Officer at Mullege Plc plays a vital role in protecting the company's stellar reputation for coffee quality. In this role, you will support the sensory lab team by preparing, testing, and documenting green and roasted coffee samples destined for international markets. This entry-level position demands high physical precision in lab setup, strict adherence to global specialty coffee protocols, and accurate data logging to ensure only premium-grade coffee is cleared for export. Key Responsibilities & Duties 1. Export Sample Processing & Setup Strict Sample Preparation: Receive incoming green coffee lot samples from washing stations, hulling mills, or suppliers, ensuring perfect identification and zero cross-contamination. Roasting & Grinding Calibration: Roast green coffee samples uniformly to exact standard profiles using laboratory sample roasters. Grind coffee precisely according to Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) protocol. Station Preparation: Set up sensory tables daily with strict portion controls, monitored water temperatures (around 93°C–95°C), specialized cupping spoons, and clean testing bowls. 2. Sensory Evaluation & Quality Assistance Sensory Assessment: Participate in daily cupping panels alongside Senior Cupping Officers to assess aroma, flavor notes, acidity, body, and uniformity. Defect Detection: Perform physical inspections on green coffee beans to count primary/secondary defects and check moisture levels before roasting. Export Grading Support: Assist in sorting and cataloging commercial vs. specialty coffee profiles (e.g., Sidamo, Yirgacheffe, Guji, Jimma) to align with client purchase contracts. 3. Data Management & Documentation Laboratory Logging: Enter physical measurements, moisture content readings, and initial cupping scores into Mullege Plc’s internal database or tracking spreadsheets. Traceability Tracking: Maintain flawless records linking sample numbers to their respective warehouse codes or lot numbers to guarantee total traceability from source to container.

company.name: Mullege PLC
company.description:
About Us


Mullege PLC is a prominent coffee exporter in Ethiopia, specializing in green Arabica coffee beans. With over three decades of experience, the company has grown from a small supplier to an internationally recognized exporter, serving clients on four continents. They operate two major plants in Addis Ababa and have a substantial annual production capacity and logistics operations. Additionally, Mullege maintains a state-of-the-art warehouse with a capacity to store over 5,000 tons of coffee. 


Our vision


Mullege's vision is to become an internationally recognized exporter of green coffee beans, driven by a strong foundation, innovative ideas, and dedication. Their mission is to provide the most refined coffee to coffee lovers globally through two processing plants in Addis Ababa and pulping stations across Ethiopia. They also aim to be a recognized freight service provider, as evidenced by their national recognition and significant revenue. 


Our success


Mullege's success story highlights its evolution from a small coffee supplier to a major exporter within three generations. Its commitment to quality control, efficient logistics, and a global reach is key to its success. Mullege has a substantial annual production capacity of 22,000 tons of coffee and a state-of-the-art warehouse. It also owns and operates a fleet of trucks for efficient coffee transportation.
