company.name: Teklehaimanot General Hospital
company.description:
About the company

Teklehaimanot General Hospital is a patient-centered private hospital in the center of Addis Ababa that provides trusted multi-disciplinary medical services. With a focus on quality and customer care, it has a distinctive, compassionate, and honest approach to serving the need of all patients. Devised with experienced and compassionate medical staff, TGH is a health coach and medical partner to cater to all medical care needs. “An earnest deed is worth more than silver and gold” so fairness in price, quality, and flexibility creates a shelter for hope and recovery.
Through decades of unwavering endeavor to be a patient-centered private hospital, TGH is proud to offer over 70 General, specialty, subspecialty, and supportive services with 402 dedicated staff, of which 329 are full-time employees and 73 are part-time and contractual employees equipped with a culture of medical teamwork. Its credit program serves over 100 companies, Local and international companies, sharing in the grandeur of full hospitality that builds lasting patient-to-care provider relationships. For seven consecutive years, TGH has been ranked “Green Level” general hospital.

Our Mission

  • To be among the premium and most preferred healthcare providers in East Africa

Our Vision

  • To provide quality health care services at a reasonable price 

Our Values

“To nurture all human beings principled in honesty through compassion with the utmost respect”
TGH, with a strong commitment to nurturing all human beings, upholds the principles of honesty, compassion, and utmost respect. Through its unwavering dedication to providing exceptional healthcare services, The Hospital strives to become a trusted institution, a place where patients find solace, comfort, and the promise of a brighter future.
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital the core value of “nurturing all human beings’’ resonates throughout every aspect of the organization. From the moment patients step through the doors, they are greeted with warmth and empathy. The hospital's dedicated team of healthcare and Customer service professionals understands the critical importance of treating patients not just as medical cases, but as individuals deserving of kindness, compassion, and personalized attention. Every patient is regarded as a unique story, and the hospital's mission is to provide holistic care that addresses both physical and emotional well-being.
“Honesty” is the bedrock upon which Teklehaimanot General Hospital stands. Transparent communication, ethical practices, and integrity are the guiding principles that shape every interaction within the hospital. Patients and their families can trust that they will receive accurate information about their conditions, treatment options, and the overall care process. The hospital's commitment to honesty ensures that patients are empowered to make informed decisions and actively participate in their healthcare journey.
“Compassion” is the lifeblood that flows through the veins of Teklehaimanot General Hospital. The hospital's healthcare professionals are not only highly skilled and knowledgeable but also deeply empathetic and understanding. They recognize that patients may be experiencing fear, pain, or uncertainty and go above and beyond to provide comfort and support. Whether it's holding a hand, offering a listening ear, or providing words of encouragement, the hospital's staff is devoted to fostering an environment that promotes healing and emotional well-being.
Above all, Teklehaimanot General Hospital treats every individual with “utmost respect”. Regardless of age, gender, socioeconomic status, or background, every patient is valued and treated with dignity. The hospital's commitment to respect extends to its commitment to cultural sensitivity and inclusivity. The diverse needs and beliefs of patients are honored, and efforts are made to create an environment that is welcoming and accommodating to all.

Why work for us

Choosing to work for Teklehaimanot General Hospital means joining a healthcare institution that values its employees, patients, and the community at large. We provide an environment that fosters professional growth, collaboration, and innovation, while emphasizing the importance of delivering exceptional patient care. With our commitment to excellence, cutting-edge facilities, and a supportive work culture, Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a fulfilling and rewarding career path for healthcare professionals seeking to make a difference.  The following facts highlight the numerous benefits and opportunities that await prospective candidates who choose TGH.
1. Commitment to Patient Care:
At Teklehaimanot General Hospital, our primary focus is on delivering high-quality patient care. Our employees are driven by a shared mission to make a positive impact on the lives of individuals and their families. By working with us, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the well-being of the community and play a crucial role in saving lives and improving health outcomes.
2. Collaborative and Supportive Work Environment:
We foster a collaborative and supportive work environment that encourages teamwork, communication, and professional growth. Our hospital values the contributions of each employee and believes in a culture of respect, inclusivity, and continuous learning. You will have the chance to work alongside skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds, creating a stimulating and enriching atmosphere that allows for personal and career development.
3. Opportunities for Professional Development:
We believe in investing in our employees' growth and development. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers a range of opportunities for professional advancement, including ongoing training programs, workshops, conferences, and mentorship initiatives. We encourage our employees to expand their knowledge and skills, fostering a culture of continuous professional development that supports career progression within the organization.
4. Competitive Compensation and Benefits:
We understand the importance of recognizing and rewarding our employees' hard work and dedication. Teklehaimanot General Hospital offers competitive compensation packages that are commensurate with industry standards, ensuring that employees feel valued and motivated. Additionally, we strictly adhere to privilege package that are stated on Ethiopian labor law.
5. Ethical and Transparent Practices:
As an organization, we prioritize ethical conduct and maintain transparency in our operations. Teklehaimanot General Hospital upholds the highest standards of integrity, ensuring that our employees work in an environment built on trust, honesty, and accountability. We are committed to maintaining a positive reputation and upholding the trust placed in us by our patients and the community.

Team Benefits

Teklehaimanot General Hospital has implemented a comprehensive range of employee benefits aimed at promoting employee well-being and job satisfaction. This write-up will explore the various employer benefits offered by Teklehaimanot General Hospital:
  • Partial medical coverage (including family)
  • Attractive Remuneration
  • Allowances (transportation, representation, and others)
  • Service charge
  • Successive training programs that are tailored to enrich professional, leadership and self-development skills of candidates.

fields.title: Logistics Manager
fields.description: Description of the position We are seeking a Logistics Manager for our Amhara region based in Motta with frequent travels to Lalibela. As such, the person implements the logistics strategy defined at country office level, organise the base’s logistics resources, ensure the proper application of Solidarités International’s policies, procedures and standards, and oversee the quality, performance and continuous improvement of the logistics services provided to operations. The person advise the Field Coordinator on all logistical issues at the base and acts as the functional link with the Logistics Department at the country office More details below: MANAGEMENT OF LOGISTICS ACTIVITIES Organises logistical resources to meet the base’s operational needs. Manages all logistics activities at the base in line with the guidelines set by the Logistics Department at the country office. Translates the country office’s logistics strategy into operational action plans tailored to the base’s context. Ensures that Solidarités International’s procedures and standards are properly applied. Identifies risks that may affect logistics operations and implements appropriate corrective measures. Contributes to the continuous improvement of logistics practices and processes. OPERATIONAL SUPPORT Advises the Field Coordinator and programme teams on all logistical issues at the field office. Ensures the availability of the logistical resources required to carry out operational activities. Coordinates project logistics planning in collaboration with the programme team. Contributes to the development of project proposals, budgets and donor reports on logistical aspects. Ensures the optimisation of logistical resources in support of operations. PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT Organises and supervises procurement activities at the field office. Ensures compliance with Solidarités International’s procedures and donors’ requirements. Approves procurement files falling within their level of delegated authority. Oversees market analysis, supplier monitoring and procurement timetables. Ensures the quality, compliance and traceability of procurement files. PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT Organises and supervises the receipt, storage, transport and distribution of goods. Ensures the availability of goods required for operations. Ensures that stock management and transport practices comply with requirements. Oversees stocktaking and ensures the reliability of logistics data. Ensures that procurement procedures are followed. MANAGEMENT OF LOGISTICS RESOURCES AND INFRASTRUCTURE Organises and supervises the management of the base’s vehicles, equipment and infrastructure. Ensures their availability, proper functioning and optimal use. Oversees preventive and corrective maintenance operations. Ensures the proper management of telecommunications equipment, IT assets, energy systems and other technical equipment. Ensures the compliance and safety of buildings, offices, accommodation, warehouses and other infrastructure. Ensures the proper delivery of the services necessary for the base’s operation. Identifies the need for renewal of the base’s equipment and infrastructure and monitors this process. PERFORMANCE, QUALITY AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT Monitors the base’s logistics performance indicators. Analyses the results and implements the necessary corrective actions. Ensures the quality and reliability of logistics data. Contributes to standardisation, knowledge management and continuous improvement initiatives. Proposes solutions aimed at improving the quality and efficiency of logistics services. RISK MANAGEMENT AND SECURITY Contributes to the implementation of the security strategy in relation to the technical and logistical aspects of the base. Ensures the availability of the logistical resources required for incident management. Ensures that procedures relating to safety-critical equipment are properly followed. Helps to identify logistical risks and implement mitigation measures. Contributes to security assessments and the base’s operational readiness. COORDINATION AND REPRESENTATION Represents Solidarités International in dealings with local authorities, service providers, partners and other stakeholders on logistical matters, as delegated by the Field Coordinator. Develops and maintains relationships with the base’s suppliers and partners. Contributes to local logistics coordination initiatives where relevant. BUDGET AND ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT Draws up and monitors the base’s logistics budget. Ensures the efficient use of financial resources allocated to logistics. Monitors logistics expenditure and proposes any necessary adjustments. Ensures the quality of the logistical information required for operational and financial reports. REPORTING Ensures the quality, reliability and completeness of the database’s logistics data. Produces and analyses the logistics indicators for the base. Provides reports to the Logistics Department of the country office and the Field Coordinator. Contributes to the consolidation of information and the sharing of best practice. MANAGEMENT Is responsible for the effective implementation of HR policies and processes to ensure that both the necessary number of staff and the required expertise are available for the activities for which they are responsible. Analyses, quantifies and assesses the human resources requirements of their team. Recruits and ensures the induction of the team under their supervision. Assesses the performance of team members, Trains and supports team members, Leads and facilitates communication within their team. Ensures the dissemination of best practice. INTERNAL CONTROL Is responsible for the conformity of the documents they produce FILING AND ARCHIVING Is responsible for filing and archiving the documents they produce in accordance with internal procedures FIGHT AGAINST ABUSE Creates and maintains a work environment that prevents inappropriate behaviour.# Participates in the promotion of SI's ethical framework. At any time, respects the protection of information exchanged within the framework of an abuse notification and its treatment Implements abuse risk mitigation measures PARTNERSHIPS May contribute, in line with their role and responsibilities, to the verification of SI's implementation partners. May contribute to the implementation of a plan to support and strengthen SI's partners.May participate in the control requirements for partners' actions in line with their role and responsibilities. This list is not exhaustive and other related tasks (within the scope of their role) may be assigned at the request of their line manager.

company.name: Solidarités International
company.description:
Who are we ?

The NGO Solidarités International assists populations affected by conflicts and violence, epidemics, natural or climate-related disasters and economic collapse. Our humanitarian teams are committed to helping people whose lives, health and security are threatened, by meeting their most vital needs: food, water, shelter and hygiene. Our mandate is to respond to crises by distributing emergency aid in person and, in parallel, by implementing long-term solutions that enable affected populations to regain sustainable access to water, sanitation, hygiene, diversified livelihoods and safe housing.

Solidarités International is registered in Ethiopia in December 2022 and is aiming at developing emergency programs in true collaboration with the beneficiary communities and local stakeholders.

Our mandate and value

Solidarités International commitment to assist populations affected by the most severe crises dates back to 1980. We always provide aid at the request of the affected population or its representatives, in cooperation with our local partners. Our field teams mainly comprise locally hired staff, to help ensure that the aid provided fits the population’s needs as closely as possible. We are fiercely determined to constantly uphold the humanitarian principles of humanity, independence, impartiality and neutrality. Solidarités International also demonstrates unique technical and social engineering capabilities, which we continue to perfect by building on the innovations and development efforts of our teams and partners.

Find out more about our history explained here.

Why work for us ?

In 2022, our 2,641 staff members worked relentlessly to achieve our collective goal: to provide assistance for people affected by conflicts, violence, epidemics, natural and climate-related disasters and economic collapse in the countries where we work.

As part of its global strategy, Solidarités International is committed to

  • Further develop the professionalism of its human resources;
  • Support and value the diversity of our staff and their experience;
  • Set up conditions that fosters our team’s commitment.

Our teams have always been our NGO’s greatest strength. They share the values that guide our humanitarian action and enable our organization to fulfil its mandate: courage, integrity, professionalism, team spirit and unfailing commitment.

Working conditions

In Solidarités International, we prioritize not only making a meaningful impact in the world but also in your career. Joining our team means:

  • Competitive Compensation: we offer competitive compensation packages firmly rooted in the local job market, ensuring fair compensation.
  • Advanced Social Support: Our benefits include health coverage, maternity and paternity leave and a range of other benefits.
  • Career Advancement: Experience real growth opportunities within our organization.
  • Inclusivity and Fairness: We nurture a culture that values equality, transparency, and the recognition of individual contributions.
  • Transparent HR Policies: Our open HR management policies ensure each decisions’ are justified and communicated to all.
  • Safe Work Environment: Our staff’s security is our prime concern.
  • Zero Tolerance for SEAH: We maintain a strict stance against any type of abuse – all act of exploitation, abuse and/or sexual harassment (SEAH).

In Solidarités International, we're committed to improving the world and providing a fulfilling and evolving career for our dedicated team." You are neither anonymous nor interchangeable: neither is Solidarités International!

Solidarités International is an equitable employer committed to find all forms of discrimination. SI will ever ask for any remuneration to take part in a recruitment process.

company.name: Solidarités International
company.description:
Who are we ?

The NGO Solidarités International assists populations affected by conflicts and violence, epidemics, natural or climate-related disasters and economic collapse. Our humanitarian teams are committed to helping people whose lives, health and security are threatened, by meeting their most vital needs: food, water, shelter and hygiene. Our mandate is to respond to crises by distributing emergency aid in person and, in parallel, by implementing long-term solutions that enable affected populations to regain sustainable access to water, sanitation, hygiene, diversified livelihoods and safe housing.

Solidarités International is registered in Ethiopia in December 2022 and is aiming at developing emergency programs in true collaboration with the beneficiary communities and local stakeholders.

Our mandate and value

Solidarités International commitment to assist populations affected by the most severe crises dates back to 1980. We always provide aid at the request of the affected population or its representatives, in cooperation with our local partners. Our field teams mainly comprise locally hired staff, to help ensure that the aid provided fits the population’s needs as closely as possible. We are fiercely determined to constantly uphold the humanitarian principles of humanity, independence, impartiality and neutrality. Solidarités International also demonstrates unique technical and social engineering capabilities, which we continue to perfect by building on the innovations and development efforts of our teams and partners.

Find out more about our history explained here.

Why work for us ?

In 2022, our 2,641 staff members worked relentlessly to achieve our collective goal: to provide assistance for people affected by conflicts, violence, epidemics, natural and climate-related disasters and economic collapse in the countries where we work.

As part of its global strategy, Solidarités International is committed to

  • Further develop the professionalism of its human resources;
  • Support and value the diversity of our staff and their experience;
  • Set up conditions that fosters our team’s commitment.

Our teams have always been our NGO’s greatest strength. They share the values that guide our humanitarian action and enable our organization to fulfil its mandate: courage, integrity, professionalism, team spirit and unfailing commitment.

Working conditions

In Solidarités International, we prioritize not only making a meaningful impact in the world but also in your career. Joining our team means:

  • Competitive Compensation: we offer competitive compensation packages firmly rooted in the local job market, ensuring fair compensation.
  • Advanced Social Support: Our benefits include health coverage, maternity and paternity leave and a range of other benefits.
  • Career Advancement: Experience real growth opportunities within our organization.
  • Inclusivity and Fairness: We nurture a culture that values equality, transparency, and the recognition of individual contributions.
  • Transparent HR Policies: Our open HR management policies ensure each decisions’ are justified and communicated to all.
  • Safe Work Environment: Our staff’s security is our prime concern.
  • Zero Tolerance for SEAH: We maintain a strict stance against any type of abuse – all act of exploitation, abuse and/or sexual harassment (SEAH).

In Solidarités International, we're committed to improving the world and providing a fulfilling and evolving career for our dedicated team." You are neither anonymous nor interchangeable: neither is Solidarités International!

Solidarités International is an equitable employer committed to find all forms of discrimination. SI will ever ask for any remuneration to take part in a recruitment process.

The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments. The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services. The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities. Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. B. Community Mobilization and Engagement Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions. Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities. Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities. Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children. Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions. Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate. C. Protection Identification and Referral Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns. Provide information on available services and support options. Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways. Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements. Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required. Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures. D. Support to Community Protection Mechanisms Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures. Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors. Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns. fields.title: Junior Contract Engineer (Site Based)
fields.description: Ascend Consulting Engineers Plc is an Ethiopian consulting engineering firm based in Addis Ababa. The firm specializes in construction contract administration, claims management and dispute resolution. We advise Employers, Contractors and Consultants on contracts governed by the FIDIC Conditions of Contract and by the Ethiopian public procurement, conditions and we represent clients in Dispute Review Expert, Dispute Board and arbitration proceedings. Our portfolio covers road, bridge, building, aviation and industrial park projects across Ethiopia. We work in small, senior teams. Every member is expected to take direct responsibility for the files placed in their hands. To meet a growing workload, the firm invites applications from qualified professionals for the following positions. Position 3: Junior Contract Engineer (Site Based) Number required: One (1) Duty Station: Project site, as assigned Minimum Experience: 2 years Education: BSc in Civil Engineering/COTM Employment type: Full time, subject to a probation period Purpose of the Position: The site based Junior Contract Engineer is the eyes of the firm on the project. The holder secures the contemporary records on which every claim depends, serves notices in time, keeps the head office informed of events as they happen rather than after they have passed, and prepares the draft claim report for each claim event arising on the project. Main Duties and Responsibilities: Collect, organize and safeguard contemporary records, including site diaries, daily labour and equipment returns, weather records, delivery records, survey data, test results and photographs with dates. Monitor site events that may give rise to a claim, and report them to the head office immediately so that notices are served within the time allowed by the contract. Draft site correspondence, requests for information, confirmations of verbal instructions and notices for review by the Contract Engineer. Maintain registers of instructions, variation orders, drawings, notices, correspondence and claims for the project. Follow up joint measurement, quantity records and interim payment certificates, and record any deduction or dispute. Track actual progress against the accepted programme and record the causes of any delay or disruption. Prepare the draft claim report for each claim event arising on the project. Attend site meetings, take reliable notes and check the minutes issued by others for accuracy. Coordinate with the contractor's site management and with the Engineer's staff on contractual matters, within the limits set by the head office. Terms of Employment: Salary is negotiable and will be fixed according to qualification, experience and the outcome of the interview. Benefits and allowances are provided in accordance with the firm's personnel policy. Appointment is subject to a probation period in accordance with the Ethiopian Labour Proclamation.

company.name: Transsion Manufacturing PLC
company.description:
TRANSSION MANUFACTURING PLC.

Background

Transsion Holdings is a manufacturer of mobile phones based in Shenzhen, China. It was the largest smartphone manufacturer by sales in Africa in 2017, and also sells mobile phones in South Asia. Its brands include phone brands, Itel and Infinix after-sales service brand Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. It manufactures phones in China, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Bangladesh and recently at India.

Transsion Holdings Pvt. Ltd was founded as Transsion Technology in Hong Kong in 2006, with a focus on the development, manufacturing, sales, and services of mobile communication products. Transsion entered the African market with its Tecno and Itel brands, and started focusing on the African market in July 2008, initially with feature phones Transsion released its first smartphone in 2014.Transsion set up its Nigerian subsidiary in June 2008, and had subsidiaries in seven countries in Africa by October that year. Transsion set up a manufacturing plant in Ethiopia in 2011. Transsion entered the Indian market in 2016. The market share of Transsion's smartphone brands in Africa combined surpassed that of Samsung in 2017, making Transsion the largest manufacturer of smartphones for the African market in the fourth quarter of 2017.Transsion was also the largest manufacturer of mobile phones in Africa in the first half of 2017.Transsion's 2018 attempt at a reverse takeover failed. In October 2018, Transsion Holdings started producing smartphones in their new manufacturing plant in Bangladesh.Transsion Holdings became a public listed company in September 2019 by listing on the STAR Market section of the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

Operations

Transsion sells mobile phones in Africa and South Asia. It operates mobile phone brands Tecno, Itel, and Infinix, as well as after-sales support service Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. Spice Digital, an Indian phone brand, was acquired in 2017. Transsion manufactures its phones in China, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan. Transsion was the first non-African mobile phone company to set up an after-sales support network in Africa.Transsion's success in the African market has been attributed to tailoring its phones' features to the needs of the African market. Transsion's phones offer a featurethat calibrates camera exposures for darker skin tones, allowing face details to be retained. Transsion developed phones with dual SIM functionality, which were well received because African users commonly used more than one SIM card at a time save money. Transsion released phones with long battery life, which are suited to low electrification rates in Africa and the propensity of blackouts. The phones included support for multiple African languages, and Tecno was the first major mobile phone brand in Ethiopia to include support for an Amharic keyboard. Transsion heavily advertises its mobile phone brands in Africa.

Vision

To become the most popular provider of smart devices and mobile services for

consumers in global emerging markets

Mission

To improve the lives of as many people as possible through technology and

innovation

CORE VALUES

·      Customer

Customers are both the starting point and the end point for all work of TRANSSIONers

·      Respect

Respect defines how we treat each other and our differences.

·      Openness

Staying open connects us to the future and its possibilities.

·      Innovation

Innovation is essential to achieving breakthroughs on different levels, both

personal and organizational.

·      Sharing

Sharing invites every “I” to become “we”.

·      Bottom line

We always show compassion, even if it puts us at a disadvantage.

fields.title: Protection Officer
fields.description: Medical Teams Calling Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world. Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes. JOB SUMMARY Protection Officer Response contributes to the calling of Medical Teams by implementing response activities which include case management, psychosocial support, safe space activity, and another related project. The position holder will train and supervise social workers and community activists in Refugee camps & host Communities to prevent and respond to GBV issues. This includes providing ongoing training and mentorship for community workers, and community activists, developing a weekly, monthly, and quarterly work plan, and utilizing monitoring and evaluation systems to ensure high-quality services, smooth communication, collaboration, and coordination among partners from the protection, health, legal, and psychosocial sectors committed to reducing the incidence of violence against women. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Prepare and develop weekly and monthly work plans for GBV-related prevention activities, ensuring alignment with the overall program objectives. Implement GBV prevention and response activities, including fieldwork and community-based programs, ensuring that activities are in line with GBV IASC guidelines and best practices. Process and maintain accurate case documentation, including case histories, assessments, interventions, and progress reports, ensuring all information complies with confidentiality standards. Apply protection principles such as confidentiality, safety, and non-discrimination in all program activities, ensuring that GBV survivors are treated with respect and dignity. Prepare outreach materials and awareness campaigns tailored to local communities, ensuring that the information is relevant and culturally appropriate. Implement community-based interventions in partnership with relevant stakeholders such as women and children’s affairs, teachers, medical providers, and law enforcement. Process referrals to appropriate service providers for GBV survivors, ensuring that their needs are met, and all required documentation is provided. Apply the necessary legal frameworks to all protection activities, ensuring that the rights of survivors are upheld in accordance with national laws and international standards. Prepare regular reports, including weekly updates, case progress reports, and activity summaries for submission to the Protection Manager and field coordinator. Implement and support the delivery of capacity-building initiatives for community workers and partners, ensuring effective coordination in response to GBV incidents. Process requests for protection of supplies and services, ensuring adherence to the logistical and financial policies of the organization. Apply best practices in the integration of GBV response activities into health, education, and legal services to ensure holistic support for survivors. Prepare documentation and reports for submission to relevant authorities as required, ensuring that the information complies with legal standards and confidentiality of policies. Implement any other duties assigned by the Protection Manager or senior leadership to support the effective delivery of the GBV program. Support the integration of accountability practices into program activities by following established procedures during planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting. Help ensure that accountability is reflected in day-to-day tasks, team interactions, and when working with partners or communities. Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation & Abuse, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding. Other Duties Maintain a clean and safe working environment, disposing of waste and sharps appropriately. Other duties as assigned Utilize volunteers when appropriate.

fields.title: CCTV System Supply and Installation ToR for Digital Horizon Project partner Schools
fields.description: Introduction and Background SOS Children’s Villages in Ethiopia, a member association of SOS Children’s Villages International, was established in response to the 1973 famine. Since its inception, the organization has been committed to supporting children who have lost parental care or are at risk of losing it through childcare, protection, family strengthening, education, and health services. In addition, SOS Children’s Villages in Ethiopia provides humanitarian assistance to communities affected by conflict, drought, and other emergencies, with a particular focus on vulnerable women and children. The organization currently operates across eight regional states, namely Tigray, Addis Ababa, Amhara, Harari, Oromia, Sidama, South Ethiopia, Southwest Ethiopia, and Somali. As part of its commitment to improving educational quality and promoting digital transformation in schools, SOS Children’s Villages in Ethiopia is implementing the Digital Horizon (DH) Project in the Tigray Region. The project aims to strengthen teaching, learning, and school administration through the integration of digital technologies in selected schools. By expanding access to ICT infrastructure, digital learning resources, and data-driven management practices, the initiative seeks to create a modern, inclusive, and technology-enabled educational environment. To support this goal, digital centers and classrooms are being established to provide students and teachers with access to modern computing facilities, internet connectivity, and innovative digital tools that enhance learning outcomes and foster digital literacy. A key component of this initiative is the establishment of digital centers within targeted schools. These centers aim to provide students and teachers with access to modern ICT infrastructure, digital learning tools, and internet-enabled educational resources. To ensure the safety and security of these digital centers, the implementation of a CCTV surveillance system is a critical component of the project. Therefore, the primary objective of this document is to define the requirements and scope for securing the digital centers in the targeted schools through the design, installation, and operation of an effective surveillance system. Objective s The overall objective is to design, supply, installation and maintenance of a CCTV surveillance system. This system will be deployed to secure the digital centers in targeted schools, ensuring the protection of ICT infrastructure, safeguarding students and staff, and supporting the continuity of digital learning initiatives. Scope of Work shops The supplier has the following scopes, but is not limited to the following tasks: The installation of the CCTV surveillance system will be carried out in selected digital centers across targeted schools in Tigray. The coverage is limited to digital rooms only and does not extend to the entire school premises. The specific locations and number of schools are Mekelle: 3 schools, Kola -Temben: 1 school, Samre: 2 schools, Adwa: 1 school, and Axum: 4 schools. Conduct a detailed survey of each digital center to determine optimal camera placement. Design High level diagram which shows Equipment installation and position of the equipment in each school. Prepare a comprehensive CCTV system design, specifying the number of cameras, type, resolution, storage, and network requirements. Assess the existing LAN and rack suitability for CCTV equipment, or recommend procurement of a new rack, and supply all required hardware. Install and configure the CCTV system according to the approved design, ensuring proper cable management, labeling, and compliance with safety standards. Incorporate cloud or alternative data backup mechanisms in the design and ensure indoor and outdoor cameras support night detection. Integrate the CCTV system with existing ICT infrastructure where applicable, and conduct full functionality testing for live monitoring, recording, playback, and remote access. Provide system calibration and troubleshooting to ensure optimal performance, and train designated project and school staff on operation, maintenance, and basic troubleshooting, supported by user manuals and documentation. Offer a warranty for system components and installation, along with technical support and maintenance services under agreed terms. Technical Specifications The CCTV surveillance system shall meet the following minimum technical requirements: o Cameras: High-resolution IP/HD cameras suitable for both indoor and outdoor environments. Feature Indoor Camera (Minimum) Outdoor Camera (Minimum) Resolution 1080p HD or Above 1080p HD or above Sensor 1/3” CMOS 1/2.8” CMOS Lens 3-9 mm varifocal 2.8-12 mm / 8-32 mm varifocal Low-light capability 0.1 Lux (B/W), 0.6 Lux (Color) IR night vision, 30m+ Weatherproofing Not required IP66/IP67 Durability Standard indoor casing IK10 vandal-resistant Standards CE/UL/BIS, ONVIF CE/UL/BIS, ONVIF Power PoE support PoE support Estimated number of cameras per school: RNo. School Name Location Camera Camera 1 Alumuni Secondary School Axum 4 4 2 Kaleb Secondary School Axum 4 4 3 Kedamawi Minilik Secondary School Axum 4 4 4 Axum Secondary School Axum 4 4 5 Nigiste Saba (No. 2) Secondary School Adwa 4 4 6 Guya Secondary School Kola Temben 3 3 7 Fire sweat preparatory & secondary school Samre 3 4 8 Samre Secondary School 2 Samre 4 4 9 Alene Secondary School Mekelle 4 4 10 Messebo Secondary School Mekelle 4 4 11 SOS School Mekelle 12 14 Storage: Capacity to store continuous recordings for a minimum of 30 days based on the total number of cameras installed. Monitoring: Centralized or remote monitoring capabilities, with secure access controls. Display: Full HD monitors with size 55 inches. Network: Integration with existing school ICT networks or deployment of a standalone secure network where required. Power: Integrate with reliable power supply with backup solutions to ensure uninterrupted operation All materials, accessories, and components used in the installation and implementation must meet current standard technological features and comply with standard quality benchmarks. This includes basic AI functions such as human detection and motion detection. N.B: Any missing items, accessories, or components required for the full functionality of the surveillance system, even if not explicitly listed in the specifications, shall be the responsibility of the vendor to supply and install at no additional cost. Role and Responsibility SOSCVE Provide access to facilities for site surveys, installation, and maintenance. Coordinate with school staff to facilitate smooth implementation. Oversee project execution and ensure alignment with school security objectives. Monitor installation progress and verify adherence to technical requirements. The project technical team will conduct regular site inspections to verify compliance with technical specifications and timelines. Performance of the CCTV system will be monitored against agreed benchmarks, including recording quality, storage capacity, and system uptime. Provide feedback and guidance to ensure system performance meets operational needs. Support schools in evaluating the effectiveness of the CCTV system post-installation. Service provider/Vendor Need assessment to identify the number of cameras, and other ICT devices necessary for effective delivery. The vendor must provide clear, complete, and itemized specifications for all materials, devices, and equipment to be supplied. Design, supply, install, test, and maintain the CCTV system in accordance with the approved specifications. Ensure compliance with safety standards and best practices. The vendor must ensure that all staff adhere strictly to the SOS CV’s safeguarding standards and code of conduct during the execution of the contract. Any misconduct or breach of the safeguarding policy of the organization by any staff member of the vendor shall be the sole responsibility of the vendor. The vendor will be held fully accountable for such actions, including disciplinary measures, and any corrective actions. All installations and configurations must be carried out in line with recognized professional standards. Deliver training, documentation, and warranty/maintenance support Deliverable The vendor shall deliver the following deliverables: Site survey and CCTV system design document. High level diagram which shows the design and equipment of installation. Timeline & Deliverables Schedules. Clear and detailed device specifications. Detail information on CCTV hardware and software to be included. User training sessions and operational manual. Warranty and maintenance support plan. Timeline The project is expected to be completed within the following timeframe: Site survey and design: 1 week Procurement and delivery of equipment: 4 weeks Installation and Testing: 3 weeks Training and handover: 1 week

fields.title: Senior International Banking Officer
fields.description: Ext/Vaca/055/2026 The Senior International Banking Officer is responsible for implementing the Bank's foreign currency (FCY) mobilization and international banking initiatives by conducting business analysis, monitoring performance, supporting districts and branches, identifying new business opportunities, promoting FCY products and services, and maintaining relationships with key FCY customers and institutions. The role prepares reports, action plans, and recommendations; coordinates with internal and external stakeholders; and submits findings to the manager to support informed decision-making and achievement of the bank's international banking objectives.

company.name: Ahadu Bank S.C
company.description:
Why work for us?


By joining us, you'll help empower Ethiopians through our pioneering cutting-edge financial services. Join our passionate team, driven by purpose, integrity, and a desire to make a real difference. We offer a dynamic environment, opportunities for growth, and the chance to be part of something revolutionary. Embrace your purpose and build a fulfilling career. This is your chance to shape the future of Ethiopian finance.


Employee Benefits

  • Competitive salary and benefits package
  • Medical Coverage
  • Salary Advance Loan
  • Consumer Loan
  • Mortgage and Vehicle Acquisition Loan.



The Company

Established by visionary entrepreneurs and professionals, Ahadu Bank provides a different model of banking centered on the philosophy of Inclusive Intermediation.

Founded by over 10,000 shareholders and incorporated under the Ethiopian Banking Business Proclamation, Ahadu Bank offers full-fledged commercial banking services. The Bank is domiciled in Ethiopia with its Head Office located on Africa Avenue, Sunshine Building, Addis Ababa.

Ahadu Bank completed the National Bank of Ethiopia's (NBE) initial capital requirement on January 2, 2021, and received its banking license on October 5, 2021. On June 29, 2022, the bank received authorization from the NBE to begin operations and officially opened its doors on July 16, 2022.

According to a June 2024 report, the bank now boasts over 100 branches and a workforce exceeding 900 employees nationwide.


Mission

Pioneer avant-garde financial services for promoting the economic welfare of Ethiopians.


Vision

Take a lead role in the financial sector, in 2025 E.C, in support of the aspirations of the citizenry and the country.


Core values

  1. Fear of God
  2. Passion for Serving
  3. Honesty
  4. Organizational Learning
  5. Proactive Accountability
  6. Humaneness


Our way

We strive to drive the development of Ethiopia's financial services to benefit Ethiopians in a sustainable and inclusive way. We strive to have a positive socio-economic impact in every aspect of our business. We believe that addressing the needs of the unbanked and underbanked by reaching out to rural communities, supporting and nurturing small businesses, practicing responsible banking principles, and investing in innovative technology to digitize our operations helps us create value for our customers, shareholders, and the broader community.


Culture

At Ahadu Bank, our culture thrives on a unique blend of purpose and progress. We're driven by a deep desire to make a positive impact, evident in our core values of social responsibility and financial empowerment for all Ethiopians. We're a passionate team, working together to pioneer cutting-edge financial solutions. Our commitment to innovation goes hand-in-hand with integrity, ensuring we operate with honesty and ethical practices. We believe in fostering a growth mindset, embracing "Organizational Learning" to continuously develop ourselves and each other. This collaborative spirit is core to our success, as we build a supportive and dynamic environment where everyone can thrive. If you're looking to make a real difference and be part of something revolutionary, Ahadu Bank is the place for you.

fields.title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Development of a Training Curriculum: "Budgeting for Equity: A Practical Guide for Addis Ababa"
fields.description: 1. Background The Center for Budgetary Governance Advocacy (CBGA) is a local civil society organization based in Addis Ababa working on fiscal transparency and gender-responsive budgeting. Under its project “Advancing Gender Equity and Transparency in Budgetary Governance in Addis Ababa,” funded by Christian Aid/EU CSF+, CBGA works with sub-city administrations, sector offices and partner civil society organizations to strengthen gender-responsive and transparent budget practices in Addis Ababa. 1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Community-Based Social Work

  • Establish and maintain constructive relationships with community members and community structures.
  • Identify protection and social concerns affecting individuals, families, and communities.
  • Support communities to identify their own protection priorities and solutions.
  • Promote participation of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Provide appropriate basic social support within the scope of professional competence.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

B.   Community Mobilization and Engagement

  • Mobilize and engage communities in project interventions.
  • Support community structures to participate effectively in protection activities.
  • Facilitate community dialogue and awareness activities.
  • Work with community and religious leaders to promote positive attitudes and practices that protect women, girls, and children.
  • Promote community ownership and sustainability of protection interventions.
  • Ensure community engagement is inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and culturally appropriate.

C.   Protection Identification and Referral

  • Identify individuals and groups experiencing or at risk of protection concerns.
  • Provide information on available services and support options.
  • Facilitate safe and appropriate referrals through established referral pathways.
  • Follow up on referrals when appropriate and in accordance with confidentiality and consent requirements.
  • Coordinate with service providers and relevant authorities as required.
  • Immediately report serious protection and safeguarding concerns through established procedures.

D.   Support to Community Protection Mechanisms

  • Support the Protection Officer in strengthening community protection structures.
  • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to community-based protection actors.
  • Support community structures to identify and address protection concerns.

  • Document community concerns, actions, and feedback and share relevant information with the Protection Officer.

E.   Support to Women and Girls Safe Space

  • Support the safe and effective functioning of the WGSS.
  • Promote safe access and participation of women and girls.
  • Provide information and basic social support within the scope of the role.
  • Support linkages between WGSS users and appropriate specialized services.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, accessibility, and respect.
  • Identify operational or protection concerns affecting women and girls and report them to the Protection Officer.

F.    Community Prevention and Social Support

  • Support community initiatives aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate discussions that promote positive social norms and protective behaviors.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally identified protection solutions.
  • Encourage positive family and community support systems.
  • Provide appropriate information and awareness on available protection and social services.

G.  Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Provide regular updates to the Protection Officer.
  • Support collection of project monitoring information and community feedback.
  • Document referrals and follow-up actions in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible.
  • Ensure all records are safely stored and protected.

H. Safeguarding and Accountability

  • Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members.
  • Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns.

company.name: Transsion Manufacturing PLC
company.description:
TRANSSION MANUFACTURING PLC.

Background

Transsion Holdings is a manufacturer of mobile phones based in Shenzhen, China. It was the largest smartphone manufacturer by sales in Africa in 2017, and also sells mobile phones in South Asia. Its brands include phone brands, Itel and Infinix after-sales service brand Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. It manufactures phones in China, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Bangladesh and recently at India.

Transsion Holdings Pvt. Ltd was founded as Transsion Technology in Hong Kong in 2006, with a focus on the development, manufacturing, sales, and services of mobile communication products. Transsion entered the African market with its Tecno and Itel brands, and started focusing on the African market in July 2008, initially with feature phones Transsion released its first smartphone in 2014.Transsion set up its Nigerian subsidiary in June 2008, and had subsidiaries in seven countries in Africa by October that year. Transsion set up a manufacturing plant in Ethiopia in 2011. Transsion entered the Indian market in 2016. The market share of Transsion's smartphone brands in Africa combined surpassed that of Samsung in 2017, making Transsion the largest manufacturer of smartphones for the African market in the fourth quarter of 2017.Transsion was also the largest manufacturer of mobile phones in Africa in the first half of 2017.Transsion's 2018 attempt at a reverse takeover failed. In October 2018, Transsion Holdings started producing smartphones in their new manufacturing plant in Bangladesh.Transsion Holdings became a public listed company in September 2019 by listing on the STAR Market section of the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

Operations

Transsion sells mobile phones in Africa and South Asia. It operates mobile phone brands Tecno, Itel, and Infinix, as well as after-sales support service Carlcare and accessories brand Oraimo. Spice Digital, an Indian phone brand, was acquired in 2017. Transsion manufactures its phones in China, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan. Transsion was the first non-African mobile phone company to set up an after-sales support network in Africa.Transsion's success in the African market has been attributed to tailoring its phones' features to the needs of the African market. Transsion's phones offer a featurethat calibrates camera exposures for darker skin tones, allowing face details to be retained. Transsion developed phones with dual SIM functionality, which were well received because African users commonly used more than one SIM card at a time save money. Transsion released phones with long battery life, which are suited to low electrification rates in Africa and the propensity of blackouts. The phones included support for multiple African languages, and Tecno was the first major mobile phone brand in Ethiopia to include support for an Amharic keyboard. Transsion heavily advertises its mobile phone brands in Africa.

Vision

To become the most popular provider of smart devices and mobile services for

consumers in global emerging markets

Mission

To improve the lives of as many people as possible through technology and

innovation

CORE VALUES

·      Customer

Customers are both the starting point and the end point for all work of TRANSSIONers

·      Respect

Respect defines how we treat each other and our differences.

·      Openness

Staying open connects us to the future and its possibilities.

·      Innovation

Innovation is essential to achieving breakthroughs on different levels, both

personal and organizational.

·      Sharing

Sharing invites every “I” to become “we”.

·      Bottom line

We always show compassion, even if it puts us at a disadvantage.

Job Description 

Position: Talent Development Specialist


Department

Human Resources

Reports To

HR Manager

Location

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Employment Type

Full-time

About the Role

We are looking for a Learning & Talent Development Specialist to lead the design, delivery, and evaluation of organization-wide learning initiatives — and to own our Management Trainee (MT) Program from end to end.
In this role, you will build a culture of continuous learning, develop future leaders, and ensure our people have the skills and capabilities to drive Transsion's growth across emerging markets.
You will collaborate closely with department heads, HR Business Partners, external trainers, and university partners to deliver impactful learning experiences at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Learning & Development

  • Conduct Training Needs Assessments (TNA) across all departments and country offices.
  • Develop and execute the annual Learning & Development plan aligned with business strategy.
  • Design training curricula, presentations, manuals, and blended learning materials (classroom + digital).
  • Organize and coordinate internal and external training programs, including e-learning initiatives.
  • Deliver training sessions on company policies, soft skills, leadership, and professional development.
  • Develop and maintain the annual training calendar and ensure timely execution.
  • Monitor employee participation and maintain accurate training records in the LMS/HRIS.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness through assessments, surveys, Kirkpatrick-level metrics, and performance data.
  • Manage the training budget and optimize resource allocation for maximum ROI.
  • Promote a culture of continuous learning through internal campaigns, learning platforms, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

Management Trainee (MT) Program

  • Develop and manage the annual MT recruitment plan in alignment with workforce and succession needs.
  • Partner with department heads to identify future leadership and specialist talent requirements.
  • Support employer branding at universities, career fairs, and graduate recruitment events.
  • Coordinate end-to-end MT candidate sourcing, assessments, interviews, and selection.
  • Design and continuously improve the MT curriculum, rotation plans, and development roadmap.
  • Coordinate structured onboarding and orientation for each MT cohort.
  • Assign mentors and coaches; monitor mentoring quality and progress.
  • Track trainee performance, learning milestones, and competency development against defined benchmarks.
  • Organize leadership workshops, business simulations, case studies, and cross-functional project assignments.
  • Prepare progress reports and presentations for HR leadership and senior management.
  • Measure MT program effectiveness and ROI; recommend improvements each cycle.
  • Recommend confirmation, promotion, extension, or reassignment based on performance reviews.
  • Maintain a talent pipeline and succession plan for future leadership positions.
  • Build and sustain partnerships with universities and educational institutions to attract top graduates.

Key Performance Indicators


KPI

Target

Annual training coverage rate

≥ 90% of employees

Training satisfaction score

≥ 4.2 / 5.0

MT program retention rate

≥ 80% through completion

MT post-program placement rate

≥ 70% in target roles within 6 months

Training budget utilization

Within ±10% of approved budget

fields.title: Chief Solution Architect and Interoperability Lead
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Role purpose Own the future-state technical architecture and ensure that ForLab+ and related components integrate securely and sustainably with Ethiopia’s national digital-health ecosystem, authoritative registries and existing transactional systems. Key responsibilities · Assess current applications, infrastructure, registries, standards, data flows, interfaces, ownership and technical debt relevant to the supply chain. · Define the target architecture, integration patterns, data contracts, security model, deployment model and phased transition roadmap. · Ensure authoritative use of the Master Facility Registry, National Product Catalog and other approved registries without creation of competing internal sources of truth. · Design interoperability with logistics, warehouse, enterprise-resource, cold-chain, service-delivery and health-information systems as prioritized. · Set engineering standards for APIs, messaging, identity and access, auditability, offline synchronization, observability, testing and documentation. · Lead architecture reviews, technical risk decisions, integration testing, performance testing, security assurance and release readiness. · Ensure traceable transformation from source transactions to integrated datasets, alerts and downstream analytics. · Design for intermittent connectivity, realistic support capacity, open standards, maintainability and reasonable recurrent costs. · Develop technical documentation, source-code and configuration custody arrangements, administrator training and government handover plans. Expected results · A stakeholder-approved current-state assessment and future-state architecture. · Secure, documented and tested integrations with prioritized national systems and registries. · A production-ready platform with observable performance, auditable data flows and reliable offline operation where required. · Government technical teams able to administer, support and evolve the deployed solution.

The Chief Nursing Officer is responsible for the overall leadership, management, coordination, supervision, and continuous improvement of nursing services at Landmark General Hospital. The CNO ensures that nursing care is safe, ethical, evidence-based, patient-centered, efficient, and compliant with applicable Ethiopian laws, professional requirements, hospital policies, WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF) standards, and applicable hospital accreditation standards.

The CNO shall serve as a key nursing leader for implementation and monitoring of the WHO Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Framework (PSFHF).

Responsibilities include:

  • 1. Ensure nursing services comply with applicable PSFHF requirements.
  • 2. Promote a strong patient-safety culture throughout nursing services.
  • 3. Ensure safe, evidence-based nursing practices are consistently implemented.
  • 4. Monitor nursing compliance with patient identification, medication safety, infection prevention, falls prevention, pressure injury prevention, safe handover, documentation, and other patient-safety practices.

  • Maintain appropriate evidence and records demonstrating nursing compliance with PSFHF requirements. WHO's PSFHF specifically addresses leadership and management, patient and public involvement, safe evidence-based clinical practices, safe environments, and lifelong learning; these areas should therefore be reflected in the CNO's accountability.

C. Accreditation and Quality Improvement

The CNO shall be a key responsible person for ensuring nursing readiness for and compliance with hospital accreditation requirements. Responsibilities include:

  • Ensure nursing services comply with applicable national and international accreditation standards adopted by Landmark General Hospital.
  • Participate in hospital accreditation planning, implementation, internal assessment, corrective action, and follow-up activities.
  • Coordinate with the Quality and Safety Department to identify nursing-related accreditation gaps.
  • Develop and implement corrective and preventive action plans for identified nursing deficiencies.

D. Nursing Quality and Performance Monitoring

  • Establish and monitor nursing quality indicators and key performance indicators.
  • Monitor patient outcomes and nursing-sensitive indicators.
  • Conduct or facilitate regular nursing audits.
  • Review nursing documentation and patient-care records.
  • Monitor compliance with nursing standards, protocols, and clinical guidelines.
  • Identify trends, risks, and performance gaps and initiate improvement actions.
  • Present nursing quality and performance reports to hospital management.
  • Develop quality-improvement projects based on identified nursing and patient-safety

problems.

Nursing Management Rounds

  • Establish a structured nursing management-round schedule.
  • Conduct regular rounds with nursing heads and supervisors.

Assess:

  • Patient safety
  • Emergency preparedness

  • Nursing documentation
  • Patient identification
  • Medication administration practices

  • Promote continuing professional development.

  • Ensure evidence-based nursing care is provided.
  • Promote respect for patient rights, dignity, privacy, confidentiality, and informed participation.
  • Ensure appropriate nursing assessment, care planning, implementation, evaluation, and documentation.
  • Promote effective communication and safe clinical handover.
  • Ensure timely escalation of deteriorating patients.
  • Promote multidisciplinary collaboration.
  • Monitor patient and family satisfaction with nursing services.

Risk Management and Incident Management

1. Identify nursing-related clinical and operational risks.

2. Ensure timely reporting and escalation of incidents.

3. Participate in root-cause analysis and other incident-review processes.

4. Implement corrective and preventive actions.

5. Monitor recurring incidents and develop strategies to prevent recurrence.

6. Ensure lessons learned from incidents are communicated to nursing staff.

J. Staffing and Resource Management

1. Develop nursing staffing plans according to patient volume, acuity, and service

requirements.

2. Ensure appropriate nurse-to-patient allocation.

3. Monitor overtime, absenteeism, turnover, and staffing shortages.

4. Participate in recruitment and selection of nursing personnel.

5. Recommend staffing adjustments based on service needs.

4. Maintain accreditation and PSFHF-related nursing evidence.

5. Ensure nursing records are available and organized for internal and external assessment.

6. Ensure nursing data are used for quality improvement and management decisions.

The CNO has authority to:

 Direct and supervise nursing services.

 Assign and reassign nursing personnel according to service needs.

company.name: Ahadu Bank S.C
company.description:
Why work for us?


By joining us, you'll help empower Ethiopians through our pioneering cutting-edge financial services. Join our passionate team, driven by purpose, integrity, and a desire to make a real difference. We offer a dynamic environment, opportunities for growth, and the chance to be part of something revolutionary. Embrace your purpose and build a fulfilling career. This is your chance to shape the future of Ethiopian finance.


Employee Benefits

  • Competitive salary and benefits package
  • Medical Coverage
  • Salary Advance Loan
  • Consumer Loan
  • Mortgage and Vehicle Acquisition Loan.



The Company

Established by visionary entrepreneurs and professionals, Ahadu Bank provides a different model of banking centered on the philosophy of Inclusive Intermediation.

Founded by over 10,000 shareholders and incorporated under the Ethiopian Banking Business Proclamation, Ahadu Bank offers full-fledged commercial banking services. The Bank is domiciled in Ethiopia with its Head Office located on Africa Avenue, Sunshine Building, Addis Ababa.

Ahadu Bank completed the National Bank of Ethiopia's (NBE) initial capital requirement on January 2, 2021, and received its banking license on October 5, 2021. On June 29, 2022, the bank received authorization from the NBE to begin operations and officially opened its doors on July 16, 2022.

According to a June 2024 report, the bank now boasts over 100 branches and a workforce exceeding 900 employees nationwide.


Mission

Pioneer avant-garde financial services for promoting the economic welfare of Ethiopians.


Vision

Take a lead role in the financial sector, in 2025 E.C, in support of the aspirations of the citizenry and the country.


Core values

  1. Fear of God
  2. Passion for Serving
  3. Honesty
  4. Organizational Learning
  5. Proactive Accountability
  6. Humaneness


Our way

We strive to drive the development of Ethiopia's financial services to benefit Ethiopians in a sustainable and inclusive way. We strive to have a positive socio-economic impact in every aspect of our business. We believe that addressing the needs of the unbanked and underbanked by reaching out to rural communities, supporting and nurturing small businesses, practicing responsible banking principles, and investing in innovative technology to digitize our operations helps us create value for our customers, shareholders, and the broader community.


Culture

At Ahadu Bank, our culture thrives on a unique blend of purpose and progress. We're driven by a deep desire to make a positive impact, evident in our core values of social responsibility and financial empowerment for all Ethiopians. We're a passionate team, working together to pioneer cutting-edge financial solutions. Our commitment to innovation goes hand-in-hand with integrity, ensuring we operate with honesty and ethical practices. We believe in fostering a growth mindset, embracing "Organizational Learning" to continuously develop ourselves and each other. This collaborative spirit is core to our success, as we build a supportive and dynamic environment where everyone can thrive. If you're looking to make a real difference and be part of something revolutionary, Ahadu Bank is the place for you.
