This role plays a critical leadership function in driving AI-enabled automation, enterprise system integration, and digital productivity solutions across the Group’s multi-sector operations including manufacturing, export, trading, logistics, and agriculture. The position ensures the development and delivery of scalable, secure, and integrated enterprise solutions that support end-to-end business processes by connecting ERP systems, digital applications, mobile platforms, data analytics, and workflow automation tools. The incumbent will lead the development of AI-enabled automation, paperless business processes, and digital platforms that improve operational efficiency, reduce manual work, and enable data driven decision making across Kerchanshe Group. This role is also responsible for ensuring seamless integration across enterprise platforms, enabling a unified ecosystem where ERP, business applications, analytics systems, and digital platforms operate as a single integrated enterprise solution. Main Duties and Responsibilities Digital Solution Strategy and Innovation Develop and implement a solution development strategy that supports Kerchanshe Group’s digital transformation roadmap. Lead initiatives focused on automation, AI-driven solutions, paperless operations, and enterprise productivity platforms. Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through digital innovation and process automation. Promote adoption of emerging technologies such as AI, workflow automation, low-code platforms, and intelligent analytics solutions. Enterprise Application and Solution Development Lead the design, development, and deployment of enterprise digital solutions that support business operations across the corporate group. Ensure applications support end-to-end business process automation and enterprise productivity. Oversee the development of internal systems, digital platforms, mobile applications, and workflow automation tools. Ensure all developed solutions align with enterprise architecture and digital governance standards. Enterprise Systems Integration Lead the development of integration frameworks connecting ERP systems with other enterprise platforms including business applications, data platforms, and external services. Ensure seamless data flow across systems to create a unified digital ecosystem across the organization. Develop and manage API-based integrations, middleware services, and automation pipelines. Support the creation of “one integrated enterprise platform” where ERP acts as the core system integrated with all supporting applications. AI, Automation, and Paperless Operations Lead initiatives that promote AI adoption and intelligent automation across business processes. Drive the transition toward paperless operations by implementing digital workflows and document automation solutions. Implement solutions for business process automation, robotic process automation (RPA), and digital document management systems. Develop tools that enhance decision-making through AI-assisted analytics and predictive insights. Solution Architecture and Technology Governance Establish standards for enterprise solution architecture, system scalability, and secure development practices. Ensure solutions follow best practices in system design, integration architecture, data governance, and security frameworks. Maintain strong alignment between technology solutions and business strategy. Oversee system performance, maintainability, and long-term scalability of enterprise applications. Team Leadership and Capacity Development Lead and mentor a team of software developers, application engineers, and digital solution specialists. Build internal capability in modern development frameworks, AI tools, and enterprise solution engineering. Encourage a culture of innovation, experimentation, and continuous learning. Ensure efficient allocation of development resources across digital transformation projects. Business Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement Work closely with business units to identify opportunities for process optimization and automation. Translate operational requirements into scalable and integrated digital solutions. Support senior leadership in implementing enterprise productivity and digital transformation initiatives. About the company

As the largest producer and exporter of coffee in Ethiopia, Kerchanshe Trading has a proud history of providing quality coffees to the local and international markets. Founded on the principles of bringing fairness and transparency to the coffee value chain while satisfying customer demand, Kerchanshe is also a company with heart and vision.

Kerchanshe specializes in coffees sourced from Yirgacheffe, Lekempti, Gimbi, Djimma, and Sidamo, names that epitomise fine Arabica coffee. Since its inception 15 years ago, Kerchanshe has established a track record of fair trading and excellent customer service, and now employs over 1,250 permanent staff and 10,000 seasonal staff. Directly and indirectly, it impacts the livelihoods of over 1 million coffee growers throughout the southern and south-western coffee-cultivating regions of Ethiopia.

The passion for fine coffee is coupled with consistent reinvestment not only in improved infrastructure, technology and processes, but Kerchanshe also invests 10% of its annual profits into social responsibility programs such as building schools and providing clean water to the communities it serves

OUR VISION

To be the leader in innovation and quality among coffee producers and exporters while caring for the environment.

OUR MISSION

We are committed to providing the finest high-quality coffee beans to our customers worldwide while forging mutually beneficial relationships with the community and the environment that we live in.

QUALITY POLICY

At Kerchanshe we are highly conscious of the fact that the quality of our beans is what sets us apart.

 

Our Mission

"We are driven to deliver unparalleled quality coffee beans to discerning customers worldwide, fostering enduring relationships with both our communities and the natural world."

Our Vision

"To pioneer innovation and excellence within the global coffee industry while nurturing a profound respect for environmental preservation."

Our Values

Ethical Integrity: We steadfastly adhere to the highest ethical standards in all our dealings, prioritizing integrity and accountability.

Sustainable Practices: We embrace sustainable methodologies that seamlessly integrate with the environment, ensuring responsible stewardship of our resources.

Customer-Centric Excellence: Our unwavering commitment to consistency, integrity, and excellence ensures unparalleled service and satisfaction for our customers.

Empowered Workforce: We empower and champion our diverse workforce, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous growth.

Community Enrichment: We are deeply committed to giving back to our communities through meaningful engagement and impactful initiatives, embodying our ethos of corporate citizenship.

Why work for us

Embark on a fulfilling journey with Kerchanshe Group, where you'll discover more than just a job. Join us for stimulating career opportunities, personalized work schedules that accommodate your lifestyle, a vibrant and inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and innovation, and comprehensive compensation and benefits packages designed to enhance your overall satisfaction and well-being.

In addition to these offerings, you'll have access to ongoing professional development and training programs to further hone your skills and expand your expertise. Furthermore, at Kerchanshe, we prioritize work-life balance, providing resources and support to help you thrive both personally and professionally.

Join our community at Kerchanshe Group, where your individuality is celebrated, your growth is nurtured, and your contributions make a meaningful impact. Together, let's build a brighter future for ourselves and our communities.

Team Benefits

At Kerchanshe Group, we prioritize the welfare and satisfaction of our employees by providing a suite of professional benefits tailored to enhance their work experience. Our comprehensive offerings include:

  • Subsidized canteen services at both headquarters and coffee washing stations/farms
  • Dedicated employee transportation services
  • Annual employee recognition program, celebrating outstanding contributions
  • Provision of vehicles with fuel for executive management
  • These benefits underscore our commitment to cultivating a supportive and rewarding environment, where employee well-being and professional growth are paramount.

As the largest producer and exporter of coffee in Ethiopia, Kerchanshe Trading has a proud history of providing quality coffees to the local and international markets. Kerchanshe specializes in coffees sourced from Yirgacheffe, Lekempti, Gimbi, Djimma, and Sidamo, names that epitomise fine Arabica coffee. Since its inception 15 years ago, Kerchanshe has established a track record of fair trading and excellent customer service, and now employs over 1,250 permanent staff and 10,000 seasonal staff. Directly and indirectly, it impacts the livelihoods of over 1 million coffee growers throughout the southern and south-western coffee-cultivating regions of Ethiopia.

fields.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning and Data Quality Lead
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Role purpose Build a credible measurement, evaluation and learning system that distinguishes implementation outputs from real operational outcomes and provides decision makers with timely evidence on what works, for whom, under what conditions and at what cost. Key responsibilities · Develop the theory of change, results framework, indicator reference sheets, learning agenda and evaluation questions. · Define baselines, targets, denominators, data sources, disaggregation, collection frequency and accountability for each indicator. · Design a feasible evaluation approach that strengthens attribution through comparison, phased rollout, interrupted time series or other appropriate methods. · Measure system use, transaction completeness, latency, inventory accuracy, stock availability, stockout duration, wastage, alert closure and decision response. · Establish routine data-quality assurance, reconciliation, verification and audit procedures across source and integrated systems. · Ensure ethical, secure and documented management of evaluation and operational data. · Work with implementation teams to create rapid learning cycles while maintaining independence in outcome assessment. · Manage baseline, periodic review and end-line activities, including evaluation subawards or consultants. · Communicate findings honestly, including null results, implementation limitations, unintended effects and remaining evidence gaps. Expected results · An approved, auditable measurement and evaluation plan with credible baselines and targets. · Regular data-quality and implementation-performance findings used for course correction. · A defensible pilot evaluation that separates deployment claims from verified operational effects. · A learning package that informs scale-up, cost, sustainability and future investment decisions.

raw_payload.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning and Data Quality Lead
raw_payload.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Role purpose

Build a credible measurement, evaluation and learning system that distinguishes implementation outputs from real operational outcomes and provides decision makers with timely evidence on what works, for whom, under what conditions and at what cost.

Key responsibilities

· Develop the theory of change, results framework, indicator reference sheets, learning agenda and evaluation questions.

· Define baselines, targets, denominators, data sources, disaggregation, collection frequency and accountability for each indicator.

· Design a feasible evaluation approach that strengthens attribution through comparison, phased rollout, interrupted time series or other appropriate methods.

· Measure system use, transaction completeness, latency, inventory accuracy, stock availability, stockout duration, wastage, alert closure and decision response.

· Establish routine data-quality assurance, reconciliation, verification and audit procedures across source and integrated systems.

· Ensure ethical, secure and documented management of evaluation and operational data.

· Work with implementation teams to create rapid learning cycles while maintaining independence in outcome assessment.

· Manage baseline, periodic review and end-line activities, including evaluation subawards or consultants.

· Communicate findings honestly, including null results, implementation limitations, unintended effects and remaining evidence gaps.

Expected results

· An approved, auditable measurement and evaluation plan with credible baselines and targets.

· Regular data-quality and implementation-performance findings used for course correction.

· A defensible pilot evaluation that separates deployment claims from verified operational effects.

· A learning package that informs scale-up, cost, sustainability and future investment decisions.

company.name: Solidarités International
company.description:
Who are we ?

The NGO Solidarités International assists populations affected by conflicts and violence, epidemics, natural or climate-related disasters and economic collapse. Our humanitarian teams are committed to helping people whose lives, health and security are threatened, by meeting their most vital needs: food, water, shelter and hygiene. Our mandate is to respond to crises by distributing emergency aid in person and, in parallel, by implementing long-term solutions that enable affected populations to regain sustainable access to water, sanitation, hygiene, diversified livelihoods and safe housing.

Solidarités International is registered in Ethiopia in December 2022 and is aiming at developing emergency programs in true collaboration with the beneficiary communities and local stakeholders.

Our mandate and value

Solidarités International commitment to assist populations affected by the most severe crises dates back to 1980. fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead Role purpose Build and sustain the government co-leadership, governance, accountability and institutional arrangements required for the program to operate within Ethiopia’s health system and continue beyond external implementation support. Key responsibilities · Develop and maintain a stakeholder and political-economy map covering national agencies, lead executive offices, programs, regional authorities and implementation partners. · Establish and facilitate steering, technical working group and operational review mechanisms with documented mandates and decision rights. · Coordinate with the Ministry of Health, EPI, RMNCH, digital-health and planning functions, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA and regional health bureaus. · Translate technical proposals into institutionally feasible roles, policies, SOPs, accountability mechanisms and approval pathways. · Embed government counterparts in assessment, product prioritization, architecture, implementation, evaluation and transition decisions. · Lead capacity-transfer plans covering product ownership, system administration, data governance, support, supervision and performance management. · Track institutional commitments, policy decisions, unresolved ownership issues and readiness for transfer. · Coordinate sustainability and recurrent-cost planning with relevant institutions and development partners. · Identify duplication, mandate conflicts and partner dependencies and facilitate resolution through agreed governance channels. Expected results · Functional governance bodies with documented decisions and consistent participation. · Clear institutional ownership of systems, data, integrations, support and performance-review processes. · Approved SOPs, accountability arrangements and transition milestones. · Government counterparts able to perform progressively larger shares of operational functions.

raw_payload.title: Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead
raw_payload.description:
About Opian

Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them.

Our philosophy

We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.

Government Partnership and Institutionalization Lead


Role purpose

Build and sustain the government co-leadership, governance, accountability and institutional arrangements required for the program to operate within Ethiopia’s health system and continue beyond external implementation support.

Key responsibilities

· Develop and maintain a stakeholder and political-economy map covering national agencies, lead executive offices, programs, regional authorities and implementation partners.

· Establish and facilitate steering, technical working group and operational review mechanisms with documented mandates and decision rights.

· Coordinate with the Ministry of Health, EPI, RMNCH, digital-health and planning functions, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA and regional health bureaus.

· Translate technical proposals into institutionally feasible roles, policies, SOPs, accountability mechanisms and approval pathways.

· Embed government counterparts in assessment, product prioritization, architecture, implementation, evaluation and transition decisions.

· Lead capacity-transfer plans covering product ownership, system administration, data governance, support, supervision and performance management.

· Track institutional commitments, policy decisions, unresolved ownership issues and readiness for transfer.

· Coordinate sustainability and recurrent-cost planning with relevant institutions and development partners.

· Identify duplication, mandate conflicts and partner dependencies and facilitate resolution through agreed governance channels.

Expected results

· Functional governance bodies with documented decisions and consistent participation.

· Clear institutional ownership of systems, data, integrations, support and performance-review processes.

· Approved SOPs, accountability arrangements and transition milestones.

· Government counterparts able to perform progressively larger shares of operational functions.

Developing leadership for a world of hope

The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable. The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles. Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms. Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality. Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark

Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda)

Duration: 12 months

Report To: Project Coordinator

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable.

The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Protection Programme Coordination

  • Lead the day-to-day implementation of protection activities in the assigned woreda.
  • Translate project plans and objectives into practical woreda-level implementation plans.
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved plans, budgets, quality standards, and timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with the Project Coordinator on progress, priorities, challenges, and required actions.
  • Provide technical supervision and guidance to the Social Worker.
  • Maintain effective coordination with relevant government offices, community structures, religious leaders, and other stakeholders.
  • Represent the project in relevant woreda-level coordination forums and meetings.
  • Identify protection risks, operational challenges, and emerging needs and recommend appropriate responses.

B.   Community-Based Protection and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming.
  • Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms.
  • Facilitate meaningful engagement of community leaders, religious leaders, local authorities, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other relevant groups.
  • Promote community-led identification and prioritization of protection concerns and solutions.
  • Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems.
  • Promote locally appropriate prevention and response mechanisms for protection concerns.

C.   Protection Risk Identification and Referral

  • Monitor protection risks and trends within the assigned woreda.
  • Ensure appropriate identification and referral of individuals requiring specialized protection and other essential services.
  • Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways.
  • Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services.
  • Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms.

D.   Community Engagement and Prevention

  • Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers.
  • Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally owned solutions to identified protection concerns.
  • Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

E.   Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls.
  • Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services.
  • Monitor the quality and accessibility of services provided through the WGSS.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, and informed choice for women and girls accessing services.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS.

F.    Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting

  • Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards.
  • Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information.
  • Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning.
  • Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially.

G.  Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards.
  • Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups.
  • Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks.
  • Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Immediately report safeguarding, PSEA, and serious protection concerns through established organizational procedures.

H.  Financial and Resource Management

  • Support efficient use of project resources at woreda level.
  • Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures.
  • Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps.
  • Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.

Sales Agents will work across both the property acquisition and buyer-facing sides of the sales process , from prospecting property owners and building our property inventory to qualifying buyers, conducting property tours, managing negotiations, and supporting transactions through closing. The ideal candidate will be confident, persistent, client-focused, and comfortable working in a target-driven environment that requires both active prospecting and strong relationship management . This role involves significant field work, client interaction, follow-up, negotiation, and the use of digital tools and CRM systems. Build and maintain a strong pipeline of property owners, buyers, and sales opportunities. Conduct listing presentations, explain RE/MAX services, and secure signed listing agreements. Qualify buyers by understanding their property requirements, budget, financing status, priorities, and purchase timeline. Match qualified buyers with suitable properties based on their needs and preferences. Verify properties through physical inspection and collect accurate property information, owner identification, title documents, photos, and other required documentation. Ensure properties are accurately presented with complete information, appropriate pricing, professional visual assets, and updated listing status. Coordinate with marketing and back-office teams to ensure properties are prepared and published effectively. Arrange and conduct property tours and walkthroughs for prospective buyers. Lead and support negotiations between buyers and sellers, including offers, counteroffers, and deal coordination. Prepare offers and support transactions through the closing process. Collaborate closely with other Sales Agents to communicate property availability, buyer requirements, viewing schedules, pricing changes, seller requirements, and negotiation updates. Coordinate with Finance, Legal, Operations, and Marketing teams to facilitate smooth transaction progression. Maintain accurate CRM records, activity logs, follow-up schedules, client information, and sales pipeline updates. Deliver a professional and transparent client experience from initial contact through listing, property viewing, negotiation, and transaction completion. Represent the RE/MAX brand professionally and consistently in all client and market interactions. What We Are Looking For We are looking for confident, driven, persistent, and client-focused individuals who are comfortable with active sales and field work. You should be willing to prospect for new business, make cold calls, meet clients in the field, follow up consistently, and work toward clear sales objectives. The ideal candidate should be able to build trust with both property owners and buyers, handle objections, negotiate effectively, and maintain strong relationships throughout the sales process. You should also be comfortable learning and using digital tools, WhatsApp, and CRM systems to manage your clients and sales activities. Key Competencies Prospecting & Lead Generation: Confidence in cold outreach, field prospecting, and developing new sales opportunities. Relationship Management: Ability to build trust, understand client needs, and maintain strong client relationships. Negotiation & Closing: Ability to handle objections, negotiate effectively, and move opportunities toward successful transactions. Persistence & Follow-Up: Strong discipline, resilience, and commitment to following up with prospects and managing an active sales pipeline. Professionalism & Accountability: Commitment to ethical sales practices, transparency, accurate record keeping, professional client interaction, and strong representation of the RE/MAX brand.

About the Lutheran World Federation (LWF)

We are a global communion of churches in the Lutheran tradition, living and working together for a just, peaceful, and reconciled world. LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in over 20 countries. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world.

Lutheran World Federation (LWF) in Ethiopia  

LWF World Service Ethiopia is a registered foreign charity, which has been operating in Ethiopia since 1973 implementing various development and humanitarian projects in different parts of Ethiopia. LWF World Service Ethiopia works closely with the Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus (EECMY), the Ethiopian Government, UN organizations and other funding partners. Its thematic areas include the promotion of food security and sustainable livelihood, sustainable natural resources management, emergency preparedness, response and rehabilitation, and capacity building. 

A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and in order to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures.

LWF Safeguarding Commitment

LWF World Service is committed to creating and maintaining a safe organization where people we come in contact with are protected from harm and abuse. Harm and abuse may include but are not limited to physical, psychological, and sexual violence and abuse, financial and material abuse, all forms of modern slavery, and all forms of maltreatment and exploitation.

We are a global communion of churches in the Lutheran tradition, living and working together for a just, peaceful, and reconciled world. LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in over 20 countries. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world.

Lutheran World Federation (LWF) in Ethiopia  

LWF World Service Ethiopia is a registered foreign charity, which has been operating in Ethiopia since 1973 implementing various development and humanitarian projects in different parts of Ethiopia. LWF World Service Ethiopia works closely with the Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus (EECMY), the Ethiopian Government, UN organizations and other funding partners. Its thematic areas include the promotion of food security and sustainable livelihood, sustainable natural resources management, emergency preparedness, response and rehabilitation, and capacity building. 

A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and in order to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures.

LWF Safeguarding Commitment

LWF World Service is committed to creating and maintaining a safe organization where people we come in contact with are protected from harm and abuse. Harm and abuse may include but are not limited to physical, psychological, and sexual violence and abuse, financial and material abuse, all forms of modern slavery, and all forms of maltreatment and exploitation.

INVITATION FOR BIDS

Selection of a Travel Agent for the Provision of Air Ticketing Services for HRNS-Ethiopia

1. Introduction

HRNS-Ethiopia (HANNS R. NEUMANN STIFTUNG) is an international non-governmental organization implementing development programs across multiple field offices in Ethiopia. To ensure continued value for money, transparency, and quality of service, HRNS-Ethiopia invites qualified and experienced travel agencies to submit proposals for the provision of comprehensive domestic and international air ticketing services for its staff, consultants, partners, and other eligible travellers.

2. About the Organization

HRNS-Ethiopia works to support sustainable development programs and is committed to sound procurement practices. The organization requires the services of a qualified, independent, and reputable travel agency to manage its air travel needs efficiently and cost-effectively.

3. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of this assignment is to select a qualified travel agent capable of providing full and comprehensive air ticketing services (local and international flights) at the lowest available cost, with reliable, timely, and professional service delivery to eligible travellers of HRNS-Ethiopia and its affiliates.

4. Scope of Work

The selected travel agent will be responsible for providing comprehensive air ticketing services. Key responsibilities include:

  • Advising on airfares promptly.
  • Processing and sending flight reservations upon request.
  • Delivering airline tickets within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt of the Client's Travel Authorization.
  • Issuing and sending invoices promptly for reconciliation.
  • Handling reconfirmation, revalidation, and re-issuing of tickets affected by changes.
  • Providing timely notifications of airport closures, cancellations, or flight delays.
  • Negotiating the lowest possible airfares.
  • Facilitating special meal requests, seat assignments, and frequent flyer programme registration.
  • Applying any discounts offered by airlines to the Client.
  • Designating a key contact person for emergency and after-hours support.

Detailed technical and functional specifications are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR)

Application Deadline

All proposals must be submitted no later than August 24, 2026, at 4:00 PM local time, to the HRNS-Ethiopia country office at the following address:

HRNS-Ethiopia
Bole Sub City, Woreda 06, House Number 289/12

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

fields.title: Head of Procurement & Supply Chain Management
fields.description: Compensation & Benefits Basic Salary: ETB 75,000 Housing Allowance (HA): ETB 11,000 Additional benefits will be communicated to shortlisted candidates. About the Opportunity A leading organization in the manufacturing and industrial sector is seeking an experienced and strategic Head of Procurement & Supply Chain Management to lead and optimize its end-to-end procurement, logistics, inventory, and supply chain operations. This is a senior leadership role responsible for driving cost efficiency, supplier performance, operational excellence, and supply chain resilience across the business. The successful candidate will work closely with executive leadership to develop procurement strategies, strengthen supplier partnerships, improve inventory and logistics performance, and build a high-performing procurement and supply chain function. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute procurement and supply chain strategies aligned with business objectives. Lead sourcing, supplier selection, contract negotiation, and vendor relationship management. Oversee logistics, transportation, warehousing, and distribution operations to ensure efficiency and cost optimization. Implement inventory control systems that improve availability while minimizing excess stock and working capital. Ensure compliance with procurement regulations, customs requirements, and internal governance standards. Identify and mitigate supply chain risks through proactive planning and supplier management. Prepare and manage procurement and logistics budgets and deliver measurable cost-saving initiatives. Lead, mentor, and develop procurement, logistics, and warehouse teams. Collaborate with Finance, Operations, and Production to align procurement and supply chain plans with operational requirements. Drive process improvement initiatives, including ERP, procurement, and warehouse management system optimization. Monitor procurement and logistics KPIs and use data-driven insights to improve performance and decision-making.

fields.title: Project Accountant
fields.description: Main Duties & Responsibilities of the Position Holder: He/She shall: Ensure that the overall Supervision of the project Financial Activities are properly performed and follows up that the daily routines are carried out smoothly. Assist the Team Leader in all aspects of administrative actions. See to it that adequate stock of supplies are requested on time and maintained in accordance with the policy of LWF. Operate and maintain the project’s Accounts according to LWF-ET procedures. Participate in the preparation of annual/ Working Budget of the project jointly with the program staff. Prepare monthly Fund Request together with the program staff based on the planned activity for the period. Make sure that the monthly fund request is for the activities planned for that period only. Make sure that the finance part of the Quarterly Monitoring Report (QMR) of the project tally the Narrative part of the report Collect the monthly financial report of the project from head office finance every month and should discuss with the concerned project staff Code all disbursements & receipts according to LWF/ET procedure. Make sure that all disbursements are summarized according to the cost centers and account codes. Ensure that LWF Procurement Procedures are followed and relevant financial documents, such as purchase requisitions, proforma invoice, purchase order, and Goods receiving Notes are properly raised. Prepares and checks Financial Statements before they are sent to the Head Office every month and to reach Head Office before five days of the next month. It includes cash count balance. Prepare monthly bank reconciliation statements. Supervise the Store Keepers and see to it that the purchase storing and issuing of goods are processed strictly in accordance with LWF procedures. Make sure that all project Fixed Assets are registered properly in accordance with LWF procedures. Control and Assist the Secretary/Cashier in all financial matters. Prepare monthly Payroll/ Pay Sheet for Casual workers if any, based on the approved attendance and other relevant documents in consultation with the Team Leader . Together with the Team Leader , He is Answerable for all Purchases and Disbursements in regard to budgetary provisions and stipulations. Make sure that all necessary and appropriate taxes like 2% or 30% With Hold tax (WHT), Income taxes, pension contributions are deducted and paid to the concerned offices of government on time. Make sure that all disbursements are in accordance with LWF financial procedures. Make sure that all disbursements are not out of the Budget Allocated for each line items As a responsible head for accounts and personnel administration of the project, he makes surprise cash count & staff supervision, and reports to the Team Leader . Where the Accountant is not convinced about certain payments or payment procedures authorized by the Team Leader , he should explain his/her concerns. But if still there is disagreement, the accountant should refer to the Finance Manager at head office for advice. Follow procedure as outlined in LWF World Service Ethiopia Staff Rules, Collective Agreement and other Operation Manuals; Perform any other duties as assigned to him by the Team Leader or his designate. This Job Description may be revised by the LWF/WS- Ethiopia at any time as it deems necessary

fields.title: MMS Market Shaping Strategy Consultant
fields.description: Activity Duration 6 months Duty Station Addis Ababa, with travel to regions as required Reporting To CEO, YADAM Foundation, and Programmed Team Working With YADAM team and stakeholders Contract Type Consultancy service agreement (output/deliverable-based) Date August 7 2026 BACKGROUND YADAM Foundation implements a nutrition advocacy and technical assistance program with UNICEF Ethiopia, supporting the national transition of maternal antenatal supplementation from Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) to Multiple Micronutrient Supplements (MMS), in line with WHO's updated antenatal care guidance. company.name: Hope Enterprise’s University College
company.description:
Hope Enterprises or Hope is a local NGO that was established in 1971 in Addis Ababa to help the needy help themselves through basic needs, education, competence, job and business mediation and value education. As Hope was completing its 32 years of humanitarian service in 2003, it’s then Executive Director, Dr. Minas Hiruy, recommended to the Board the establishment of an outstanding liberal arts university college by submitting a full-fledged proposal. After some discussion, the Board and the General Assembly of Hope accepted the proposal, establishing Hope University College as the first public benefits institution of higher learning in the country on November 25, 2003.  Soon after, the Board adopted a new structure comprising the Ladders of Hope that subsumed the existing and non-college activities of Hope as one division and Hope University College as another division, opening the way for the university college to operate autonomously.
 

Values

The University College believes in goodwill to humankind and to nature and in the concretization of this concern as a step to making the world a community of hope, justice, peace and progress. The University College holds dear the advancement of liberal education as a means of personal and social transformation and regards the provision of education to all as an important public responsibility.

Vision

The vision of the University College is to contribute to the renewal and transformation of society through knowledge and value based education and graduates who can make a difference using what they had gained in the university college.

Mission

The University College, having a mission to provide aspiring leaders the option of pursuing world-class education without leaving their country and cultural setting, shall enable the development of leaders, who being capable of independent work, problem solving, analysis, innovation and reflection, can make a difference in the development of society and in mutually and sustainably supportive relations between man and nature.

Mission Statement

Developing leadership for a world of hope

fields.description: Invitation to Bid Consultancy Services for Salary Scale, Salary Range Assessment and Employee Benefits Review Introduction Three Roots International (TRI) invites qualified and eligible consulting firms or consultants to submit Technical and Financial Proposals for the provision of consultancy services to conduct a comprehensive salary scale, salary range, allowance & accommodation, and employee benefits review. TRI is an international nonprofit organization registered by the Authority for Civil Society Organizations (ACSO) under Registration No. 4931. TRI's mission is to cultivate community development and economic capacity by empowering families through education, health, and income-generating activities. Since its establishment, TRI has worked in partnership with rural communities to reduce extreme poverty through programs implemented in Ethiopia, particularly in the Bishoftu area. The consultancy is intended to review the organization's current salary and benefits structure and recommend a competitive, equitable, and financially sustainable compensation framework based on market benchmarking and job evaluation. This assignment aims to ensure that the organization's remuneration structure remains aligned with labor market conditions, organizational strategy, and best human resource management practices. The Terms of Reference (TOR) contained in this document provide the detailed background, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, consultant qualifications, proposal submission requirements, evaluation criteria, reporting arrangements, payment schedule, and other conditions governing this consultancy assignment. Background Three Roots International (TRI) is committed to maintaining a fair, transparent, competitive, and sustainable compensation and benefits system that supports the attraction, motivation, and retention of qualified employees. To ensure that the organization's remuneration structure remains aligned with labor market conditions, organizational strategy, and best human resource management practices, the organization seeks to engage a qualified consultant to undertake a comprehensive salary scale, salary range, and employee benefits assessment. 2. Purpose of the Assignment The overall purpose of this consultancy is to review the organization's current salary and benefits structure and recommend a competitive, equitable, and financially sustainable compensation framework based on market benchmarking and job evaluation. 3. Objectives The consultant shall: ● Review the existing salary structure, grading system, and employee benefits. ● Conduct a salary benchmarking study against comparable organizations in the sector. ● Assess internal equity and external competitiveness of current salaries. ● Review the organization's employee benefits package and recommend improvements. ● Develop an updated salary grading structure with corresponding salary ranges. ● Recommend policies and implementation strategies for the revised compensation system. 4. Scope of Work The consultant will undertake, but not be limited to the following tasks: A. Inception Phase ● Hold inception meetings with management. ● Review organizational policies, HR manuals, job descriptions, salary scales, and related documents. ● Develop an inception report detailing the methodology, work plan, and timeline. B. Job Analysis and Evaluation ● Review existing job descriptions. ● Conduct job evaluation using an appropriate methodology. ● Assess internal job hierarchy and grading. C. Market Salary Survey ● Identify relevant comparator organizations. ● Conduct salary and benefits benchmarking. ● Analyze market compensation trends. D. Salary Structure Review ● Assess the current salary grading system. ● Develop appropriate salary bands/ranges for each grade. ● Recommend salary progression mechanisms. ● Propose salary adjustment scenarios based on affordability. E. Employee Benefits Assessment Review all employee benefits including, where applicable: ● Medical insurance ● Pension and retirement benefits ● Leave entitlements ● Housing benefits ● Transport allowance ● Communication allowance ● Per diem and travel benefits ● Insurance coverage ● Performance incentives ● Other employee welfare programs Provide recommendations for improving the competitiveness and sustainability of the benefits package. F. Implementation Plan Develop an implementation roadmap including: ● Cost implications ● Phased implementation options ● Risk assessment ● Change management recommendations 5. Deliverables The consultant shall provide: Inception Report. Salary and Benefits Benchmarking Report. Job Evaluation Report. Draft Salary Scale and Salary Range Structure. Draft Employee Benefits Review Report. Final Compensation and Benefits Report incorporating stakeholder feedback. Presentation of findings and recommendations to management. 6. Duration of the Assignment The consultancy is expected to be completed within 6–8 weeks from the date of contract signing. Methodology The consultant is expected to apply an appropriate methodology, including: ● Document review ● Interviews with management and staff ● Job evaluation ● Salary market survey ● Benchmarking analysis ● Data analysis ● Validation workshops 9. Reporting The consultant will report directly to the National Director and will work closely with the Finance & Admin Lead throughout the assignment. 10. Confidentiality The consultant shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all organizational information obtained during the assignment and shall not disclose such information without prior written authorization. 11. Payment Schedule Payments may be made based on deliverables as follows: ● 20% upon approval of the Inception Report. ● 40% upon submission and acceptance of the Draft Report. ● 40% upon submission and approval of the Final Report and presentation. Proposal Requirements Interested consultants or consulting firms are invited to submit a comprehensive proposal comprising the following: 1. Technical Proposal The technical proposal should clearly demonstrate the consultant's understanding of the assignment and include: ● A detailed methodology and approach to delivering the assignment. ● A comprehensive work plan, including key activities, deliverables, and timelines. ● The proposed team composition (where applicable), including roles and responsibilities. ● A description of the quality assurance and risk management approach. 2. Financial Proposal A detailed financial proposal that includes: ● A breakdown of professional fees. ● Any reimbursable expenses and associated costs. ● The total cost of the assignment, inclusive of all applicable taxes and fees. ● The proposed payment schedule, linked to key deliverables where appropriate. 3. Company Profile or Curriculum Vitae (CV) ● For consulting firms: A company profile outlining the organization's background, areas of expertise, legal status, and relevant capabilities. ● For individual consultants: An up-to-date Curriculum Vitae highlighting qualifications, professional experience, and relevant technical expertise. 4. Relevant Experience and References Evidence of successful completion of assignments of similar scope and complexity, including: ● A brief description of each assignment. ● Client name and location. ● Duration and value of the assignment (where appropriate). ● Contact details for at least three professional references who may be contacted for verification. 5. Samples of Previous Work Provide at least three examples of comparable assignments successfully completed within the past five (5) years. Each example should include: ● The project title and client. ● The objectives and scope of the assignment. ● The consultant's specific role and responsibilities. ● Key outputs, outcomes, or achievements. ● Completion date. Incomplete proposals or those that fail to provide the required documentation may be deemed non-responsive and may not be considered during the evaluation process. 13. Evaluation Criteria Proposals will be evaluated based on: Criteria Weight Technical Approach and Methodology 35% Relevant Experience 30% Qualifications of Key Personnel 20% Financial Proposal 15% The consultant with the highest combined technical and financial score will be considered for contract award.

The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539. Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable. The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles. Key Responsibilities A. Protection Programme Coordination Lead the day-to-day implementation of protection activities in the assigned woreda. Translate project plans and objectives into practical woreda-level implementation plans. Ensure activities are implemented according to approved plans, budgets, quality standards, and timelines. Coordinate closely with the Project Coordinator on progress, priorities, challenges, and required actions. Provide technical supervision and guidance to the Social Worker. Maintain effective coordination with relevant government offices, community structures, religious leaders, and other stakeholders. Represent the project in relevant woreda-level coordination forums and meetings. Identify protection risks, operational challenges, and emerging needs and recommend appropriate responses. B. Community-Based Protection and Stakeholder Engagement Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming. Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms. Duty Station: One of the following intervention woredas: Mai(t)sebri, Dima, Sheraro, Tahtay-Adyabo, Irob, Gulo-Mekeda, Sanja, Dabat, and Debark

Number of Positions: 9 (one per intervention woreda)

Duration: 12 months

Report To: Project Coordinator

Organization: New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO)

Organizational Profile
1.1 General Information

New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) is an indigenous, non-governmental, non-profit humanitarian organization established in 2007 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The organization was previously registered at the Ministry of Justice under registration number 3018 and later registered and licensed by the Federal Charities and Societies Agency as an Ethiopian resident’s charity by the Charities and Societal Proclamation No. 621/2009 by registration No. 0539. NMWEO has been re-registered according to the Civil Society Organizations Proclamation No.113/2019 with registration No. 0539.

Vision 

We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

Core Values and Belief

·       Humanity

·       Gender sensitive

·       Accountability

·       Equity

·       Teamwork and Excellence

·       Partnership and networking

Job Purpose

The Protection Officer is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of protection activities at woreda level. The Officer will lead the implementation of community-based protection interventions, strengthen community protection committees, facilitate consultations on child and early marriage, support the implementation of community action plans, and oversee the rehabilitation and functioning of the existing Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS), where applicable.

The Protection Officer will work closely with the Social Worker, community structures, religious leaders, local authorities, and relevant service providers to ensure that protection activities are inclusive, community-led, safe, accountable, and consistent with protection, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender, disability inclusion, and Do No Harm principles.

Key Responsibilities

A.   Protection Programme Coordination

  • Lead the day-to-day implementation of protection activities in the assigned woreda.
  • Translate project plans and objectives into practical woreda-level implementation plans.
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved plans, budgets, quality standards, and timelines.
  • Coordinate closely with the Project Coordinator on progress, priorities, challenges, and required actions.
  • Provide technical supervision and guidance to the Social Worker.
  • Maintain effective coordination with relevant government offices, community structures, religious leaders, and other stakeholders.
  • Represent the project in relevant woreda-level coordination forums and meetings.
  • Identify protection risks, operational challenges, and emerging needs and recommend appropriate responses.

B.   Community-Based Protection and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Strengthen community ownership and participation in protection programming.
  • Support the establishment, capacity, functionality, and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms.
  • Facilitate meaningful engagement of community leaders, religious leaders, local authorities, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other relevant groups.
  • Promote community-led identification and prioritization of protection concerns and solutions.
  • Strengthen collaboration between community structures and formal protection and social service systems.
  • Promote locally appropriate prevention and response mechanisms for protection concerns.

C.   Protection Risk Identification and Referral

  • Monitor protection risks and trends within the assigned woreda.
  • Ensure appropriate identification and referral of individuals requiring specialized protection and other essential services.
  • Maintain knowledge of available services and functional referral pathways.
  • Promote safe, confidential, informed, and survivor-/person-centered referral practices.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers and government structures to strengthen access to services.
  • Ensure urgent protection concerns are appropriately escalated through established mechanisms.

D.   Community Engagement and Prevention

  • Lead community engagement approaches aimed at preventing protection risks and harmful practices.
  • Facilitate dialogue and collaboration among communities, leaders, authorities, and service providers.
  • Promote positive social and behavioral change related to protection, safety, dignity, and rights.
  • Support communities to develop and implement locally owned solutions to identified protection concerns.
  • Ensure community engagement approaches are conflict-sensitive, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

E.   Women and Girls Safe Space Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to ensure the existing WGSS is safe, accessible, functional, and responsive to the needs of women and girls.
  • Ensure appropriate linkages between WGSS services and relevant protection, health, psychosocial, legal, and other services.
  • Monitor the quality and accessibility of services provided through the WGSS.
  • Promote confidentiality, dignity, safety, and informed choice for women and girls accessing services.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address operational and protection concerns affecting the WGSS.

F.    Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting

  • Monitor implementation against project objectives, indicators, targets, and quality standards.
  • Ensure accurate and timely collection and documentation of project information.
  • Work closely with MEAL staff on monitoring, data quality, accountability, feedback, and learning.
  • Prepare regular activity and progress reports for the Project Coordinator.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Ensure protection information is managed securely and confidentially.

G.  Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability

  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and humanitarian protection standards.
  • Promote gender equality, disability inclusion, child safeguarding, and meaningful participation of vulnerable groups.
  • Ensure activities do not expose beneficiaries or communities to additional risks.
  • Promote awareness and use of feedback, complaint, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Immediately report safeguarding, PSEA, and serious protection concerns through established organizational procedures.

H.  Financial and Resource Management

  • Support efficient use of project resources at woreda level.
  • Ensure activities are implemented within approved budgets and procedures.
  • Provide timely information on resource requirements and operational gaps.
  • Support proper documentation and accountability for project resources.
