fields.title: (ToR) To Hire a Service Provider (SP) To Provide Technical Assistance (TA) to the Partner Microfinance Institution (MFI) in the Afar Region
fields.description: Terms of Reference (ToR) To Hire a Service Provider (SP) To Provide Technical Assistance (TA) to the Partner Microfinance Institution (MFI) in the Afar Region Institution: FC Africa Development. Project Title: Economic Recovery for Conflict-Affected Population (ER-CAP) Project Implementation Location: Afar Region – Abala Woreda About FC AFRICA DEVELOPMENT FC Africa Development is an economic development organization dedicated to empowering vulnerable communities by designing and implementing sustainable projects across various sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, and services. Our multidisciplinary teams leverage local expertise to drive enterprise growth, improve access to finance, and foster skill development. With a proven track record, we've successfully created jobs, generated wealth, and attracted investments, ultimately leading to the formation and growth of thriving businesses. About the ER-CAP Program The Economic Recovery for Conflict-Affected Population Project (ER-CAP) is a five-year project aiming to improve the economic adaptation, protection, and recovery of populations affected by conflict. The program, led by Mercy Corps in collaboration with the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and FC Africa Development, uses an integrated conflict-sensitive, systems-strengthening, climate-smart, and inclusive approach to enhancing systems that support the economic recovery of communities in three regions: Afar (Abala), Tigray (Mekelle), and Amhara (Woldiya). The program aims to benefit 43,540 individuals, with a specific focus on Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), host communities, and returnee women, youth, and other marginalized groups. The expected outcomes include resilient livelihoods, improved access to financial products and services, and enhanced capacity to mitigate protection risks through access to justice and psychosocial support. As part of this consortium, FC Africa Development primarily focuses on facilitating tailored access to finance to support conflict-affected communities, such as internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities. To ensure effective implementation on the ground, it is crucial to establish and strengthen partnerships with key financial service providers including microfinance institutions (MFIs), savings and credit cooperatives (SACCOs), and banks across all intervention sites. Strengthening the institutional capacity of these financial institutions and providing tailored technical assistance is therefore essential to the program's access-to-finance objectives. Background and Rationale Under the ER-CAP program, FC Africa Development has established a strategic partnership with a Microfinance Institution (MFI) operating in Afar Region to expand access to finance for conflict-affected communities in Abala Woreda. Two years of conflict in Northern Ethiopia significantly disrupted the operations, systems, and institutional capacity of financial service providers operating in the region, including the partner MFI. As ER-CAP moves further into its implementation phase, FC Africa Development, in consultation with the partner MFI, has identified three priority, mutually reinforcing interventions required to restore and strengthen the institutional capacity of the MFI: (i) revision and updating of the MFI's internal manuals and guidelines; (ii) technical support for the implementation of a Core Banking System (CBS); and (iii) loan portfolio management and resource mobilization training for key staff, management, and board members. FC Africa Development seeks to engage a qualified service provider to deliver all three components in an integrated and coordinated manner. This approach is expected to ensure coherence across the interventions, reduce transaction, and enable the service provider to effectively sequence and implement the activities. Objective of the Assignment The overall objective of this assignment is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the partner MFI in Afar Region by updating its internal manuals and guidelines, supporting the effective implementation of its Core Banking System, and building the capacity of its key staff, management, and board members in loan portfolio management and resource mobilization, with an emphasis on Interest-Free Banking principles. Assignment Duration The overall assignment is expected to be completed within four (4) calendar months from the date of contract signing. A detailed, jointly agreed work plan and implementation schedule will be finalized during the inception phase, allowing for reasonable sequencing and, where feasible, parallel implementation of the three components. Scope of Work The service provider will be directly responsible for executing activities split across three highly interconnected components: Components One: Revision and Updating of Internal Manuals and Guidelines The partner MFI's existing operational manuals and guidelines including credit/financing policy, operations, and risk management manuals require review and updating to reflect current National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) directives, post-conflict operational realities, and enhancing of Interest-Free Banking (IFB) product lines. FC Africa Development seeks a consultancy service with practical experience in microfinance policy and procedure development to review the MFI's existing manuals, identify regulatory and operational gaps, and revise/update the manuals, accordingly, including embedding IFB-compliant procedures and controls. Objective The objective of this component is to review and update the partner MFI's internal manuals and guidelines to ensure they are current, regulatory-compliant, operationally sound, and reflective of the institution's Interest-Free Banking product lines. Specific Objectives: · Conduct a comprehensive desk review of the MFI's existing internal manuals and guidelines (credit/financing policy manual, operations manual, risk management manual, and any existing IFB operational guidelines). · Identify regulatory, operational, and IFB-compliance gaps in the existing manuals against NBE directives, cooperative/microfinance proclamations, and relevant good international practice. · Revise and update the identified manuals, incorporating IFB-compliant procedures, internal controls, governance arrangements, and risk management practices. · Facilitate a validation workshop with the MFI's management and board to review, discuss, and endorse the revised manuals. · Incorporate feedback from the validation workshop and finalize the approved manuals and guidelines, submitted in both hard and soft copy. Deliverables: · Inception report outlining the methodology, detailed work plan, and data collection/review tools for this component. · Manuals gap assessment report summarizing findings from the desk review and stakeholder consultations. · Draft revised manuals and guidelines package, including tracked changes/comments where relevant. · Validation workshop report, including participant feedback and agreed revisions. · Final, approved manuals and guidelines package (hard and soft copy). · Support the MFI in organizing board meeting and approval process of the updated internal manuals. Timeframe Thirty (30) Calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase. Component Two: Core Banking System (CBS) Implementation Support The partner MFI is implementing a Core Banking System (CBS) to modernize its operations and enhance service delivery to conflict-affected communities in Afar Region. FC Africa Development seeks a consultancy service with practical CBS implementation experience to support the MFI in configuring the system including for Interest-Free Banking product modules validating data migration and building staff capacity through on-site training at the MFI's operations in Semera and Abala Woreda. Objective The objective of this component is to provide hands-on technical assistance to the partner MFI for the effective implementation of its Core Banking System, ensuring the system is properly configured (including for IFB products), data is accurately migrated, and staff in Semera and Abala Woreda are competent to operate it. Specific Objectives · Assess the current status of CBS implementation at the MFI (data migration progress, and IT infrastructure readiness) and identify implementation gaps and risks. · Support the configuration/parameterization of CBS modules relevant to both conventional and Interest-Free Banking products. · Support data cleansing, migration validation, and reconciliation between legacy records and the new CBS. · Develop a CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP) tailored to the MFI's staff and IFB product lines. · Conduct on-site, hands-on CBS training for relevant staff at the MFI's Semera location and its Abala Woreda branch. · Provide post-training, post-go-live troubleshooting and handholding support to consolidate staff competence and system stability. Deliverables: · Inception report and detailed work plan for the CBS implementation support assignment. · CBS implementation status and readiness assessment report. · CBS configuration and IFB-module support report. · CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP). · On-site training reports for Semera and Abala Woreda, including attendance lists and participant feedback. · Final CBS implementation support report, including recommendations for post-go-live stabilization, and a live Core banking system. Timeframe Two Calander months inclusive of on-site training, mentoring and coaching days in Semera and Abala Woreda. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase. Component Three: Loan Portfolio Management and Resource Mobilization Training (Interest-Free Banking Focused) The service provider will assess current portfolio management practices, develop a tailored training manual, and build the capacity of key staff, management, and board members to manage an expanding IFB financing portfolio soundly. It also evaluates existing resource mobilization methods and delivers specialized IFB-compliant training to help the MFI diversify its funding sources, sustain its growth, and effectively expand its outreach into conflict-affected communities. Objective Enhance the knowledge and practical skills of the partner MFI's key staff, management, and board members in effective loan/financing portfolio management, within an Interest-Free Banking framework. It also aims to strengthen their capacity to develop and implement resource mobilization strategies that are compliant with Interest-Free Banking principles. Specific Objectives · Assess the MFI's current loan/financing portfolio management practices, tools, and capacity gaps, including underwriting, appraisal, monitoring, and non-performing financing (NPF) management. · Assess the MFI's current resource mobilization practices, products, and challenges, including its existing deposit base and funding sources. · Develop a tailored, IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and materials, covering credit risk fundamentals, sound underwriting and appraisal, monitoring and follow-up, and IFB-specific risk classification and provisioning practices. · Develop an IFB-compliant resource mobilization training manual and materials, covering deposit mobilization approaches and outreach/marketing strategies. · Develop a practical resource mobilization action plan/roadmap tailored to the MFI's operating context in Afar Region. · Deliver structured training to key staff, management, and board members of the MFI on loan portfolio management and resource mobilization. · Conduct pre- and post-training assessments to measure knowledge gained and inform follow-up support needs. Deliverables: · Inception report outlining methodology, work plan, and training approach. · Portfolio management capacity gap assessment report. · Resource mobilization assessment report. · IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and PowerPoint materials. · IFB-focused resource mobilization training manual and materials. · Resource mobilization action plan/roadmap for the MFI. · Training delivery report, including attendance, pre/post-assessment results, and participant feedback. Timeframe Thirty (30) calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase. No Deliverable No of Working Days 1 Inception report 3 2 Portfolio management and resource mobilization capacity gap assessment 8 3 Develop IFB-focused training manuals and materials 12 4 Deliver training to staff, management, and board 4 5 Training report and recommendations 3 Total 30 Note: training-related costs (such as training hall, stationery, refreshment, lunch, transport, and DSA) will be covered by FC Africa. Methodology This assignment will employ a mixed-methods approach, combining desk-based reviews of documents with primary data collection, hands-on technical assistance, and structured training delivery. The service provider is expected to develop and agree a detailed work plan and methodology based on this ToR and discussions with FC Africa's ER-CAP Access to Finance team. · Desk review: review of the MFI's operational manuals, financing/credit policy, by-laws, board minutes, audit reports, CBS documentation, and relevant National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) directives. · Key informant interviews: Key informant interviews with the MFI's board members (where appropriate), senior management, middle management, and branch staff in Semera and Abala Woreda. · Focus group discussions: Focus group discussions with relevant staff and, where appropriate, community members/clients to inform the resource mobilization and portfolio management components. · Technical assistance and training delivery: Hands-on technical assistance and coaching for manuals revision and CBS configuration, alongside structured, participatory training delivery for the capacity-building components.

·         Validation workshop report, including participant feedback and agreed revisions.

 

·         Final, approved manuals and guidelines package (hard and soft copy).

 Timeframe

   Thirty (30) Calendar days. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase.

Component Two: Core Banking System (CBS) Implementation Support

The partner MFI is implementing a Core Banking System (CBS) to modernize its operations and enhance service delivery to conflict-affected communities in Afar Region. FC Africa Development seeks a consultancy service with practical CBS implementation experience to support the MFI in configuring the system including for Interest-Free Banking product modules validating data migration and building staff capacity through on-site training at the MFI's operations in Semera and Abala Woreda.

Objective

The objective of this component is to provide hands-on technical assistance to the partner MFI for the effective implementation of its Core Banking System, ensuring the system is properly configured (including for IFB products), data is accurately migrated, and staff in Semera and Abala Woreda are competent to operate it.

   Specific Objectives

·         Assess the current status of CBS implementation at the MFI (data migration progress, and IT infrastructure readiness) and identify implementation gaps and risks.

·         Support the configuration/parameterization of CBS modules relevant to both conventional and Interest-Free Banking products.

·         Support data cleansing, migration validation, and reconciliation between legacy records and the new CBS.

·         Develop a CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP) tailored to the MFI's staff and IFB product lines.

·         Conduct on-site, hands-on CBS training for relevant staff at the MFI's Semera location and its Abala Woreda branch.

·         Provide post-training, post-go-live troubleshooting and handholding support to consolidate staff competence and system stability.

 

 Deliverables:

·         Inception report and detailed work plan for the CBS implementation support assignment.

·         CBS implementation status and readiness assessment report.

·         CBS configuration and IFB-module support report.

·         CBS user manual/standard operating procedure (SOP).

·         On-site training reports for Semera and Abala Woreda, including attendance lists and participant feedback.

·         Final CBS implementation support report, including recommendations for post-go-live stabilization, and a live Core banking system.

Timeframe

Two Calander months inclusive of on-site training, mentoring and coaching days in Semera and Abala Woreda. A detailed timeline will be developed during the inception phase.

Component Three: Loan Portfolio Management and Resource Mobilization Training (Interest-Free Banking Focused)

The service provider will assess current portfolio management practices, develop a tailored training manual, and build the capacity of key staff, management, and board members to manage an expanding IFB financing portfolio soundly. It also evaluates existing resource mobilization methods and delivers specialized IFB-compliant training to help the MFI diversify its funding sources, sustain its growth, and effectively expand its outreach into conflict-affected communities.

Objective

Enhance the knowledge and practical skills of the partner MFI's key staff, management, and board members in effective loan/financing portfolio management, within an Interest-Free Banking framework. It also aims to strengthen their capacity to develop and implement resource mobilization strategies that are compliant with Interest-Free Banking principles.

    Specific Objectives

·         Assess the MFI's current loan/financing portfolio management practices, tools, and capacity gaps, including underwriting, appraisal, monitoring, and non-performing financing (NPF) management.

·         Assess the MFI's current resource mobilization practices, products, and challenges, including its existing deposit base and funding sources.

·      Develop a tailored, IFB-focused loan/financing portfolio management training manual and materials, covering credit risk fundamentals, sound underwriting and appraisal, monitoring and follow-up, and IFB-specific risk classification and provisioning practices.

·         Develop an IFB-compliant resource mobilization training manual and materials, covering deposit mobilization approaches and outreach/marketing strategies.

·         Develop a practical resource mobilization action plan/roadmap tailored to the MFI's operating context in Afar Region.

·         Deliver structured training to key staff, management, and board members of the MFI on loan portfolio management and resource mobilization.

·         Conduct pre- and post-training assessments to measure knowledge gained and inform follow-up support needs.

Deliverables:

This assignment will employ a mixed-methods approach, combining desk-based reviews of documents with primary data collection, hands-on technical assistance, and structured training delivery. The service provider is expected to develop and agree a detailed work plan and methodology based on this ToR and discussions with FC Africa's ER-CAP Access to Finance team.

The bank was established with the largest initial shareholder base in the history of Ethiopia's private banking sector, comprising over 167,000 shareholders. The bank's paid-up capital has reached more than 7.4 billion ETB. As of recent financial reporting, its total capital reserves exceed 10.285 billion Birr.

Amhara Bank operates a network of over 322 branches across Ethiopia, serving a customer base of approximately 2.9 million individuals.


Digital Banking

The bank provides digital financial services, primarily through a proprietary mobile banking application. The digital platform has registered over 1.2 million subscribers.


Interest-Free Banking

Amhara Bank operates a full-fledged interest-free banking (IFB) window under the brand name "Marhaba," which was launched on March 18, 2023. The service offers Sharia-compliant financial products tailored for customers seeking non-interest financial solutions.

Vision We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents. Mission Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs. Core Values and Belief · Humanity · Gender sensitive · Accountability · Equity · Teamwork and Excellence · Partnership and networking Job Purpose The Social Worker will support the implementation of community-based protection interventions at woreda and community level. The position will work directly with individuals, families, communities, and community structures to identify protection and social needs, strengthen community participation, facilitate access to appropriate services, and promote safe and inclusive community environments. The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services. The position will apply social work principles, confidentiality, dignity, informed consent, safeguarding, PSEA, gender equality, disability inclusion, child protection, accountability, and Do No Harm throughout all activities. Contribute to project reports, lessons learned, success stories, and case documentation where appropriate and ethically permissible. Ensure all records are safely stored and protected. H. Safeguarding and Accountability Comply with NMWEO safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, code of conduct, data protection, and other relevant policies. Maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy and dignity of community members. Promote safe reporting of protection and safeguarding concerns. Ensure that activities are implemented according to Do No Harm principles. We envision a country in which women and girls have equal opportunity, claim their rights and free from any violence, and become effective social change agents.

Mission

Our mission is to empower Ethiopian women, girls, and youth in economic, political, and social dimensions, and help them unlock their potential in decision-making through capacity building, advocacy, leadership development, and humanitarian intervention programs.

The Social Worker will contribute to strengthening community protection mechanisms, prevention of harmful practices, community mobilization, referral and follow-up, community action, and the effective functioning of protection-related services.

raw_payload.description:
About Us

Ethio-BioPharma Enterprise (EBPE) is Ethiopia’s state-owned pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise, established to build the nation’s capacity to manufacture vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, medical supplies and other healthcare technologies locally. Operating under EIH, EBPE is developing an integrated pharmaceutical campus at the Kilinto Special Economic Zone in Addis Ababa, co-locating multiple manufacturing units that share infrastructure, talent, and corporate services.

Job Summary

I. GENERAL POSITION DESCRIPTION

Main Purpose of the post

The Operations Manager is responsible for leading the design, installation, and testing of all technical and digital systems. This role ensures that the construction of manufacturing plants for Vaccines, Pharmaceuticals, Diagnostics, and Medical Supplies meets all engineering codes and international regulatory standards (EFDA and WHO-GMP). The manager is accountable for making sure all machinery, utility systems (water, air, power, and specialized gases), Building Management Systems (BMS), and IT networks are properly set up, validated, and ready for full-scale production.

II. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / ACCOUNTABILITY

A. Engineering, Facility Construction and Utility Installation

  1. Lead the review and approval of engineering designs, drawings, P&IDs, equipment layouts, utility layouts, and technical specifications to ensure compliance with project requirements, engineering standards, and WHO-GMP requirements.
  2. Manage the planning, installation, and commissioning of mechanical utility systems including HVAC, Water for Injection (WFI), Purified Water (PW), Pure Steam, Clean Compressed Air, Process Gases, Vacuum, Chilled Water, Plant Steam, and associated piping systems.
  3. Oversee the construction and installation of process utilities, environmental systems, drainage networks, Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), fire protection systems, and other building services while coordinating civil, structural, and electrical interfaces.
  4. Coordinate and supervise contractors, consultants, and equipment suppliers to ensure construction, equipment installation, and utility works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, project schedules, quality standards, and contract requirements.
  5. Review construction materials, fabrication methods, welding procedures, pressure testing, equipment installation, and utility system testing to ensure compliance with applicable engineering and pharmaceutical standards.
  6. Ensure all mechanical, electrical, civil, plumbing, automation, and utility installations comply with Ethiopian regulations, international engineering standards, EFDA requirements, WHO-GMP guidelines, and health, safety, and environmental requirements.

B. Automation, Electrical and Information Systems

  1. Coordinate the installation and integration of electrical distribution systems, Building Management Systems (BMS), Environmental Monitoring Systems (EMS), automation, PLC/SCADA systems, and IT infrastructure.
  2. Oversee the implementation of enterprise IT infrastructure, server rooms, communication networks, ERP integration, and data management systems required to support facility operations.
  3. Ensure cybersecurity, data integrity, backup systems, and computerized infrastructure comply with applicable regulatory and operational requirements.

C. Equipment Testing and Validation

  1. Acceptance Testing: Lead the Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) at supplier locations and Site Acceptance Tests (SAT) once machinery arrives at the plant to verify they work as ordered.
  2. Equipment Qualification: Manage the formal process of Installation Qualification (IQ) and Operational Qualification (OQ) to prove that all machines and utilities are installed and functioning correctly.

  1. Develop engineering SOPs, preventive maintenance strategies, operating manuals, and engineering documentation required for facility operation.
  2. Plan spare parts, maintenance tools, engineering consumables, and utility operation requirements to support reliable plant operation.

The Operations Manager is authorized to:

1. Approve or reject technical designs, equipment specifications, and completed installation work.

2.Stop any construction or installation activity that does not meet the specified technical or quality standards.

3.Direct external contractors on-site regarding technical requirements and timelines.

4.Sign off on technical milestones before payments are released to vendors or contractors.

5.Recommend engineering changes and corrective actions to improve project performance, safety, quality, and operational readiness.

fields.title: Access and Safety Officer
fields.description: Medical Teams Calling Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world. Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates' eligibility thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes. JOB SUMMARY The Access and Safety Officer contributes to the calling of Medical Teams by assisting in the implementation of safety, access, and security policies and procedures to support the organization’s operations. This field-based role involves building and maintaining relationships with local authorities and stakeholders, conducting risk assessments, and ensuring staff are trained in access and security protocols to create a safe working environment. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Create and maintain professional relationships with local authorities, community leaders, and other stakeholders in project locations to ensure community acceptance and collaboration. Create and maintain a network of security contacts and information sources for triangulation purposes. Monitor local government requirements and processes for travel and project implementation, ensuring up-to-date knowledge of regulations. Administrate access, registration, or movement permission requests for field staff, ensuring necessary letters are obtained and renewed on time. Uphold Medical Teams image positively to external stakeholders, highlighting the value and results of its work. Establish and maintain positive working relationships with sector personnel with other local NGOs/UN. Attend relevant inter-agency security coordination meetings to stay informed of regional security dynamics as required by the Field Coordinator. Conduct desktop and on-the-ground risk assessments for new locations, evaluating risks to staff, beneficiaries, and assets. Assess safety and security conditions of potential facilities, reconciling recommendations for necessary improvements. Coordinate with Field program staff on how security concerns impact project plans and work implementation. Ensure that all vehicles, facilities, and equipment comply with Medical Teams' security standards, administrating improvements when necessary. Uphold the Field Operations Safety and Security Policy, creating recommendations on SOPs, protocols, and practices to mitigate risks. Review and update safety and security SOPs regularly, ensuring approval and dissemination across the team. Collaborate on the development and implementation of contingency plans, including for crisis management, evacuation, relocation, and medical evacuation. Lead and train Field staff in security simulations and drills to ensure preparedness for emergency situations. Collect, analyze, and communicate security information from various sources, producing weekly access and security updates. Organize and lead regular security briefings for field staff, visitors and stakeholders. Maintain a clear and organized filing system for all access and security-related documentation. Track and map all security incidents, providing timely analysis to inform security management strategies. Ensure staff are checking in and that movement information is recorded and updated regularly. Brief new staff on safety procedures and security updates, ensuring regular refresher briefings for existing staff. Document and report on security incidents, drafting incident reports promptly for submission to Country Access and Safety Manager and to senior leadership. Assist in identifying training needs for staff, leading safety and security training according to the Medical Teams Safety and Security Training Manual. Provide regular training and scenario drills on personal security, compound security management, defensive driving, and communications procedures. Administrate the line management of the guards, ensuring that they have everything they need to fulfill their role and perform well. Promote the conditions for effective teamwork and commitment to Medical Teams’ values and operating principles. Lead by example regarding Medical Teams’ safety and security procedures. Ensure accountability is integrated into country strategies, program design, monitoring and evaluations, recruitment, staff onboarding, training and performance management, partnership agreements, and highlighted in reporting. Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation & Abuse, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding code of conduct and behavior expectations.

company.name: Marie Stopes International Ethiopia
company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

fields.title: Project Director
fields.description: About Opian Opian is an Ethiopian health-technology and innovation company building decision infrastructure for stronger health systems. We combine deep knowledge of how care and supply chains operate, human-centred product design, data engineering and responsible artificial intelligence. Our work helps health workers, managers and public institutions turn fragmented data into timely decisions—so essential medicines, vaccines and services are available where and when people need them. Our philosophy We believe useful innovation is not novelty for its own sake. It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment. · Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow. · Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients. · Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level. · Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea. · Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team. · Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification. What this means for candidates Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger. · Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries. · Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone. · Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership. Role purpose Provide overall strategic, technical and fiduciary leadership for a national digital supply-chain transformation program focused on improving last-mile visibility and availability of vaccines and RMNCH commodities. The Project Director will be accountable for results, government co-leadership, partner alignment, delivery quality, risk management and the progressive transfer of operational responsibilities to Ethiopian institutions. Key responsibilities · Provide overall leadership and maintain a single, outcome-oriented program strategy across assessment, architecture, product development, pilot implementation, governance, evaluation and transition. · Serve as the principal senior representative to the Ministry of Health, program lead executive offices, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA, regional health bureaus, universities and implementation partners. · Establish decision rights, escalation mechanisms, steering arrangements and performance-management routines that keep government counterparts in substantive leadership roles. · Approve annual and quarterly plans, budgets, staffing, subaward scopes, major technical decisions and corrective actions. · Ensure that product and integration choices align with national digital-health architecture, authoritative registries and existing transactional systems. · Hold workstream leads accountable for measurable improvements in data quality, system use, stock visibility, decision latency and commodity-management performance. · Anticipate political, institutional, technical, financial and operational risks and ensure timely mitigation and transparent communication. · Lead sustainability, institutionalization and handover planning from the first year, including ownership, recurrent costs, hosting, source-code custody and support arrangements. · Ensure compliance with applicable organizational policies, safeguarding, information security, privacy and ethical requirements. Expected results · A government-endorsed program governance and delivery model with clear decision rights and accountability. · Integrated workplans and budgets delivered on schedule with material risks actively managed. · A credible pilot that demonstrates routine use and operational value, not only system deployment. · An agreed scale-up and transition pathway with progressively reduced dependence on external implementation support.

It is the disciplined work of understanding a real problem, challenging assumptions, building and testing a better response, measuring what changes, and strengthening the institutions that must sustain the result. Technology is valuable only when it improves a decision, a workflow or an outcome in the real operating environment.

· Start with reality: design around the health workers, workloads, incentives, infrastructure and constraints that actually exist—not an imported ideal workflow.

· Build with people, not for them: government counterparts and frontline users are co-designers, decision-makers and eventual owners, not passive recipients.

· Strengthen the system, not a standalone application: connect workflows, data, institutions and incentives so information can lead to action across every level.

· Push boundaries responsibly: make ambitious but testable bets, protect safety and privacy, and change direction quickly when evidence contradicts the original idea.

· Make capability local and durable: transfer knowledge, product ownership and operational responsibility so progress continues without permanent dependence on an external project team.

· Be honest about impact: distinguish deployment from adoption and activity from results; make claims specific, measurable and open to verification.

What this means for candidates

Opian is looking for accomplished specialists who are also builders. Candidates should bring exceptional depth in their discipline, intellectual courage, practical judgment and the humility to learn from users and evidence. We value people who can move from ambiguity to a testable approach, from a workshop to an operating routine, and from a promising pilot to an institutionally owned system. The standard is simple: show not only what you know, but what you personally built, changed, tested, learned and left stronger.

· Work across public health, supply chain, policy, product, technology and field implementation boundaries.

· Turn expertise into usable products, processes, decisions and measurable improvements—not reports alone.

· Operate with urgency while preserving quality, public trust, data protection, service continuity and government ownership.


Role purpose

Provide overall strategic, technical and fiduciary leadership for a national digital supply-chain transformation program focused on improving last-mile visibility and availability of vaccines and RMNCH commodities. The Project Director will be accountable for results, government co-leadership, partner alignment, delivery quality, risk management and the progressive transfer of operational responsibilities to Ethiopian institutions.

Key responsibilities

· Provide overall leadership and maintain a single, outcome-oriented program strategy across assessment, architecture, product development, pilot implementation, governance, evaluation and transition.

· Serve as the principal senior representative to the Ministry of Health, program lead executive offices, EPSS, EPHI, EFDA, regional health bureaus, universities and implementation partners.

· Establish decision rights, escalation mechanisms, steering arrangements and performance-management routines that keep government counterparts in substantive leadership roles.

· Approve annual and quarterly plans, budgets, staffing, subaward scopes, major technical decisions and corrective actions.

· Ensure that product and integration choices align with national digital-health architecture, authoritative registries and existing transactional systems.

· Hold workstream leads accountable for measurable improvements in data quality, system use, stock visibility, decision latency and commodity-management performance.

· Anticipate political, institutional, technical, financial and operational risks and ensure timely mitigation and transparent communication.

· Lead sustainability, institutionalization and handover planning from the first year, including ownership, recurrent costs, hosting, source-code custody and support arrangements.

· Ensure compliance with applicable organizational policies, safeguarding, information security, privacy and ethical requirements.

Expected results

· A government-endorsed program governance and delivery model with clear decision rights and accountability.

· Integrated workplans and budgets delivered on schedule with material risks actively managed.

· A credible pilot that demonstrates routine use and operational value, not only system deployment.

· An agreed scale-up and transition pathway with progressively reduced dependence on external implementation support.

fields.title: Purchase Executive- Contract
fields.description: The Purchase Executive – Contracts is responsible for managing all supplier contracts and agreements within the Supply Chain Department. The role ensures that all procurement transactions are governed by valid, compliant, and up-to-date contracts that safeguard the company’s interests. The position involves preparing, reviewing, and maintaining supplier contracts, coordinating with legal and finance departments, and monitoring supplier compliance with contractual terms and performance standards. Contract Preparation and Administration Draft, review, and finalize supplier and service contracts in coordination with the Deputy Manager – SCM and Legal Department. Ensure all contracts reflect accurate commercial terms, scope of work, and delivery obligations. Maintain a centralized contract management system with proper indexing and retrieval. Monitor contract validity periods, renewal dates, and termination clauses. Coordinate with suppliers to ensure timely renewal or closure of expiring contracts. Verify supplier documentation including licenses, tax compliance, and registration certificates. Monitor and enforce compliance with terms on pricing, quality, delivery timelines, and confidentiality. Identify potential contractual risks and escalate issues to management for mitigation. Support vendor evaluation processes by tracking contract compliance and performance metrics. Maintain communication logs and correspondence related to supplier agreements. Documentation and Record Keeping Maintain accurate and complete contract files including correspondence, addendums, and performance records. Ensure all contract-related documents are properly stored and easily accessible for audits. Support Finance and Legal teams with relevant documentation for supplier payments and dispute resolution. Track and update supplier details and contract data in the ERP system. Provide input for management decision-making on supplier retention, renewal, or termination. Support internal and external audits related to procurement contracts. Collaborate with the Legal and Compliance departments to align contract templates with company policy.

company.name: Hope Enterprise’s University College
company.description:
Hope Enterprises or Hope is a local NGO that was established in 1971 in Addis Ababa to help the needy help themselves through basic needs, education, competence, job and business mediation and value education. As Hope was completing its 32 years of humanitarian service in 2003, it’s then Executive Director, Dr. Minas Hiruy, recommended to the Board the establishment of an outstanding liberal arts university college by submitting a full-fledged proposal. After some discussion, the Board and the General Assembly of Hope accepted the proposal, establishing Hope University College as the first public benefits institution of higher learning in the country on November 25, 2003.  Soon after, the Board adopted a new structure comprising the Ladders of Hope that subsumed the existing and non-college activities of Hope as one division and Hope University College as another division, opening the way for the university college to operate autonomously.
 

Values

The University College believes in goodwill to humankind and to nature and in the concretization of this concern as a step to making the world a community of hope, justice, peace and progress. The University College holds dear the advancement of liberal education as a means of personal and social transformation and regards the provision of education to all as an important public responsibility.

Vision

The vision of the University College is to contribute to the renewal and transformation of society through knowledge and value based education and graduates who can make a difference using what they had gained in the university college.

Mission

The University College, having a mission to provide aspiring leaders the option of pursuing world-class education without leaving their country and cultural setting, shall enable the development of leaders, who being capable of independent work, problem solving, analysis, innovation and reflection, can make a difference in the development of society and in mutually and sustainably supportive relations between man and nature.

Mission Statement

Developing leadership for a world of hope

company.name: Ahadu Bank S.C
company.description:
Why work for us?


By joining us, you'll help empower Ethiopians through our pioneering cutting-edge financial services. Join our passionate team, driven by purpose, integrity, and a desire to make a real difference. We offer a dynamic environment, opportunities for growth, and the chance to be part of something revolutionary. Embrace your purpose and build a fulfilling career. This is your chance to shape the future of Ethiopian finance.


Employee Benefits

  • Competitive salary and benefits package
  • Medical Coverage
  • Salary Advance Loan
  • Consumer Loan
  • Mortgage and Vehicle Acquisition Loan.



The Company

Established by visionary entrepreneurs and professionals, Ahadu Bank provides a different model of banking centered on the philosophy of Inclusive Intermediation.

Founded by over 10,000 shareholders and incorporated under the Ethiopian Banking Business Proclamation, Ahadu Bank offers full-fledged commercial banking services. The Bank is domiciled in Ethiopia with its Head Office located on Africa Avenue, Sunshine Building, Addis Ababa.

Ahadu Bank completed the National Bank of Ethiopia's (NBE) initial capital requirement on January 2, 2021, and received its banking license on October 5, 2021. On June 29, 2022, the bank received authorization from the NBE to begin operations and officially opened its doors on July 16, 2022.

According to a June 2024 report, the bank now boasts over 100 branches and a workforce exceeding 900 employees nationwide.


Mission

Pioneer avant-garde financial services for promoting the economic welfare of Ethiopians.


Vision

Take a lead role in the financial sector, in 2025 E.C, in support of the aspirations of the citizenry and the country.


Core values

  1. Fear of God
  2. Passion for Serving
  3. Honesty
  4. Organizational Learning
  5. Proactive Accountability
  6. Humaneness


Our way

We strive to drive the development of Ethiopia's financial services to benefit Ethiopians in a sustainable and inclusive way. We strive to have a positive socio-economic impact in every aspect of our business. We believe that addressing the needs of the unbanked and underbanked by reaching out to rural communities, supporting and nurturing small businesses, practicing responsible banking principles, and investing in innovative technology to digitize our operations helps us create value for our customers, shareholders, and the broader community.


Culture

At Ahadu Bank, our culture thrives on a unique blend of purpose and progress. We're driven by a deep desire to make a positive impact, evident in our core values of social responsibility and financial empowerment for all Ethiopians. We're a passionate team, working together to pioneer cutting-edge financial solutions. Our commitment to innovation goes hand-in-hand with integrity, ensuring we operate with honesty and ethical practices. We believe in fostering a growth mindset, embracing "Organizational Learning" to continuously develop ourselves and each other. This collaborative spirit is core to our success, as we build a supportive and dynamic environment where everyone can thrive. If you're looking to make a real difference and be part of something revolutionary, Ahadu Bank is the place for you.

fields.title: Senior Accountant
fields.description: Job Opening: Senior Accountant – Miawa Water Distribution Location: Ethiopia, Oromia Region, Sheger City, Ashewa Mada Job Type: Full-Time Department: Finance & Accounting Reports To: Finance Manager Company Briefing Miawa Purified Natural Water, a key brand under Miawa Group, is positioned as an affordable, pure, and accessible beverage brand built on quality and strong market visibility. Serving diverse market segments—including retail, HORECA (hotels, restaurants, and cafes), and institutions—our product portfolio spans 0.33L, 0.5L, 1L, and 2L bottle sizes. The distribution arm of Miawa Group operates a robust hybrid distribution model, combining independent sub-agents and a direct delivery van fleet to secure wide market coverage. Miawa Group maintains strict operational standards, relying on systematic financial and sales performance reporting to drive brand consistency and sustainable commercial growth. Job Summary We are seeking an analytical, highly organized, and proactive Senior Accountant to oversee the financial operations of our Miawa Water distribution company. In this role, you will be responsible for general ledger management, route sales reconciliations, inventory accounting across all bottle sizes, expense tracking, and financial reporting. The ideal candidate possesses strong experience in FMCG or beverage distribution, comfortable handling high-volume daily transactions across direct delivery fleets and sub-agent networks while maintaining strict internal controls and tax compliance. Key Responsibilities Financial Reporting & General Ledger: Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements for the distribution business in compliance with local accounting standards and Miawa Group reporting guidelines. Route & Channel Sales Reconciliation: Perform daily and weekly reconciliations of cash, credit, and digital transactions from direct delivery van fleets and sub-agent sales channels. Inventory & Cost Accounting: Oversee inventory accounting for all SKU sizes (0.33L, 0.5L, 1L, and 2L), reconcile physical stock counts against ledger records, track product breakages/losses, and calculate cost of goods sold (COGS). Operational Expense & Budget Tracking: Monitor operational expenses—including fleet maintenance, fuel, driver allowances, and marketing promotional tools—against approved budgets and maintain systematic performance reports. Month-End & Year-End Close: Lead month-end close procedures, revenue recognition, accruals, bank reconciliations, and variance analysis to present clear financial insights to management. Taxation & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure full compliance with all tax regulations (VAT, Withholding Tax, Payroll Tax, and Corporate Income Tax), ensuring timely calculations, filings, and payments. Audit Preparation & Internal Controls: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external auditors, maintaining complete audit trails and enforcing internal financial controls over cash collection and credit terms.

company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.

fields.description: Job Opening: Fleet Supervisor – Miawa Water Distribution Location: Ethiopia, Oromia Region, Sheger City, Ashewa Mada or Furi Job Type: Full-Time Department: Operations & Logistics Reports To: Operations Manager Job Summary We are seeking a highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented Fleet Supervisor to oversee our daily delivery van operations. In this role, you will be responsible for monitoring driver movements, maintaining complete operational and service histories for all delivery vans, enforcing routine preventive maintenance, and managing relationships with external garage service providers. The ideal candidate has strong supervisory skills, basic mechanical knowledge, and hands-on experience managing light commercial vehicle fleets in a fast-paced distribution environment. Driver Movement & Route Supervision: Track and monitor daily driver movements, route compliance, and delivery schedules using GPS tracking systems and daily trip logs. Oversee driver attendance, dispatch, daily vehicle check-outs/check-ins, and adherence to safe driving practices. Address route delays, vehicle breakdowns, or driver issues in real time to minimize disruption to delivery operations. Fleet Records & Van History Maintenance: Maintain comprehensive, up-to-date physical and digital logs for each delivery van (including mileage, fuel consumption, accident records, insurance, and licensing). Document every repair, part replacement, and service event to build an accurate lifespan and cost history for each vehicle. Routine Maintenance & Service Following: Develop and enforce a systematic preventive maintenance schedule for all vans based on mileage, operational hours, and manufacturer guidelines. Conduct routine physical inspections of delivery vans to check oil levels, tire conditions, brakes, lights, and overall cleanliness before vehicles hit the road. Garage & Service Provider Follow-Up: Serve as the primary point of contact for external garages, workshops, and spare parts suppliers. Authorize, track, and follow up on off-site repairs to ensure quick turnaround times and minimize fleet downtime. Inspect completed repair work at third-party garages to verify quality standards before accepting vehicles back into service. Review garage job cards, repair estimates, and invoices for cost accuracy before submitting them to finance for payment. Incident & Safety Management: Investigate vehicle accidents, damage incidents, or mechanical failures; prepare formal incident reports and coordinate insurance claims. Ensure all vehicles remain fully compliant with safety standards, traffic regulations, and government licensing requirements.

fields.title: Senior Project Manager
fields.description: Role purpose: The Senior Project Manager (SPM) is responsible for the overall leadership, management, successful delivery, and achievement of results of the Ethiopia Local Governance Project (ELGP). The position provides strategic, technical, operational, financial, and partnership oversight to ensure that project objectives, outcomes, donor requirements, and Helvetas quality standards are achieved across the Amhara and Sidama regions. The SPM directly supervises the Governance Officer and the two Partnership and Capacity Development Officers, and oversees the performance, compliance, and capacity strengthening of sub-grantees (i.e. local CSO implementing partners). The role serves as the primary focal point for engagement with government signatories, including regional councils, planning bureaus, bureaus of finance, sector offices, and other strategic stakeholders, ensuring strong collaboration, ownership, and institutionalisation of project approaches. The SPM provides leadership in adaptive management, risk management, conflict-sensitive programming, Gender and Social Equity (GSE), localisation, and accountability processes, while promoting the sustainability and scaling of Integrated Community-Based Participatory Planning (ICBPP), social accountability, and participatory local governance systems. The position is ultimately accountable for the effective utilisation of project resources, achievement of project results, organisational learning, and the overall success of ELGP. Key Responsibilities: 1. Provide strategic leadership and ensure effective delivery of ELGP results in Amhara and Sidama regions: Lead the overall planning, implementation, coordination, and adaptive management of ELGP in line with project objectives, donor requirements, annual work plans, budgets, and Helvetas policies. Provide strategic direction to project staff, sub-grantees, and partners to achieve project outcomes related to citizen participation, effective council oversight, and responsive public service delivery. Oversee project progress against targets, milestones, budgets, and contractual obligations, ensuring timely delivery of outputs and outcomes. Lead annual, quarterly, and monthly planning processes and ensure quality implementation across all project locations. Assess operational, programmatic, political, and security risks and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are implemented. Ensure Gender and Social Equity (GSE), conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, accountability, and localisation principles are integrated throughout project implementation. 2. Strengthen partnerships, institutional capacity, and local governance systems for sustainable impact: Provide leadership and oversight for engagement with regional councils, planning bureaus, finance bureaus, WCSA offices, sector bureaus, CSOs, CBOs, and other strategic stakeholders. Supervise and support Governance, Partnership and Capacity Development Officers and other project staff to ensure quality technical assistance and partner support. Oversee the selection, management, performance monitoring, and capacity strengthening of sub-grantees and local partners. Promote institutionalisation of Integrated Community-Based Participatory Planning (ICBPP), grievance redress mechanisms, Financial Transparency and Accountability (FTA), Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB), and other governance approaches within government systems. Facilitate collaboration and learning among government institutions, civil society organisations, community structures, and development partners. Represent Helvetas and ELGP in steering committee meetings, GO-NGO forums, Communities of Practice on Local Governance (CoP-LG), donor meetings, and other strategic platforms. 3. Ensure quality assurance, accountability, learning, and evidence-based decision-making: Lead project performance monitoring, review progress against indicators, and ensure effective use of MEAL data for decision-making and adaptive management. Ensure timely preparation and submission of high-quality technical, financial, donor, and organisational reports. Oversee budget management, financial compliance, resource allocation, and efficient use of project funds. Ensure implementation quality standards, operational procedures, manuals, and technical approaches are consistently applied across project locations and partners. Promote documentation and dissemination of lessons learned, best practices, success stories, and governance innovations from ELGP and its predecessor ALGP+. Support evidence-based advocacy, policy engagement, and scaling of successful governance approaches to strengthen accountable and participatory local governance systems in Ethiopia.

The SPM provides leadership in adaptive management, risk management, conflict-sensitive programming, Gender and Social Equity (GSE), localisation, and accountability processes, while promoting the sustainability and scaling of Integrated Community-Based Participatory Planning (ICBPP), social accountability, and participatory local governance systems. The position is ultimately accountable for the effective utilisation of project resources, achievement of project results, organisational learning, and the overall success of ELGP.

 Key Responsibilities:

1.      Provide strategic leadership and ensure effective delivery of ELGP results in Amhara and Sidama regions:

  • Lead the overall planning, implementation, coordination, and adaptive management of ELGP in line with project objectives, donor requirements, annual work plans, budgets, and Helvetas policies.
  • Provide strategic direction to project staff, sub-grantees, and partners to achieve project outcomes related to citizen participation, effective council oversight, and responsive public service delivery.
  • Oversee project progress against targets, milestones, budgets, and contractual obligations, ensuring timely delivery of outputs and outcomes.
  • Lead annual, quarterly, and monthly planning processes and ensure quality implementation across all project locations.
  • Assess operational, programmatic, political, and security risks and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are implemented.
  • Ensure Gender and Social Equity (GSE), conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, accountability, and localisation principles are integrated throughout project implementation.

 2.      Strengthen partnerships, institutional capacity, and local governance systems for sustainable impact:

  • Provide leadership and oversight for engagement with regional councils, planning bureaus, finance bureaus, WCSA offices, sector bureaus, CSOs, CBOs, and other strategic stakeholders.
  • Supervise and support Governance, Partnership and Capacity Development Officers and other project staff to ensure quality technical assistance and partner support.
  • Oversee the selection, management, performance monitoring, and capacity strengthening of sub-grantees and local partners.
  • Promote institutionalisation of Integrated Community-Based Participatory Planning (ICBPP), grievance redress mechanisms, Financial Transparency and Accountability (FTA), Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB), and other governance approaches within government systems.
  • Facilitate collaboration and learning among government institutions, civil society organisations, community structures, and development partners.
  • Represent Helvetas and ELGP in steering committee meetings, GO-NGO forums, Communities of Practice on Local Governance (CoP-LG), donor meetings, and other strategic platforms.

3.    Ensure quality assurance, accountability, learning, and evidence-based decision-making:

  • Lead project performance monitoring, review progress against indicators, and ensure effective use of MEAL data for decision-making and adaptive management.
  • Ensure timely preparation and submission of high-quality technical, financial, donor, and organisational reports.
  • Oversee budget management, financial compliance, resource allocation, and efficient use of project funds.
  • Ensure implementation quality standards, operational procedures, manuals, and technical approaches are consistently applied across project locations and partners.
  • Promote documentation and dissemination of lessons learned, best practices, success stories, and governance innovations from ELGP and its predecessor ALGP+.
  • Support evidence-based advocacy, policy engagement, and scaling of successful governance approaches to strengthen accountable and participatory local governance systems in Ethiopia.

company.description:
About the company

Marie Stopes International (MSI) is one of the largest international Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) and Family Planning (FP) organizations in the world. We are a results oriented social enterprise that develop efficient, effective and sustainable SRH/FP programmes around the world.

Marie Stopes International Ethiopia (MSIE), a partner of MSI, is currently undertaking a dramatic scale-up of health service delivery for low income women and couples in Ethiopia. This includes expanding services in clinics and rural outreach programs into new regions of Ethiopia and creating social franchising networks of private quality service providers.  MSIE announces information about job vacancies widely and encourages applications from all sectors of the community.  MSIE considers all applicants based on their abilities and will ensure no group is disadvantaged on the basis of disability, gender, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (which includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins), religion or belief, economic or social class, sex, HIV/AIDs status and political affiliation.

MSIE also implements a Safeguarding Policy to safeguard and protect the rights of staff, children, young people and vulnerable sections of the community and to this end, successful candidates will need to sign MSIE’s ‘code of conduct’ and undergo a background check. The Safeguarding Policy includes an adult Safeguarding, dignity at work place, child safeguarding, human trafficking and anti-slavery, sexual harassment, equality and diversity.  MSIE applies zero tolerance approach for the violation such policies. 

MSIE is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to hiring and retaining female employees. The organization has flexible policies including: travel policy for pregnant and lactating women, flexible work hour for non-clinic staff without reducing the total working hour. Women employees have access to on-job mentorship which aim to create gender-sensitive and inclusive work environment. As such, qualified women are encouraged to apply 

 

Our Mission

Ensuring the Individual’s Right to Children by Choice not Chance.

Vision
To become a sustainable nationwide provider of high quality, integrated reproductive health/family planning services.

Our Values

1 Mission driven
With unwavering commitment, we exist to empower women and men to have children by choice not chance.

2 Client centred
We are dedicated to our clients and work tirelessly to deliver high-quality, high-impact services that meet their individual needs.

3 Accountable
We are accountable for our actions and focus on results, ensuring long term sustainability and increasing the impact of the Partnership.

4 Courageous
We recruit and nurture talented, passionate and brave people who have the courage to push boundaries, make tough decisions and challenge others in line with our mission.
 

Why work for us

MSI works in 37 countries around the world to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

For an individual woman or girl, being able to choose when she has children means having the power to take control of her future.
It can mean having the ability to finish her education, pursue a career, look after the children she already has and ensure she remains healthy. MSI was founded in 1976 to provide the contraception and safe abortion services that give women and girls a choice. Since then, choice has been at the heart of everything that we do and our mission remains clear: to help women and girls to have children by choice, not chance.

MSI is a global organisation with 11,000 team members working in 37 countries to deliver our mission. Starting from one single clinic in London, our organisation has grown from one clinic in central London to become one of the world’s largest providers of high quality, affordable contraception and safe abortion services.
Over the last 40 years, we have touched the lives of more than 120 million women and girls, giving them the power to take control of their futures. But we know that there is much more to do, today there are over 230 million women who want to use contraception but can't and that number continues to grow.
